Well-posedness is established under two complementary conditions: (1) sufficiently small initial and boundary data, and (2) non-positive boundary data of arbitrary size. The latter condition utilizes the strong minimum principle for the corresponding linear heat equation to ensure the global invertibility of the nonlinear Cole-Hopf map. The proofs combine linear estimates for the heat IBVP with nonlinear bounds obtained through Taylor series representations and the algebraic properties of Sobolev spaces.
Using artificial delays for prescribed/fixed-time static output feedback control of linear systems

In this paper, we address the prescribed/fixed-time control problem for linear time-invariant systems with relative degree $r\geq 2$ using delayed time-varying static output feedback. In addition to controllability and observability, we assume that a truncated observability matrix is nonsingular. Within the act-and-wait control framework, two types of artificial delays are introduced into the output feedback: one to realize static output feedback and the other to achieve prescribed/fixed-time control. By constructing smooth periodic delayed output feedback controllers, we achieve prescribed-time input-to-state stability (ISS) with respect to matched disturbances and measurement noise. Next, we consider systems with measurement delays. Note that existing predictor methods are not applicable to static output feedback delay compensation. We propose delayed controllers that achieve fixed-time stability in the presence of large known slowly-varying delays (with delay derivatives less than one) and even in the presence of large unknown constant delays for systems with nilpotent matrices. Moreover, we present a design for the case of discrete-time periodic measurements with a small sampling period. When the system reduces to a chain of integrators, prescribed/fixed-time convergence can be achieved with arbitrarily large artificial delays introduced by static output feedback avoiding high gain and managing with large known slowly-varying or sawtooth delays (corresponding to discrete-time measurements) or unknown constant delays. In the case of unknown constant delays, this leads to a low-gain controller that may efficiently attenuate measurement noise. Numerical examples verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.
Global invertibility of polynomial mappings and connectedness of preimages of large spheres
Francisco Braun; Zbigniew Jelonek; Maria Michalska

We prove that a polynomial mapping $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant is a global diffeomorphism provided the preimage of large circles are connected. In higher dimensions this result fails and we present families of counterexamples. Yet, in dimension $3$, we prove that if the preimages of large spheres are connected, then the Jelonek set of the mapping is not homeomorphic to a line and, provided that it has codimension at least $2$, cannot have a single end at infinity.
Fixed Points of the Yang-Mills Gradient Flow in the Vortex Sector

We study the Yang-Mills gradient flow of center vortices in SU(2) gauge theory. For axially symmetric vortices the flow reduces exactly to a linear diffusion equation for the radial profile: a Gaussian core keeps its shape while its width grows as $\sqrt{R^2+4t}$, the flux is exactly conserved, and the thin vortex is the unique bounded fixed point, though not an attractor. Off-diagonal perturbations are governed by a pair of radial Schrödinger operators, and a variational computation shows that, frozen at any instant, the Abelian core has a tachyonic mode for every winding $n\geq 1$. Since the core spreads while the mode grows, we pass to self-similar variables, where the unstable modes are known in closed form, with growth exponents $μ_{n,m}=n-1+m$. Multiply wound vortices are therefore unstable, while the fundamental vortex is exactly marginal and stays Abelian. A scaling argument rules out any static vortex in the transverse plane, and the instability acquires a simple geometric meaning that shortens the path traced in SU(2) by the holonomy of a growing loop, lowering the winding by two. The flow thus drives every vortex toward the Abelian core of winding $n \bmod 2$, with non-Abelian structure appearing only as the transient through which multiply wound cores unwind.
Exploring topological features of a complex network of prime factors and composite numbers
Carlos Daniel Tamayo-Castro; Aldo Ramirez-Arellano; Juan Bory-Reyes

Prime numbers are mathematical concepts of particular interest because of their relative rarity among integers, as well as the relative unpredictability of their occurrence and density along the integer sequence. They constitute the building blocks of all other composite numbers, giving rise to the interesting and important concept of prime factorization, a process guaranteed by the fundamental theorem of arithmetic. Among the several works that have been reported about prime numbers and their interrelationship with composite numbers, some have considered derived graphs and/or networks. In this paper, we derive some topological features of a bipartite complex network of prime factors and composite numbers. More specifically, we prove mathematically that the network's diameter is exactly five regardless of the number of nodes. In particular, we show that certain nontrivial sub-networks have minimal diameter equal to four, which is, again, independent of the number of nodes as long as the network is large enough. The last shows that this network is of small-world type. We also characterize exactly the number of boundary nodes in the network and present a couple of algorithms to identify the most important, relevant, influential, or central nodes of the network. Finally, we focus on the computation of the information dimensions on the basis of Shannon and Tsallis entropies of the studied complex network. The results show both decreasing as the number of nodes increases. Furthermore, both entropies indicate that box coverings at the diameters \(\varepsilon=[3,4]\), group nodes into roughly the same number of boxes, independent of the number of nodes in the network.
On Lewis's homotopy in distance-regular graphs
MollyAnn Burkey; William J. Martin; Freud Oulon

In 2000, Lewis introduced a nested sequence of normal subgroups of the fundamental group of a distance-regular graph $Γ$. While the full homotopy group itself is simply a free group, it is interesting to determine the smallest integer $k$ such that every closed walk in $Γ$ can be built, up to homotopy, from closed walks of "essential length" $k$ or less. Lewis proved that $k\le 6$ for any $Q$-polynomial distance-regular graph $Γ$ that is not a pseudoquotient. In this paper, we prove that $k=3$ for Johnson graphs and that $k=4$ in the case of Hamming graphs. We also compute the homotopy groups of natural cell complexes associated to the folded Johnson graphs and folded cubes. The paper finishes with some open questions and suggestions for further lines of investigation.
Recent results on diffeomorphisms of $4$-manifolds make essential use of families of embeddings of $1$-manifolds into $4$-manifolds. We survey what is currently known about such families.

We study the efficiency--complexity tradeoff for resource-limited agents through directed first-passage percolation. Nonnegative i.i.d. edge weights represent physical energy expenditure, while the logarithmic size of a constrained path family measures representational complexity. For translation-invariant families, a path-joining property yields deterministic large-distance costs in rational directions and joint convexity in constraint parameter and direction, under suitable moment and feasibility assumptions. Our main result concerns the limiting cost parameterized by path-family entropy. Using techniques from analytic combinatorics in several variables (ACSV), we establish its almost-sure existence and joint continuity in entropy and direction for nested families satisfying additional generating-function conditions, on the corresponding entropy range. Path-count asymptotics supply the change of parameter linking this cost to the constraint-parameterized cost. Two planar examples constrain the number of turns or the number of East-runs of length at least two.
A simple improvement on Kerman's approximation to the median of the beta distribution

Kerman's approximation to the median of the Beta$(α,β)$ distribution is the ratio $g(α)/(g(α) + g(β))$ with $g(x) = x - 1/3$, using the first two terms of the asymptotic expansion of the median of the standard gamma distribution. We extend this elegant ratio form to the one-parameter family with $g(x) = x - 1/3 + c_1/x$, in which $c_1 = 0$ gives Kerman's. For large shape parameters along any ray $β= rα$ with $r > 1$, the resulting approximation is eventually a lower bound on the median if $c_1 \le 8/405$ and an upper bound if $c_1 \ge 1/45$. We recommend $c_1 = 1/36$ for its simplicity: it makes $g(x) = (x - 1/6)^2/x$ a perfect square over $x$, and it is within 1% of the minimax value of $c_1$ for $α, β\ge 1$ under several error measures, while the theoretically distinguished values $8/405$ and $1/45$ are less accurate. The approximation is then $((α- 1/6)^2/α)/((α- 1/6)^2/α+ (β- 1/6)^2/β)$. Its relative error lies between -0.171% and +0.212% for all $1 \le α\le β$, compared with up to -3.8% for Kerman's. It is more accurate than Kerman's approximation wherever the latter is defined, with relative error never more than 13/32 of Kerman's, the ratio approached asymptotically. The same $g(α)$ is a useful approximation to the gamma distribution median, overestimating it by at most 0.212% for shape parameter $α\ge 1$.
Delio Jaramillo-Velez; Hiram H. López; Rodrigo San-José; Nart Shalqini

We give a combinatorial characterization of the $\rm{v}$-number of a $t$-closed neighborhood ideal associated to a graph $G$, and investigate its relation with other invariants such as the $t$-domination number and the smallest size of a ball of radius $t$ in the graph $G$. We present several new cases where it is satisfied that the $\rm{v}$-number is bounded above by the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity. We analyze the behavior of the $\rm{v}$-number of a $t$-closed neighborhood ideal with respect to the parameter $t$. Lastly, we compute explicit formulas for the $\rm{v}$-number in the case of paths, cycles, and caterpillars, and analyze the case of Hamming graphs.

In this paper, we introduce the notion of an omni-representation of a Leibniz conformal algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ on a $\mathbb{C}[\partial]$-module $M$ as a Leibniz conformal algebra homomorphism from $\mathfrak{g}$ to the conformal omni-Lie algebra $\mathfrak{gc}(M)\oplus M$. We show that the right $λ$-action of a representation induces a Maurer--Cartan element. When $M$ is a free $\mathbb{C}[\partial]$-module of finite rank, it also defines, via the conformal dual $M_c^*$, a $1$-cocycle with values in $M_c^*\otimes M\cong\mathfrak{gc}(M)$. Consequently, every such representation gives rise to an omni-representation on $M_c^*\otimes M$. We characterize omni-representations with values in the graph of a conformal embedding tensor. Finally, we introduce the omni-cohomology theory of Leibniz conformal algebras and establish the relation between omni-cohomology groups and the usual cohomology groups.
Between the Semi-Random Process and G(n,p)

We study a random graph process that connects the Erdős--Rényi random graph with the semi-random process. In each round, a uniformly random vertex is revealed together with a uniformly random candidate set of $s$ possible partners, and Builder chooses one of them. We study how this limited adaptivity $s$ changes the hitting times of monotone graph properties and how the familiar logarithmic ``coupon--collector'' delays in random graphs are reflected in this setting.
Solving Large SDPs from Flag Algebra Problems

The flag algebra method is a general tool in extremal combinatorics, which has been useful in tackling open problems concerning graphs, hypergraphs, permutations, point sets, and other structures. The method establishes combinatorial inequalities via sums of squares, which are usually obtained by a semidefinite relaxation of the original combinatorial problem. A typical application of the method in graph theory starts with fixing a parameter $n$ followed by constructing a semidefinite program based on the (subgraph) structure of all $n$-vertex graphs. In the standard formulation before symmetry reductions, there is a coefficient constraint for every admissible $n$-vertex graph up to isomorphism. For 3-uniform hypergraphs, there are 2,136 of them on 6 vertices and 7,013,320 on 7 vertices. While solving the resulting program for $n=6$ is an easy task on any modern computer, the programs for $n = 7$ seems out of reach, mainly because the SDP solvers need too much RAM. Yet solving such programs for as large $n$ as possible is desirable because they typically yield better bounds for the original combinatorial problems. We bypass the aforementioned memory requirements by linear programming with cutting planes. Although we do not guarantee that this cutting-plane procedure reaches an optimum in finitely many iterations, in many flag algebra instances it uses much less memory and yields improved bounds for well-known hypergraph Turán problems. We use this method to obtain numerical bounds for Turán densities and codegree squared densities of several 3-uniform hypergraphs including the tetrahedron, where we obtained the upper bound 0.55753 and tetrahedron without one edge with a new upper bound 0.2865. It also allows to tackle bounds on Turán densities of 7-vertex 3-graphs using flag algebras, which was not possible before.
Helstrom geometry with time-dependent spectral calibration

In a recent work we introduced a finite scalar-qubit-scalar spectral triple whose Connes distance reproduces the Bloch-ball trace metric up to a factor $2/Λ$, where $Λ^2=μ_L^2+μ_R^2$ for isotropic link strengths $μ_L,μ_R$ appearing in the proposed Dirac operator. Here we analyse time-dependent variation of these links, independent of the qubit dynamics. In doing so, we separate the distinguishability and calibration contributions to the spectral rate. A depolarizing example demonstrates spectral growth despite a monotonic contraction of the trace-distance. More generally, we characterize the admissible trace-distance histories compatible with a given positive spectral record and exhibit contracting and reviving realizations. At fixed $Λ$, we also study a sinusoidal link imbalance that preserves the Dirac spectrum and qubit metric, while the scalar-scalar distance oscillates with half the period of the imbalance.
Joint Extension Field Point Counts for Superelliptic Curves

Fix a finite field $\mathbf{F}_q$, an integer $m\ge2$ prime to $q$, and $2\leκ\le m$. For a uniformly chosen $κ$-power-free polynomial $F\in\mathbf{F}_q[x]$ of degree $D$, we determine the limiting joint distribution of the affine point counts of $y^m=F(x)$ over $\mathbf{F}_q,\ldots,\mathbf{F}_{q^n}$ as $D\to\infty$, with $q$ and $n$ fixed. The probability generating function is a finite Euler product with explicit local factors. Equivalently, the limiting vector is a sum of independent closed-point contributions, each of which may affect several extension degrees. We obtain the formula by specializing the equidistribution and motivic Euler product formalism of Bertucci-Howe. We then compute means, covariances, and moment expansions as $q$ varies in a fixed reduced residue class modulo $m$, after the degree limit has been taken. The one-field specialization recovers the power-free affine point-count distribution of Cheong-Wood-Zaman.
V-Representability Beyond Singular Times in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory: The Hubbard Dimer Case

We study the global $V$-representability problem in time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) for the two-particle Hubbard dimer model in the spin-singlet sector. In particular, we investigate whether the time-dependent density of the interacting system obtained for a given one-body external potential $u$ (the tunable control variable) can be reproduced by a non-interacting Kohn--Sham system beyond the singular times at which the usual inversion formulas break down. We deal with both the conventional formulation of TDDFT based on some time-dependent variational principle and the recently introduced geometric formulation of TDDFT (Phys. Rev. Lett. 136 (2026) 256401, Phys. Rev. A 113 (2026) 062222). For both principles, we prove global-in-time $V$-representability, show that singular times induce non-uniqueness of the time-dependent effective potential, and classify the set of solutions.
A Cubic Underestimator for Deterministic Global Optimization

We propose a new underestimator with pointwise and Hausdorff convergence of order three for deterministic global optimization of twice continuously differentiable functions with Lipschitz continuous Hessians. The proposed underestimator is obtained by augmenting the second-order Taylor expansion with a cubic remainder term of the objective function yielding a valid global underestimator that can be used to obtain lower bounds in a branch-and-bound method to solve nonconvex global optimization problems. The underestimator is nonconvex, and finding its global minimum could be computationally expensive. Accordingly, we derive a sufficient condition under which the proposed cubic underestimator is edge-concave, so that its minimum over a box can be found by vertex evaluation, while retaining third-order convergence. We show that the maximum separation distance between the objective function and the underestimator decreases cubically with the width of the box. This higher order convergence enables the lower bounds to converge more rapidly to the optimal value as the variable bounds are progressively tightened. The proposed underestimator is incorporated into a deterministic branch-and-bound algorithm and compared with the αBB and second-order edge-concave underestimators on a collection of 130 benchmark problems. The numerical results show that the proposed underestimator outperforms the compared underestimators in terms of both the number of explored branch-and-bound nodes and total CPU time, while maintaining a competitive computational cost per node. These results demonstrate that the proposed cubic edge-concave underestimator can provide more effective lower bounds and better computational performance in deterministic global optimization.
On tame amenable flows and generalized Newelski's conjecture

We are developing some topological dynamics below a given ambit. We define and study Bohr compactifications below ambits and other related objects. We describe a natural epimorphism from the Ellis group of an ambit to the Bohr compactification below its Ellis semigroup ambit. The first main result says that, assuming tameness and hereditary amenability, this natural map is an isomorphism of topological groups. This is an abstract dynamical generalization of Newelski's conjecture, or rather a theorem of Chernikov and Simon that a natural map from the Ellis group of the flow $(S_G(M),G)$ to the definable Bohr compactification of $G$ is an isomorphism when $G$ is a definably amenable group definable in a NIP structure $M$. We give two proofs of our main result: a shorter dynamical proof and an analytic proof. In the course of the dynamical proof, we prove some results on the universal compactification flow and on the generalized Bohr compactification below a given ambit which admits a left continuous semigroup operation extending the action of $G$. The considerations around the analytic proof yield a description of the measured structure of amenable tame minimal flows, which is the second main result of this paper. We also study specializations of the above abstract topological dynamics context to model theory contexts to recover some known and to obtain some new notions and results. The main new results in the model theory contexts are: (i) a description of the Bohr compactification of the group of automorphisms of a sufficiently saturated model $\mathfrak{C}$ of a first order theory $T$ below a certain fundamental ambit associated with $\mathfrak{C}$; (ii) transfer of amenability of a NIP theory $T$ to amenability of the Ellis semigroup ambit; (iii) a version of Newelski's conjecture for spaces of local types with a description of Bohr compactifications below such spaces.
Stationary Random Iterations of Lipschitz Maps: A Generalized Displacement Condition for the Existence of Invariant Structures
Bella Figliaggi; Edgar Matias; Tiago Pereira

We study random iterations generated by infinitely many Lipschitz maps on non-compact complete separable metric spaces. We generalize classical displacement conditions ensuring the existence and uniqueness of invariant structures. We prove two main results. The first uses the graph transform operator to extend Elton's condition [A multiplicative ergodic theorem for Lipschitz maps. Stochastic Process. Appl. 34(1) (1990)] for the existence and uniqueness of invariant graphs. The second uses the Markov operator to generalize a displacement condition for stationary measures, introduced by Diaconis and Freedman [Iterated random functions. SIAM Rev. 41(1) (1999)] and by Kloeckner [Optimal transportation and stationary measures for iterated function systems. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 173(1) (2022)]. We present several examples illustrating the applicability of our results.
Optimal Control of the 2D Boussinesq Equations with Finite Codimension Constraints
Utpal Manna; Manil T. Mohan; Sangram Satpathi

We study an optimal control problem (OCP) governed by the two-dimensional (2D) Boussinesq equations, where the right-hand sides of the velocity and temperature equations are projected onto the corresponding tangent spaces of the manifolds $\mathcal{M}_1:=\{y\in\mathbb{H}:\|y\|_{\mathbb{H}}=1\}$ and $\mathcal{M}_2:=\{θ\in H:\|θ\|_H=1\}$, respectively. The resulting evolution is subject to finite-codimensional constraints, under which the state $(y,θ)$ remains on $\mathcal{M}:=\mathcal{M}_1\times\mathcal{M}_2$ throughout the time interval. A Faedo--Galerkin construction provides a unique, global, strong solution to the constrained Boussinesq system for external controls $\mathfrak{H}\in L^2(0,T;\mathbb{H})$, along with uniform energy bounds. In addition, we establish the existence of an optimal triplet $(y^*,θ^*,\mathfrak{H}^*)$ that minimizes the quadratic cost subject to the constrained Boussinesq system. Necessary conditions of the first order are obtained through a coupled state--adjoint--control system. The optimal state $(y^*,θ^*)$ remains on $\mathcal{M}$, while the optimal control lies in the tangent space: $\mathfrak{H}^*(t)\in T_{y^*(t)}\mathcal{M}_1$, for all $t\in[0,T]$. We also show that the map $\mathfrak{H}\mapsto(y_{\mathfrak{H}},θ_{\mathfrak{H}})$ in $(C([0,T];\mathbb{H})\cap L^2(0,T;\mathbb{V}))\times(C([0,T];H)\cap L^2(0,T;V))$ is Fréchet differentiable. The linearized state is the unique weak solution to the constrained linearized Boussinesq system and satisfies the necessary tangency condition. Hence, the well-posedness and first-order optimality conditions are established for the Boussinesq system under nonlinear manifold constraints.
Critical metrics for the Dirac-Yamabe eigenvalue ratio and Einstein-Dirac equations

Let $(M^n,g)$ be a closed spin manifold of dimension $n\geq 3$ with positive Yamabe constant. We prove that critical metrics for the mixed eigenvalue ratio $\mathcal H(g)=\frac{λ_1(D_g)^2}{λ_1(L_g)},$ where $D_g$ is the Dirac operator and $L_g$ is the conformal Laplacian are characterized by a harmonic section whose energy-momentum tensor satisfies an Einstein--Dirac equation. We discuss consequences of this result for Hijazi's inequality, and we construct an example to prove that $\mathcal H$ is unbounded above within the conformal class of the round sphere.
Explicit equations of three pairs of fake projective planes

We find explicit polynomial equations in their bicanonical embeddings into $\mathbb C\mathbb P^9$ for the pairs of fake projective planes labeled by $(C18,p=3,\{2\},D_3), (C18,p=3,\{2\},(dD)_3)$ and $(C18,p=3,\{2\},(d^2D)_3)$ in the Cartwright-Steger classification. We do this by starting with the equations of the commensurable fake projective plane labeled by $(C18,p=3,\{2I\})$ that were found in arXiv:2512.03213.

We construct a family of bounded, finitely additive, covariant positive operator-valued measures (POVMs) on the real line by applying generalised Banach-Cesaro asymptotic averaging to locally finite covariant POVMs. In contrast to the strictly shift-invariant case, where countably additive operator measures are restricted to scalar multiples of a single fixed operator, the introduced covariant setting allows for non-commuting averaged operator values while successfully normalising the total mass. We develop an integration theory for complex-valued functions by taking the completion of simple integrable functions with respect to the continuous operator norm induced by the positive integral of their absolute values. The integration spaces for the original and the averaged measures are shown to possess distinct null classes. Finally, we introduce the operator-valued Fourier transform on these integration spaces and analyze the core algebraic constraints imposed by the covariance property on the exponential multipliers.
Price's law for scalar waves on 1+4 dimensional subextremal Myers-Perry spacetimes

We consider Myers--Perry spacetimes $(M,g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}})$ in $1+4$ dimensions with two spin parameters $(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b})\in\mathbb{R}^2$, which are a direct generalization of the well known Kerr spacetime in $1+3$ dimensions. We prove that the Hamiltonian flow associated to $g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}}^{-1}$ is normally hyperbolically trapped for the full subextremal range \[ (|\mathbf{a}|+|\mathbf{b}|)^2<2\mathfrak{m}. \] As an application, we prove a Price law with explicit leading order terms for solutions $ϕ(t,x)$ of the scalar wave equation \[ \Box_{g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}}}ϕ=0 \] under the assumption of real mode stability. Our precise asymptotics imply that $ϕ(t,x)=ct^{-3}+\mathcal{O}(t^{-4+})$, where $c\in\mathbb{C}$ is an explicitly computable constant.
Packing colourings of claw-free subcubic graphs

We prove that every claw-free subcubic graph admits a \packA-packing colouring, confirming a conjecture of Mortada, El Zein and Al Hajjar. The proof combines a reduction to line graphs of subdivided loopless cubic multigraphs with local colouring extensions. We also give a negative answer to their question on \packB-packing colourings by constructing an infinite family of connected bridgeless claw-free cubic counterexamples. The smallest graph in this family has 36 vertices. More generally, we characterise the simple cubic graphs whose triangle expansions admit a \packB-packing colouring in terms of gated independent odd-cycle transversals. This characterisation gives a classification for connected bridgeless claw-free cubic bases and shows that the double triangle expansion of a loopless cubic multigraph admits such a colouring if and only if the multigraph has a perfect matching.
Variational Structure of Energy-Balance Climate Models with Heterogeneous Insolation

We analyse stationary Sellers-type energy-balance climate models with heterogeneous insolation $Q_\varepsilon = Q_*+\varepsilon Q_1$, both on the interval $(-1,1)$ with degenerate diffusion $κ(x)=1-x^2$ and on $\mathbb{S}^2$ with uniformly elliptic diffusion. Assuming that the homogeneous model corresponding to $\varepsilon = 0$ admits three constant equilibria $θ_S <θ_M < θ_W$ satisfying suitable non-degeneracy and spectral conditions, we prove that, for sufficiently small $\vert \varepsilon \vert $, these equilibria continue to three stationary branches $ u_S^\varepsilon$, $u_M^\varepsilon$, and $u_W^\varepsilon$. The cold and warm branches, $u_S^\varepsilon$ and $u_W^\varepsilon$ respectively, are strict local minimisers of the associated energy functional, while the intermediate branch $u_M^\varepsilon$ is non-degenerate and has Morse index one. We further establish the Palais-Smale condition and obtain a mountain-pass critical point $u^\varepsilon_{MP}$ at the minimax level between the two local minima. Under an additional isolation assumption for the homogeneous problem at the minimax level, this critical point coincides with $u_M^\varepsilon$. Lastly, a Legendre-Galerkin discretisation of the one-dimensional model numerically illustrates the three stationary branches, their discrete Morse indices, and the corresponding energy landscape.
An Elliptic Path Fibration and Holomorphic Morita Equivalence

We construct an elliptic analogue of the Alekseev-Meinrenken path fibration \cite{alekseev2009atiyah} for a simply connected complex Lie group with a nondegenerate invariant symmetric bilinear form. A natural $2$-form on the correspondence space induces a holomorphic symplectic groupoid over the space of $(0,1)$-connections and a holomorphic quasi-symplectic groupoid over the holomorphic loop group. The correspondence space defines a principal holomorphic Morita bibundle with compatible differential forms.
The endpoints $p_-=1$ and $p_+=\infty$ for the maximal operator on $L^{p(\cdot)}$ over spaces of homogeneous type

We investigate the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M$ on variable Lebesgue spaces $L^{p(\cdot)}(Ω,d,μ)$ over spaces of homogeneous type, focusing on the endpoints $p_-=1$ and $p_+=\infty$. At the lower endpoint, we prove that the boundedness of $M$ forces $p_->1$ for all exponents if and only if the space $(Ω,d,μ)$ is non-atomic. At the upper endpoint, we generalize the Muckenhoupt-Nekvinda sufficient condition of Adamadze, Diening, and Kopaliani. On bounded spaces of homogeneous type, whenever $p_->1$, this yields a boundedness criterion based on the Muckenhoupt condition alone. We also construct an unbounded space where the Muckenhoupt condition suffices for the maximal operator's boundedness.
Inequalities and asymptotics for hook numbers in two partition functions of MacMahon and Andrews
Rupam Barman; Archit Deb; Sayantan Ghorai

Motivated by recent studies of hook length biases in restricted partitions, we investigate the total number of hooks of fixed length in two partition functions introduced by MacMahon and Andrews. In $1916$, MacMahon proved that the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part appears with multiplicity one equals the number of partitions of $n$ into parts that are even or congruent to $3 \pmod{6}$. For a positive integer $r$, let $A_r(n)$ count the partitions of $n$ in which every part occurring an odd number of times occurs at least $2r+1$ times, and let $B_r(n)$ count the partitions into parts that are even or congruent to $2r+1 \pmod{4r+2}$. Andrews proved that $A_r(n)=B_r(n)$ for all positive integers $r$ and nonnegative integers $n$, thereby recovering MacMahon's identity as the special case $r=1$. We derive generating functions and asymptotic formulas for the total numbers of hooks of lengths $1$, $2$, and $3$ in both partition classes, employing Wright's circle method. These asymptotic formulas yield several hook length bias results. In particular, for sufficiently large $n$, the $B_r$-type partitions exhibit more $1$-hooks than the $A_r$-type partitions, whereas for hook lengths $2$ and $3$, the bias is reversed when $r=1$ and favors the $B_r$-type partitions when $r\geq 2$. We also establish asymptotic inequalities among hook numbers of different lengths within each partition class. Finally, for fixed hook lengths $\ell\in\{1,2,3\}$, we prove that the $B_r$-type partitions exhibit more $\ell$-hooks than the $B_{r+1}$-type partitions for sufficiently large $n$. These results reveal systematic asymptotic patterns in the distribution of small hook lengths across the two partition families.
Jensen gaps and the decomposition principle

We provide axiomatic characterizations of Jensen-gap functionals, which have the form $ρ(X)=\mathbb{E}[f(X)]-f(\mathbb{E}[X])$ for some real-valued function $f$ called the generator. This class includes important examples such as the excess growth rate, the utility premium, the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, and the variance, and is also closely related to measures of variability. We analyze various forms of convexity for Jensen gaps. To characterize Jensen gaps, we formulate conditional versions of law-invariant functionals, which are needed to state the decomposition principle. On an atomless probability space, we show that law invariance together with a binary decomposition principle is sufficient to characterize Jensen gaps on simple random variables. Under suitable continuity conditions, the characterization extends to broader classes, including compactly supported random variables and integrable random variables. We then identify the generator $f$ by imposing either of two natural invariance conditions: scaling invariance or translation invariance. The former identifies logarithmic, $x\log x$, and power generators, whereas the latter identifies exponential and quadratic generators.
Greedy Orthogonal Polynomial Manifolds with Lipschitz Control for Dimensionality Reduction and Reduced Modeling
Tomoki Koike; Benjamin Peherstorfer; Elizabeth Qian

Polynomial manifolds provide nonlinear low-dimensional representations through polynomial decoders. We propose to represent the polynomial terms of the decoder using features that are orthonormal on the training data. This empirical orthogonality enables a greedy algorithm, Greedy-OPM, which jointly selects encoder modes and polynomial features while minimizing the reconstruction error under a prescribed bound on the decoder's Lipschitz constant. Numerical experiments show that this Lipschitz constraint improves generalization away from the training data while retaining high reconstruction accuracy.
The Exact Dihedral Angle Sum Range for Circumcentral-Cevian Jaw Tetrahedra

Hajja, Hammoudeh, Hayajneh and Martini showed that a tetrahedron whose cevians to the circumcenters of the opposite faces are concurrent is either a kite or a special jaw. We determine the exact dihedral-angle-sum range on the jaw component. The lower endpoint is attained only by the regular tetrahedron, while the upper endpoint is approached only in the degenerate limit. The proof reduces the family to one scale-invariant parameter and an explicit monotonicity argument.
Magnetic billiards:duality and magnetic Radon property

We study Birkhoff magnetic billiards inside convex planar domains for a constant weak magnetic field. We prove that there exists a functional family of centrally-symmetric convex billiard tables satisfying the so-called magnetic Radon property. These are tables which have a rotational invariant curves consisting of $4$-periodic orbits with the rotation numbers either $1/4$ or $3/4$. These billiard tables can be constructed in a neighborhood of circles. However in our construction we do not use perturbation methods but rather some topological argument for the system of ODEs governing the magnetic Radon property. In contrast with this result we consider the magnetic billiard tables having discrete rotational symmetry for the angle $2π/k, k\in\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that in this case a rotational invariant curve consisting of $k$-periodic orbits exists, if and only if the billiard table is circular. We develop several tools, which, we believe, are important for other aspects of magnetic billiards. The first is the "magnetic duality" which enables to work with the dual object---the outer magnetic billiard. Secondly, we find the generating functions of outer magnetic billiard, both the ''standard" and the "non-standard" ones.
A Borsuk-Ulam theorem for adaptive continuous measurements

We prove a Borsuk-Ulam theorem for adaptive measurements: if $2^n\le m$, then any $n$ adaptively chosen continuous functionals take identical values at two antipodal points of any sphere in $\mathbb{R}^m$. Consequently, at least $\lceil\log_2(m+1)\rceil$ adaptive continuous measurements are needed to learn the vectors of a ball in $\mathbb{R}^m$ with an error smaller than its radius, which matches the recently obtained upper bound up to one measurement. The bound extends to Bernstein widths in Banach spaces. The main idea of the proof was found by Claude Fable 5, an AI model developed by Anthropic, and we document the development in a last section.
On the stability of second-order methods for DDEs and PDDEs

In this paper, a one-parameter family of second-order implicit--explicit (IMEX) multistep methods is studied for delay differential equations (DDEs). The analysis is based on the matrix problem $y'(t)=A y(t) + B y(t-τ(t))$, where $A$ is Hermitian negative definite but $B$ is any matrix. For constant, grid-aligned delays, a field-of-values argument yields unconditional stability whenever a suitable generalized field of values $F_p(A,B)$ is contained in the open unit disk. For a constant non-grid-aligned delay, we show that quadratic interpolation does not reduce the corresponding stability disk. For genuinely variable delays, the method is formulated as a nonautonomous augmented system, and product-level sufficient conditions are obtained from a common quadratic Lyapunov inequality and from a quantitative slow-variation hypothesis. The approach developed herein is illustrated through several examples in which the discussed theory is applied not only to DDEs, but also to semidiscrete parabolic problems given by partial delay differential equations with a diffusion term.
The Geometry of Limits in ReLU Function Spaces

We study the geometry and closure of spaces of functions realized by ReLU neural networks of fixed architecture. We first establish a general result about limits of continuous piecewise-linear (CPWL) functions: the minimum number of convex sets on which a function is affine is lower semicontinuous under pointwise convergence. The proof uses a connection to hypergraph coloring and a compactness principle, and yields quantitative bounds on the polyhedral complexity of continuous limits. We then characterize the functions realizable by shallow ReLU networks with vector-valued outputs, extending a known scalar-valued characterization. Using this and the geometry of limiting hyperplane arrangements, we prove that fixed-width shallow scalar ReLU realization spaces are closed in the weighted supremum norm on the whole input space. In contrast, we construct an explicit sequence of networks with architecture $(2,3,2\mid1)$ whose limit is not realizable by that architecture. Non-closedness holds both globally in weighted supremum norm and under uniform convergence on compact sets with nonempty interior, disproving a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan, and Voigtlaender. Finally, we show that non-closedness for a fixed scalar-output ReLU architecture necessarily involves a \emph{blow-up residue}, in which diverging output coefficients amplify an emerging linear dependence among hidden features. Together, these results provide geometric and functional-analytic tools for studying the boundaries and degenerations of ReLU realization spaces.
Induced Bell-CHSH observables in the Fewster-Verch measurement scheme
M. S. Guimaraes; I. Roditi; S. P. Sorella

The Summers-Werner theorem shows that the vacuum of a relativistic quantum field theory violates the Bell-CHSH inequality maximally on complementary wedges, but it is an existence statement: it exhibits neither the observables nor an apparatus that measures them. We give an explicit operator-level realization within the Fewster-Verch measurement framework, obtaining dichotomic Bell observables of a free Majorana field in $1+1$ dimensions as observables induced by local couplings to Majorana probes. The induced system smearing factorizes exactly as $f_h=k\,b_{λ,h}$, so its support is controlled by the compactly supported coupling profile $k$; dichotomy is imposed by calibrating and normalizing the induced smearings rather than required of the probe observable; and a probe-only normal ordering yields the product of Alice's and Bob's induced bilinears, which the non-multiplicative induced map alone does not provide. Under explicit attainability hypotheses the induced observables saturate the Tsirelson bound in a state prepared from the vacuum. The construction extends to coupled scalar fields.
Combinatorial models for Quasicrystals and Schur-Weyl Duality
Glenn Appleby; Mary Claire Simone; Tamsen Whitehead McGinley

Quasicrystals were defined by Cain and Malheiro and Maas-Gariépy to model the decomposition of Schur polynomials into fundamental quasisymmetric functions. We define a new combinatorial model for crystal graphs of type $A_{n-1}$, called parsed content words, for which the decomposition into quasicrystals is particularly evident. We use the model to describe a combinatorial interpretation of Schur-Weyl duality and recover the classical combinatorial proof of the well-known expansion of homogeneous symmetric functions into Schur functions within our framework.
Inverse problems with fractional operators: an analytical study and its numerical linear algebra treatment via the GLT theory

Fractional derivatives model memory effects and nonlocal interactions beyond classical integer-order models. Fractional differential equations (FDEs) thus describe anomalous diffusion, transport in heterogeneous media, and hereditary dynamics. Their nonlocality, however, makes inverse problems challenging: unknown sources, coefficients, or initial conditions must be recovered from indirect and noisy data. Inverse problems for FDEs are usually ill-posed in the Hadamard sense, so regularization, such as the quasi-boundary value method, is required for stable reconstruction. Discretization produces large linear systems whose matrices inherit the nonlocal structure of fractional operators. Understanding the asymptotic spectral properties of these matrix sequences is essential for efficient solvers and preconditioners. Generalized Locally Toeplitz (GLT) theory provides a unified framework for the spectral distribution of large structured matrices and for preconditioner design. This thesis uses GLT theory to analyze matrix sequences from inverse problems for FDEs, construct structure-preserving preconditioners, and study nonlinear operations in the GLT algebra. In particular, it proves maximal distribution results for geometric means of GLT sequences: when the symbols commute, the geometric mean sequence remains GLT without symbol invertibility. This resolves a long-standing conjecture and shows maximality in the noncommuting degenerate case. Overall, the thesis integrates regularization, spectral analysis, and preconditioning into a coherent computational framework for inverse problems in nonlocal fractional dynamics, while enriching structured matrix analysis.
Relative delooping levels on intervals of torsion classes
Weiqing Cao; Mingfei Xu; Xiaojin Zhang

Let $U$ be a support $τ$-tilting module over a finite-dimensional algebra $A$, and let $\mathcal{V}\subseteq\operatorname{Fac}U$ be any torsion class. The exact heart $\mathcal{H}=\operatorname{Fac}U\cap\mathcal{V}^{\perp}$ has an Ext-progenerator $P$. We prove that $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,-)$ realizes $\mathcal{H}$ as a submodule-closed exact subcategory of $\operatorname{mod}B$, where $B=\text{End}_A(P)$, and preserves minimal syzygies. The global relative $k$-delooping levels are independent of $k\geq1$. Writing $g=\operatorname{glo}\text{-}\operatorname{dell}\mathcal{H}$, we obtain the sharp comparison $g\leq\operatorname{glo}\text{-}\operatorname{dell}B\leq g+1$ and $\operatorname{findim}B^{\mathrm{op}}\leq g+1$. Thus the two global levels are finite simultaneously. For wide hearts the relative levels equal their classical counterparts. We also characterize syzygy finiteness of $B$ by a finite relative syzygy stratum and obtain explicit bounds for both finitistic dimensions. If the heart is Frobenius, it is exactly the category of finitely generated Gorenstein-projective $B$-modules under this realization, and both self-injective dimensions of $B$ are at most one. We also give examples to show the main results.
Convergence Analysis of Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Descent under Relaxed Assumptions

We study convergence rates of Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Descent (NAG) method for convex optimization in both deterministic and stochastic settings. We focus on a more general smoothness condition raised from several machine learning problems empirically and theoretically. We show the accelerated convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}\left(1/T^2\right)$ in terms of the function value gap, given access to exact gradients of objective functions, matching the optimal rate for standard smooth convex optimization in \citep{nesterov1983method}. Under the relaxed affine-variance noise assumption for stochastic optimization, we establish the high-probability convergence rate of order $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sqrt{\log\left(1/δ\right)/T}\right)$ and this rate could improve to $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\log\left(1/δ\right)/T^2\right)$ when the noise parameters are sufficiently small. Here, $T$ denotes the total number of iterations and $δ$ is the probability margin. Up to logarithm factors, our probabilistic convergence rate reaches the same order of the expected rate obtained in \citep{ghadimi2016accelerated} where the assumptions of bounded variance noise and Lipschitz smoothness are required. We additionally establish the convergence rates of the studied algorithms in the non-convex setting.

We study $\mathbf{E}_n$-algebras with ramification in their $π_0$ and in particular show that the existence of ramification places strong limitations on their chromatic behavior. In particular, we show that $π_0$ of nonzero $K(1)$-local $\mathbf{E}_4$-$\mathrm{KU}$-algebras cannot have a map from the ring of integers in a ramified extension of $\mathbf{Q}_p$, and we show that a $p$-complete $\mathbf{E}_2$-ring with a map from a perfectoid ring into its $π_0$ is an associative $\mathbf{Z}_p$-algebra.
Uniform asymptotics and the Weil--Petersson constant

In their celebrated work on the large-genus asymptotic expansion of Weil--Petersson volumes, Mirzakhani and Zograf left open the question of whether the Weil--Petersson constant satisfies $C_{\mathrm{WP}}=π^{-1/2}$. We resolve the conjecture affirmatively. Our strategy is to consider a family of spectral curves interpolating between $y=z-4z^3$ and $y=\sin(2πz)/(2π)$. For each fixed number $n\geq2$ of marked points, we normalize the cusp coefficients using the action integral and the derivative at its first positive zero. We prove that the logarithmic derivatives of these normalized coefficients with respect to the family parameter are $O_n(g^{-1})$, uniformly along the family. The proof combines the descendant recursion, positivity, the dilaton equation, KdV, and coefficient asymptotics for the Painlevé I equation.
When Protection Hurts: A Cytokine Storm Theory of Supply Chain Overreaction

Supply chain resilience research has traditionally viewed defensive actions such as safety stock, backup suppliers, expedited transportation, and emergency sourcing as beneficial. However, disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2021 semiconductor shortage, and the Suez Canal blockage highlight how synchronized hoarding, duplicate ordering, and capacity reservation can amplify congestion and operational costs, sometimes worsening the original disruption. Motivated by this observation, we develop a decision-theoretic framework in which Protective Response Intensity (PRI) is an endogenous decision variable. We introduce Response-Induced Loss (RIL) to capture costs generated by defensive actions and characterize a unique optimal response that balances disruption mitigation against self-induced losses. We derive a closed-form critical response threshold beyond which RIL exceeds the original disruption intensity, a phenomenon termed a *Supply Chain Cytokine Storm*. We further propose the Cytokine Storm Index (CSI), measuring response-induced loss relative to the original disruption, and discuss its potential calibration using operational data. Extending the framework to interconnected supply networks, we derive a spectral stability condition distinguishing bounded decentralized responses from network-wide propagation. Numerical experiments show that optimal responses remain below the storm threshold, whereas proportional response heuristics can exceed it. Network responses converge or diverge according to the derived stability condition. Overall, our findings highlight that supply chain resilience depends not only on mitigating disruptions but also on keeping defensive responses proportionate to the shocks they are intended to address.
A Bestiary of Brownian Processes: A Field Guide to Boundary Conditions and Conditioning

The covariance of Brownian motion is the Green kernel of the one-dimensional Laplacian with a pinned left endpoint and a free right endpoint. This correspondence between Green's functions for the Laplacian on an interval and Brownian covariance functions turns out to be a general phenomenon. We use this correspondence to organize Brownian-derived Gaussian processes by three operations: choosing a self-adjoint realization, recentering a path, and conditioning a fixed law. Local Robin and selected nonlocal boundary conditions yield a catalogue of twelve processes with closed-form kernels, Brownian-path constructions, spectra and traces. The periodic and Neumann-Neumann realizations annihilate the constants; projecting the source and imposing zero time average selects the corresponding covariance pseudoinverses. Recentering and conditioning can both give a Brownian path zero time average, but the resulting laws differ: a constraint alone does not specify a process. A rank-one conditioning identity gives a scale-invariant criterion for the covariance effect of a shrinking family of observations. For Brownian finite differences of any fixed positive order, the covariance effect vanishes uniformly as the spacing tends to zero. For $m$-fold integrated Brownian motion, derivative constraints of orders $1,\ldots,m$ remain detectable at interior times. For simulation, we identify which grid constructions are exact and which are approximate.
Partial Information Decomposition When Some Sources Are Known: A Source Chain Rule and a No-Go Theorem

Partial information decomposition (PID) splits the information that several sources carry about a target into atoms, distinguished by which collections of sources give access to them. We ask how such a decomposition should behave when some of the sources are already known. The access structure of the atoms suggests one answer: discard the atoms that the known sources provide and regroup the rest according to which further sources unlock them. The classical construction of conditional information suggests another: recompute the decomposition under the conditional distributions and average. We show that the two answers agree, atom by atom, exactly when redundant information obeys a source chain rule, an analogue of the chain rule of mutual information: when the same sources are added to several collections, the enlarged collections share everything the added sources provide and, beyond that, exactly what the original collections share once the added sources are known. The rule divides established measures of redundant information, so that adopting or rejecting it genuinely narrows the choice of measure. Our main result is a no-go theorem: for three or more sources, the source chain rule and local positivity, the requirement that all atoms be nonnegative, cannot hold together in any PID.
Polynomial Residual Networks are Generically Identifiable
Isabel Dahlgren; Giovanni Luca Marchetti; Kathlén Kohn

We prove identifiability results for constant-width residual networks with polynomial activations and bias terms. For activations of degree at least five with generic coefficients, the fiber over a generic parameter is a singleton. For activations of degree at least three with no linear term after a suitable translation of the input, the generic fiber is given by translating biases and then scaling weights and translated biases by real roots of unity. These results specialize to networks without bias terms. With the same proof technique, we further derive necessary conditions for critical points of the ResNet parametrization, that are central in singular learning theory.

For a quasi-projective variety $X$ defined over a number field $k$, let $X'$ be its Weil restriction with respect to a finite field extension $k/k'$. We prove that the Brauer--Manin set of $X$ agrees with the Brauer--Manin set of $X'$. We also prove the agreement for Brauer--Manin set of them given by $\mathrm{Br}_1$.
On the positive Lebesgue measure of (n,k,t)-sets

We study sets in R^n that contain a unit k-dimensional disk in each direction from a subset of the Grassmannian G(n,k) of Hausdorff dimension at least t; we call them (n,k,t)-sets. In the range 2k>n, we prove that every (n,k,t)-set has positive Lebesgue measure whenever t>k(n-k-1)+1. This follows from a sharp Sobolev-to-L^2 estimate for the k-plane maximal operator over a Frostman measure on G(n,k), which also yields an L^p-L^2 estimate for every p>n/k with respect to Haar measure. In the range 2k<=n, where translations can no longer be ignored, we obtain the same threshold via a lifting argument, conditional on the quantitative Kakeya estimate in dimension n-k+1. Using the quantitative Kakeya estimate of Wang and Zahl in dimension 3, we deduce that (4,2,t)-sets have positive measure for t>3. The threshold t>k(n-k-1)+1 is sharp, in the sense that (n,k,t)-sets of measure zero exist at t=k(n-k-1)+1. These results improve the previous threshold t>n/2+k(n-k-1) of Fraser, Harris and Kroon, and give the first restricted-direction results in the range 2k<=n.
On the power of adaption and randomization 2: Non-symmetric convex sets
David Krieg; Erich Novak; Mario Ullrich

Let $S:X\to Y$ be a bounded linear operator between real Banach spaces, and let $F\subset X$ be nonempty, bounded and convex. We prove $$a_{2n-1}(S,F)\le 27n\min \{ e^{\rm ran}_n (S,F), e^{\rm ada}_n (S,F)\}.$$ Here $a_k$ is the minimal worst-case error of continuous affine algorithms of rank at most $k$, and $e_n^{\rm ran}$ and $e_n^{\rm ada}$ are the minimal errors of adaptive randomized and deterministic algorithms using at most $n$ continuous linear measurements. This shows that the gain of adaption and randomization, and even nonlinearity, is limited by a factor $27n$ for approximation in convex sets. We discuss the optimality of the result by examples.
Learning Representative Port Subsets for Efficient Fluid Antenna Systems

Fluid antenna systems (FASs) provide many candidate ports, but probing all ports for each channel realization incurs substantial online overhead. We study a complementary offline problem: compress the candidate-port space once and reuse the compressed set across future channel realizations. The method collects optimal ports from sampled training realizations, requiring only one scan of the candidate ports per realization. On a DeepMIMO 7-by-7 FAS with 49 candidate ports, 120 training realizations yield 27 representative ports on average while retaining 99.995% of the channel power gain achieved by exhaustive port selection.
Movable Curves and Ample Normal Bundles

We prove that the movable cone of a smooth complex projective variety is the closed cone generated by possibly singular curves with ample coherent normal sheaves, answering a question of Boucksom--Demailly--Păun--Peternell. For smooth curves, we establish the analogous equality in several geometric settings and give explicit constructions on blowups.
Task-Directed Spectral Design for Local Quantum Tomography

Many tomography tasks require only a low-dimensional function of the state. We study local pure-state tomography under projective-fidelity access when a parametric model, a credible center, and a differentiable downstream task are known before acquisition. The pullback Fubini--Study metric and the task metric define coordinate-invariant generalized eigendirections, which we realize as a fixed library of geodesic fidelity probes. We prove two optimality results: the probe aligned with a task coordinate is its unique variance-minimizing location up to orientation, and, when prior and measurement information are diagonal in this basis, a diminishing-return greedy rule exactly minimizes the integer-budget local task-variance surrogate over the spectral library. Under common per-shot information and the stated large-budget condition, the absolute and relative gaps to arbitrary probe directions are respectively \(O(B^{-3})\) and \(O(B^{-2})\). A closed-form local estimator is followed by a task-metric localization projection that cannot increase quadratic task loss when localization holds. In six-qubit numerical experiments, the Schmidt-spectrum design activates only one or two settings and has lower mean task error than the post hoc best adaptive results across all tested dimensions and copy budgets. For full-state tomography, it likewise has lower mean infidelity throughout the tested local regime. The fixed batch uses no feedback loops and far fewer settings; under the illustrative latency model, its acquisition cost is roughly three to four orders of magnitude lower than that of the adaptive methods.
Multi-marginal optimal transport on sub-Riemannian manifolds

In this paper, we study multi-marginal optimal transport on ideal sub-Riemannian manifolds. We establish a sub-Riemannian barycentric balance condition and prove the existence of a solution to the Monge problem under an additional assumption. We also investigate the absolute continuity of Wasserstein barycenters. Our results extend and improve upon those of Pass, Pinamonti, and Vedovato (Methods Appl. Anal. 28 (2021), 61-76) on the Heisenberg group, answering two open questions raised in their work.
Compactness of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees

In this paper, we present a complete characterization of the compactness of arbitrary finite linear combinations of composition operators acting on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees. In particular, we obtain a characterization of compactness for linear combinations satisfying the CNC. As an application, we give an affirmative answer to a conjecture raised by Choe et al. [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B 9(2022), 733--756] concerning such Hardy spaces. Furthermore, we establish the phenomenon of (double) difference cancellation for linear combinations of composition operators by constructing explicit examples.
A Necessary and Sufficient Condition for the Existence of Global Smooth Solutions to the One-Dimensional Inviscid Burgers-Vlasov System

We investigate global smooth solvability for the one-dimensional inviscid Burgers-Vlasov system. For a smooth initial fluid velocity and a nonnegative, compactly supported particle distribution, we establish a sharp necessary and sufficient threshold expressed through the sum of the initial velocity gradient and the initial particle density. The principal difficulty is to control simultaneously the nonlinear steepening of the fluid velocity, the drag coupling, the particle velocity support, and the full hierarchy of derivatives. To overcome it, we introduce a combined gradient-density quantity whose evolution closes along fluid characteristics. Its sign invariance, together with characteristic support estimates and fixed-order derivative bounds, yields global continuation whenever the initial threshold is nonnegative. If the threshold fails at one point, a Riccati comparison gives an explicit finite upper bound for the maximal smooth lifespan and identifies negative velocity-gradient blow-up when this bound is attained. We also use nonnegative regularization and compactness to extend the threshold result to initial data of any fixed finite regularity.
Weak mixing and non-recurrence along finitely generated multiplicative semigroups of $\mathbb N$

Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of primes, and let $S_{\mathcal P}$ be the multiplicative semigroup that they generate. We prove that there are an invertible weakly mixing measure-preserving transformation $T$ and a set $A$ of positive measure such that $A\cap T^{-r}A=\varnothing$ for every $r\in S_{\mathcal P}$. This gives a negative answer to Bergelson's 1996 question concerning recurrence along $\{2^m3^n:m,n\geq1\}$, and applies to every finitely generated multiplicative semigroup of positive integers. More generally, we give a sufficient condition for weakly mixing non-recurrence based on divisibility properties and separation by finitely many rotations of the circle. This criterion also applies to an infinitely generated multiplicative semigroup not contained in any $S_{\mathcal P}$ with $\mathcal P$ finite.
A no-go theorem for closed timelike curves in globally null-foliated spacetimes

The study of closed timelike curves has proceeded one spacetime at a time, and the criteria available form three families, the time function criteria, the energy condition criteria, and the topological criteria. We initiate a fourth family of criteria, elementary in form and resting on a single scalar equation rather than any energy condition. We prove that a spacetime admitting a globally defined function whose gradient is everywhere null cannot contain a closed timelike curve, and that the hypothesis is logically independent of stable causality rather than weaker than it. The proof turns on one algebraic fact, that a null covector is never orthogonal to a timelike vector, so the function grows strictly along every timelike curve and cannot close. Because the null eikonal equation alone decides the criterion, we can use it where the classical time function theorem is silent. We establish for the first time that no Kundt spacetime and no Robinson--Trautman spacetime can contain a closed timelike curve on any region where the null coordinate is globally single valued, whatever the cosmological constant and the rotation one form, which settles a question left open for gyratonic waves. We further show that the Misner, Ori and Ahmed constructions reduce to the statement that a compact null direction has turned timelike, and that the cosmological constant, the expansion and the shear are spectators in all of them.
Dirichlet problem on locally finite graphs (revised and extended version)

We study existence and uniqueness of solutions to the vertex-weighted Dirichlet problem on locally finite graphs. Let $B$ be a subset of the vertices of a connected graph $G$. The Dirichlet problem asks for a function whose discrete Laplacian is prescribed on $V\setminus B$ and whose values are prescribed on $B$. Each infinite connected component of $G\setminus B$ is called an end of $G$ relative to $B$. On finite graphs we show that the solution is the limit of an averaging process, with an explicit geometric rate given by the spectrum of the random walk, and is also the limit of the heat flow and the minimizer of an energy functional. On infinite graphs we prove two existence theorems: one with no assumption on vertex degrees, under a finite-width condition and summable data, and one for bounded data on graphs of bounded degree, where the solution is also unique among bounded functions. If there are no ends, the Dirichlet problem has exactly one solution. If there are $l$ ends, the solution set, when nonempty, has dimension at least $l$; each end carries a positive harmonic function vanishing on $B$. Calling an end parabolic when the random walk started in it hits $B$ almost surely, we show that this function can be taken bounded exactly on non-parabolic ends and is necessarily unbounded on parabolic ones, a discrete analogue of a theorem of Li and Tam. Consequently, bounded solutions are unique if and only if every end is parabolic.
On optimal stopping problems with full information and rank-dependent reward

In this paper we consider optimal stopping problems with full information and rank-dependent rewards. Our focus is on the following two problems: selecting one of the r best observations (Gusein-Zade's problem with full information) and minimizing the expected rank (Robbins' problem). In both settings we provide full characterization of the optimal stopping rules and corresponding optimal values. We also present numerical experiments in which the derived dynamic programming recursions are implemented, and approximations to optimal values are computed.
Finite-Time Blow-Up for Wave Equations with Nonlinear \(p\)-Laplacian Damping

We consider a wave equation with linear elasticity, nonlinear \(p\)-Laplacian damping acting on the velocity, and a focusing power source in a bounded three-dimensional domain. For \(2<p<r+1\leq6\), we prove finite-time blow-up in the natural energy norm for initial data in \(H_0^1(Ω)\times L^2(Ω)\) lying in the unstable potential well below its depth. This includes every nonzero initial state with nonpositive total energy and requires no sign condition on the initial displacement--velocity pairing. For positive initial energy, we establish a sufficient condition for finite-time blow-up involving the \(L^2\) pairing of the initial velocity with a fixed approximation of the initial displacement. The proof combines a shifted displacement multiplier, an auxiliary quantity built from the time integral of the spatial \(L^p\)-norm of the velocity gradient, and a weighted auxiliary functional. Linking the weight parameter to the initial value of the cumulative quantity allows us to absorb the mixed terms in the auxiliary functional estimate. Together with the shifted displacement multiplier, this yields upper bounds for the maximal existence time in both ranges \(2<p\leq3\) and \(p>3\), without assuming \(W_0^{1,p}(Ω)\) regularity of the initial displacement.
Noninteger completely monotonic degrees of Stirling remainders and their derivatives

For Stirling expansions truncated after at least two Bernoulli terms, we disprove the three real-degree conjectures recorded by Mahmoud and Qi for the signed remainders of the logarithm of the gamma function and their derivatives. We give a unified proof of the corresponding integer-degree formula, recovering known cases and resolving Zhu's conjectures for higher derivatives in this range. Every real completely monotonic degree lies strictly between the predicted integer and the next integer. We obtain a universal fractional lower bound through an explicit inverse function and a simpler rational bound valid for every derivative order. A local estimate for the negative part of the Laplace kernel's derivative with respect to its logarithmic variable makes the lower improvement proportional to the reciprocal of the combined truncation and derivative order. Together with a uniform upper bound, this determines the exact order of decay of the fractional excess for each fixed derivative order and for its supremum over all derivative orders. Sharper kernel estimates give stronger bounds for the first two degrees. The proof combines fractional positivity criteria, the classical Laplace representation, a sign characterization of the associated densities, and a convexity obstruction at the upper integer endpoint. All estimates used in the proofs are analytic. The exact real degrees and the optimal asymptotic constants remain open.
On the isomorphism problem of Cayley digraphs

A finite group $G$ is called a DCI-group provided any two Cayley digraphs $Cay(G,S)$ and $Cay(G,T)$ are isomorphic iff the two connection sets $S$ and $T$ are images of each other via automorphisms of the group $G$. Building on the vast literature on CI- and DCI-groups we present an updated list of possible DCI-groups. In addition, we give an alternative proof that does not rely on deep results from group theory. We also point out the three most important open problems related to the classification of DCI-groups.
Failure of interior $L^p$ estimates for nonlocal elliptic equations with continuous kernels

Let $0<σ<2$ and $1\leq p<\infty$. We construct a fixed linear nonlocal elliptic operator $L$ and functions $u_m\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^n)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ such that \[ \|u_m\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)}+\|Lu_m\|_{L^p(B_2)}\longrightarrow0, \qquad \liminf_{m\to\infty}\|(-Δ)^{σ/2}u_m\|_{L^p(B_1)}>0. \] The kernel is symmetric in the increment variable, uniformly elliptic, and satisfies the standard bounds on its first two derivatives in that variable. Its dependence on $x$ has a uniform modulus of continuity of order $(\log(1/r))^{-1/2}$ as $r\downarrow0$. Moreover, $\|Du_m\|_{L^p(B_4)}\to0$ for $σ>1$, and these norms remain bounded for $σ=1$. Thus the interior $L^p$ estimates for translation-invariant operators do not extend to this class under mere continuity in $x$.
Limiting moments of sample covariance matrices from large fold tensor vectors

We study the moments of sample covariance matrices $M_{n,k,m}$ formed from independent $k$-fold tensor products of $n$-dimensional random vectors. The base vectors have independent and identically distributed centered complex entries with unit variance and finite moments of all orders. For every fixed $p \in \mathbb N_+$, under suitable moment conditions, we obtain an asymptotic formula for $p$th moment as $n, k, m$ tend to infinity with $m/n^k \to c \in (0,\infty)$. There is no restriction on the growth rate of $k$ relative to $n$. We also prove a variance bound and obtain the corresponding almost sure asymptotic formula. The results recover known limiting moments in several regimes. When $k/n$ tends to infinity and the modulus of base vector entry is not constant, we establish the asymptotic growth rate for the $p$th moment of normalized matrices. In this regime, we also provide a lower bound for the growth rate of the largest eigenvalue.
Sharp Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for $q$-Araki-Woods Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Semigroups

In this paper, we establish the sharp $2$-logarithmic Sobolev inequality for $q$-Araki-Woods Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroups with $-1<q<1$ and obtain hypercontractivity along the Gross curve with the optimal coefficient, and determine the exact hypercontractive time for $1<p\le2\le r<\infty$. Reverse hypercontractivity holds in the two separate ranges $0<p<r<1$ and $-\infty<p<r<0$. An explicit counterexample rules out the proposed universal reverse curve across zero. We also obtain the complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality via the intertwining property.
Pseudospectral phenomena preventing the analyticity sector of a Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup to be ruled by the spectral angle of its generator

We study elliptic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operators in $L^2$ spaces with respect to invariant measures. These operators have discrete spectra and generate analytic semigroups. The angle defining the analyticity sector of a Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup is not always equal to the complementary angle of the spectral angle of its generator. In this work, we study the link between these two angles. More specifically, we provide a necessary and sufficient criterion ensuring that they are complementary, and explain how pseudospectral phenomena account for these two angles to fail to be complementary.
The chromatic number of a random graph with $o(n^{3/2})$ edges
Amin Coja-Oghlan; Mikhail Isaev; Mihyun Kang; Pavel Zakharov

Let $G(n,m)$ be the Erdos-Renyi random graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges and let $δ>0$. Alon and Krivelevich [Combinatorica 1997] proved that for any sequence $m\leq n^{3/2-δ}$ there \emph{exists} an integer sequence $q=q(n)$ such that the chromatic number of $G(n,m)$ equals either $q$ or $q+1$ with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$. In this paper, we give an explicit formula for this sequence $q(n)$ and confirm their result under a less restrictive assumption that $m=o(n^{3/2})$. Furthermore, we show that for all but a vanishing proportion of the admissible values of $m$, the chromatic number of $G(n,m)$ equals $q$ with high probability.
Extremal diagonal-coherent binary codes: shortened Hamming cores, deep holes, and the 64 I-Ching hexagrams

Each of the 64 hexagrams of the I-Ching, or Book of Changes, is a stack of six Yin-Yang lines and is therefore a binary vector of length 6; the eight hexagrams formed by repeating a single trigram span a doubled-trigram subspace $Δ$. We ask which binary $[6,3,3]$ codes are compatible with this trigram structure. We show that a $[6,3,3]$ code meets $Δ$ in at most four codewords, that the four are then forced to be the doubled trigrams Earth, Fire, Wind and Lake, and that exactly two codes attain this bound: the shortened Hamming code $\mathcal C_A$ and its dual. Since $\mathcal C_A$ has covering radius 2, its eight codewords, their radius-one balls, and its eight deep holes together reconstruct all 64 hexagrams. In general, we call a binary code of length $2m$ with $d \ge 3$ diagonal-coherent if it contains the half of the diagonal subspace $\{(u,u)\}$ coming from even-weight vectors $u$ -- the largest part of that subspace a single-error-correcting code can contain -- and extremal if its dimension is as large as possible. For $m\ge2$ and $r=\lceil\log_2(2m+1)\rceil$, we determine the number $N(m)$ of extremal diagonal-coherent codes with parameters $[\,2m,\ 2m-r,\ \ge3\,]$, show that diagonal coherence entails no loss of redundancy, and determine their minimum distances. We also put these codes in a normal form, determine their hulls, and show that each has covering radius $2$ with exactly $2^r-1-2m$ deep-hole cosets. Finally we propose three open problems.
Which posets are spectra of Noetherian rings? The case of height at most one

A finite poset is the prime spectrum of a Noetherian ring exactly when it has no chain of three elements, that is, it is the poset of a finite bipartite graph. This answers Conjecture 5.3 of Alkass. The substance is a construction: minimal elements become curves y=g_i(x), maximal elements points, edges the incidences, arranged by interpolation. The coordinate ring of the union of the curves, localized at the chosen points, is essentially of finite type over Q and of dimension at most one. Dropping finiteness costs two conditions, both isolated by Colbert: a poset with no chain of three elements is a Noetherian spectrum exactly when it has finitely many minimal elements and any two distinct ones have finitely many common upper bounds. A variant keeping the shape of the ideals of Alkass but changing their exponents shows why that construction produces only nested neighborhoods. Constraining the ring destroys most of this freedom: normal rings leave finite disjoint unions of stars, domains a single star, local rings a point or a finite co-star. In height two the question is open in general, but the conditions conjectured by Wiegand and Wiegand are not sufficient

We classify the representation-finite, tame, and wild contraction algebras arising from 3-fold flopping contractions of isolated cDV singularities with at worst Gorenstein terminal sources. To achieve this, we first determine the representation type of all contracted preprojective algebras of Dynkin types $\mathsf{A}$, $\mathsf{D}$, and $\mathsf{E}$, and then use the representation type invariance under iterated flops and the radical structure of contraction algebras.
An Integrated Framework for Assessing Interpretability in Exploratory Factor Analysis
Mariaelena Bottazzi Schenone; Tiziano Iannaccio; Ilaria Mozzetta; Maurizio Vichi

Interpretability in Exploratory Factor Analysis is characterized by the fundamental trade-off between structural sparseness and explained common variance. Lacking formal evaluation metrics, researchers frequently sacrifice parsimony in the pattern matrix to maximize the model's explanatory coverage. For this reason, we extend Hoyer's sparseness ratio into a flexible \texorpdfstring{$\mathcal{L}_{p_1}/\mathcal{L}_{p_2}$}{Lp1/Lp2} formulation to introduce the Interpretability Index $I$, defined as the geometric mean of explained common variance and the generalized sparseness index. We analyze the asymptotic behavior of $I$ as norm orders increase, establishing that raising $p_2$ alone yields a stable limit, whereas increasing $p_1$ and $p_2$ jointly causes the measure to saturate. The canonical choice $(p_1,p_2)=(2,4)$ balances numerical stability with a smooth, tractable objective. We finally demonstrate, on five benchmark datasets from the statistical literature, how the Interpretability Index provides a systematic criterion for selecting the optimal parametrization of the latent space according to the user's analytical goals.
Renewable model averaging for generalized linear models
Yalu Ping; Chen Xuerong; Yu Dalei

Prediction is one of the most important research topics in statistics and machine learning. Moreover, in the domain of streaming data analysis, real-time prediction has become a rapidly growing research field in recent years, owing to the abundance of streaming data. In many fields of scientific research, such as biomedical research, weather forecasting, and traffic management, improving real-time prediction of streaming data is crucial in general. However, the complicated features of streaming data, such as large-scale and high-velocity, impose both theoretical and computational challenges to the development and evaluation of real-time prediction in this field, especially when the investigator has multiple models at hand. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel Renewable Model Averaging method through Quadratic approximation (ReMAQ) for generalized linear model (GLM) for streaming data. By approximating the model averaging procedure for GLMs (which is typically a convex optimization problem) with a quadratic optimization formulation, ReMAQ allows us to update the model averaging prediction sequentially when a new batch of data arrives, without accessing the entire historical data. Moreover, ReMAQ is also computationally efficient as one only needs to consider a quadratic programming problem in each steps of updating. Under certain regular conditions, we also show that the proposed ReMAQ weight is asymptotically equivalent to that by the oracle model averaging based on the inaccessible full data, the asymptotic optimality of ReMAQ is then established accordingly. The proposed method is also assessed by simulation studies. We apply our proposed ReMAQ in the study of the Airline On-Time Performance Dataset and the results demonstrate the superiority our method in practical situations.
Global Boundedness and Finite-Time Blow-up for a Quasilinear Chemotaxis--May--Nowak System
Xueli Bai; Fang Li; Suying Liu

This paper continues the work of Bai, Li, Liu and Luo \cite{BaiLiLiuLuoPreprint} on a quasilinear chemotaxis--May--Nowak system. We establish global boundedness in three dimensions for both the parabolic--elliptic--parabolic and fully parabolic systems when $m>4/3$. For the former, we construct finite-time blow-up solutions in balls when $n=3$ and $1<m\le4/3$, and when $n\ge4$ and $0<m\le2-2/n$.
Linear statistics in the Coulomb gas: cumulants beyond rotational invariance
Paul Bourgade; Pierre Le Doussal; Gregory Schehr
