We describe $\operatorname{Aut}(S)$ in terms of the coefficients of the normal form, prove that $|\operatorname{Aut}(S)|\leq 72$, and classify the surfaces attaining the bound: two surfaces with singular canonical model and a one-parameter family $X_r$ of smooth surfaces. For the surfaces $X_r$ we compute a basis of the primitive cohomology consisting of eigenvectors of a subgroup $\mathbf{Z}/6\mathbf{Z} \times \mathbf{Z}/6\mathbf{Z}$ of $\operatorname{Aut}(X_r)$, given by residues of explicit polynomials, together with the intersection form in this basis. We then show that the natural map from $\operatorname{Aut}(X_r)$ to the group of Hodge isometries of the primitive lattice modulo $\pm1$ is injective but has image of index at least $331\,776$, so that the Torelli principle for automorphisms fails for these surfaces.
Protect the Decision, Not the Disaster: Regret-Robust Capacity Sizing and Positioning with Transportation Recourse

An operator who positions mobile resources before a disruption faces two uncertainties that are usually treated as one: how the joint state of demand and travel conditions will vary, and which part of the resulting cost the positioning decision can actually change. Standard distributionally robust optimization (DRO) protects total cost, and therefore spends much of its protection on disruption costs that every feasible design would pay. This paper evaluates the worst-case regret of a design and compares it with the worst-case premium of total-cost DRO, and shows that the regret-to-premium ratio can be bounded before any robust model is solved: from marginals for the dependence question, and from single-scenario optima and one transport linear program for the regret question. The worst-case law is a relabelling of the operating record, reassigning every recorded period wholesale to another recorded period, except at most one, which is split. The comparator that exposes the largest worst-case regret is found by a single mixed-integer program. We derive an explicit radius where the sample-average design is exactly regret-robust. For finite scenario and design sets we compute a design's worst-case regret exactly, bound it from quantities a planner already has, and show on fleet and EMS data how law-relative regret changes capacity and positioning choices relative to sample-average and worst-cost planning. We apply the decision tree to several years of New York fleet data, including the year before Hurricane Sandy, and to two emergency-service events. The test flags the pre-Sandy year as exposed. The training-support regret bounds cover realized test regret in three of four fleet folds. On Ida, where the regret-robust allocation differed from the sample-average one, it moved units toward the boroughs the storm loaded and cost less than the sample-average design.
Optimal Non-Homogeneous Improvements of the Anisotropic Hardy Inequality
Giuseppina di Blasio; Giovanni Pisante; Georgios Psaradakis

We consider the Hardy inequality associated with a strongly convex Finsler norm $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and we study its optimal non-homogeneous improvements in the whole range $1<p<\infty$. We show that the anisotropic Hardy difference controls a weighted critical Sobolev norm when $1<p<n$, a weighted exponential integrability of Trudinger type when $p=n$, where the Hardy term is replaced by its Leray logarithmic correction, and a weighted Hölder seminorm when $p>n$, proving in each regime that the logarithmic weights appear with the optimal exponents. In the borderline case $p=n$ this extends to general functions the optimal exponent previously known only for anisotropically radial functions. The proofs rely on a common ground-state reduction, combined with a splitting into an $F_o$-radial and a mean-free part for $1<p\le n$, and with an anisotropic Morrey representation formula for $p>n$.
The Number of Polytope Trees and Beyond

We study the symmetry-weighted enumeration of complexes formed by gluing copies of a regular polytope. For polytope trees and complexes obtained by attaching such trees to a fixed initial complex, we derive cut-and-join recurrences, differential equations for generating functions, explicit counting formulas, and asymptotic estimates. We then extend the method to complexes with cycles in their dual graphs, enumerating them by the numbers of polytopes and free facets. We derive recurrence relations and partial differential equations for the corresponding bivariate generating functions. In this setting, we obtain recurrences for connected configurations and explicit coefficient formulas for possibly disconnected configurations, both with and without a distinguished initial complex.
Berry-Esseen bounds for products of random matrices under a $2+δ$ polynomial moment
Zhi-Jun Cai; Qi-Man Shao; Hui Xiao; Zhuo-Song Zhang

Let $(g_{k})_{k \geq 1}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed matrices with law $μ$ on $\mathrm{GL}(d,\mathbb{R})$, where $d\geq2$ is an integer. Suppose that the closed semigroup generated by the support of $μ$ is strongly irreducible and proximal and that the polynomial moment of order $2+δ$ is finite, where $0<δ\leq 1$. We establish a Berry-Esseen bound of order $n^{-δ/2}$ for $\log \| g_{n} \cdots g_{1} v\|$, where $v$ is a nonzero vector in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $\|\cdot\|$ is an arbitrary norm on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. As an application, we also obtain a Berry-Esseen bound of order $n^{-δ/2}$ for $\log \| g_{n} \cdots g_{1}\|$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is any matrix norm. The proof combines an $m$-dependent approximation with Stein's method. The argument uses identities for exchangeable pairs constructed by resampling individual matrices, together with a concentration inequality for sums of the approximating variables.
When Are Nesterov Trajectories Eventually Locally Minimizing?

We revisit the variational characterization of Nesterov's celebrated method and study when Nesterov trajectories are eventually locally minimizing in a variational sense, a notion that we define precisely. We show that this question is equivalent to the nonnegativity of an associated Schrödinger operator acting on variations of the trajectory. For power objectives of the form \[ f(x)=\frac{1}{p}\|x\|^p \] (where $\| \cdot\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm), we give a complete characterization: Among all exponents $p\ge 2$, the Nesterov trajectory with non-zero initial position is eventually locally minimizing if and only if $p=4$. We further interpret this exceptional exponent through the stability theory of semilinear elliptic equations.
Joint Service Depth and Priority Design in Queueing Systems
Adam N. Elmachtoub; Yash Kanoria; Jonathan Y. Tan

In AI-assisted service systems, the server can choose how much processing effort to spend on each job, which we call the service depth. Deeper reasoning improves output quality but occupies the server longer and increases congestion, and the realized processing time remains random because AI models are probabilistic and tasks vary in complexity. We study the joint design of service depth and priority in a single-server queue whose customers differ in delay sensitivity, with the goal of maximizing social welfare. For each customer type, the decision maker chooses a priority level and a service depth, and service times are exponential with mean equal to the chosen depth. With two customer types and linear service values, we characterize the centralized optimum. Counterintuitively, it prioritizes the patient type and gives it a smaller service depth when patient customers are sufficiently prevalent. When delay sensitivity is private, however, incentive compatibility requires the impatient type to receive a weakly shorter sojourn time, so the optimal price menu never prioritizes the patient type. Consequently, there can be a welfare gap between the centralized decision maker's optimal control policy and the optimal decentralized pricing mechanism. With a continuum of types, the centralized optimum is monotone: more delay-sensitive customers receive weakly smaller depth and higher priority, so the optimum can be implemented by a price menu with no welfare loss. Allowing randomized depths similarly closes the gap in the two-type model. Finally, we calibrate an agentic AI service system using published coding-agent trials from DeepSWE and numerically examine priority inversion, the value of joint design, and the welfare gain from personalization.
First-order Methods for Variational Inequality Problems with Semi-Infinite Constraints

This paper studies first-order methods for monotone variational inequalities with semi-infinite constraints and presents this model as a framework covering constrained saddle-point problems, robust optimization, distributionally robust function-constrained optimization, and generalized Nash equilibrium formulations. Since feasibility must hold over infinitely many indexed constraints, direct projection onto the full feasible region is generally difficult. Therefore, we propose a single-loop primal-dual constraint extrapolation method (PD-ConEx) that updates primal variables, Lagrange multipliers, and worst-case constraint indices using first-order information, linearization, extrapolation, and projections only onto simple sets. We establish convergence guarantees for smooth and nonsmooth regimes, showing how the achievable rates depend on strong monotonicity and strong concavity of the index block. For coupled convex-concave saddle-point problems, strong convexity in the minimization block can accelerate its smooth terms even without strong concavity in the maximization block. We also develop an adaptive smooth variant with $O(1/K)$ VI-gap and feasibility guarantees without an a priori bound on generated multipliers. Moment-based and Wasserstein distributionally robust models fit within the framework, and numerical experiments on robust quadratic instances and distributionally robust learning illustrate the method's optimality and feasibility behavior.
The Intersection of nested filled-in little Julia sets have zero area

It is shown that for any infinitely renormalizable quadratic polynomial $Q_c$ the intersection $K_\infty$ of all the little filled-in Julia sets (renormalization Julia sets) containing the critical value have zero area.
Stability of certain elements in the Bernstein center

Let $G$ be a split connected reductive algebraic group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. The stable center conjecture asserts that the subspace of stable elements in the Bernstein center of $G(F)$ is a sub-algebra, and this subring is conjecturally isomorphic to the regular functions on the moduli of semi-simple Langlands parameters. Bezrukavnikov-Kazhdan-Varshavsky suggested an approach towards the stable center conjecture by explicitly constructing elements and proving their stability directly without assuming LLC, and proved the stability of the depth-$r$ projectors. Following the idea, the first author and Tsao-Hsien Chen produced a family of elements in the center which are conjecturally stable using Deligne-Lusztig parameters attached to irreducible representations. This paper proves the stability of the projectors corresponding to strongly regular Deligne-Lusztig parameters in depth-zero, and for all the positive depth elements with some restrictions on the residue characteristic.
Consistency in fractional Korn's inequalities on Lipschitz domains

We investigate fractional analogs of Korn's inequality on bounded Lipschitz domains in several contexts. Constrained and unconstrained inequalities are established; constraints include quotient spaces and spaces incorporating various classes of boundary conditions or volume constraints. We also expand the parameters of integrability for which the inequalities hold. Specifically, a fractional Korn's first unconstrained inequality holds for vector fields in the fractional Sobolev space $W^{s,p}(Ω;\mathbb{R}^n)$ for all $p \in [1,\infty]$ and all $s \in (0,1)$. In the cases $p = 1$ and $p = \infty$, the inequality has no local analog. We quantify this by investigating the consistency of the inequalities as the differentiability parameter $s \to 1$; the universal constant in the inequality remains stable for $p \in (1,\infty)$ but degenerates for $p \in \{1,\infty\}$. We introduce an explicit $L^p$-bounded projection operator onto infinitesimal rigid motions as a key tool to quantitatively strengthen the inequality.
A proof of Wang's planar D-coloring conjecture

We prove Wang's planar D-coloring conjecture. A D-coloring of a graph is a proper edge coloring in which every subgraph isomorphic to $K_4$ minus an edge is rainbow. Wang conjectured that every planar graph of maximum degree $Δ$ has a D-coloring with 9 colors if $Δ=4$, 10 colors if $Δ=5$, and $2Δ-1$ colors if $Δ\ge 6$. Hu, Kong and Wang proved the cases $Δ\le 5$ and $Δ\ge 33$. We prove the sharp bound $2Δ-1$ for every $Δ\ge 6$, settling the remaining cases. The proof uses discharging; the case $Δ=6$ is computer-assisted.
Statistical inference for boundary constrained parameters
Jaeseon Lee; Anirban Bhattacharya; Suhasini Subba Rao

Estimation and inference under boundary constraints arises in many areas of statistics, but the available asymptotic theory remains limited and fragmented relative to the classical case, where the parameter lies in the interior of the parameter space. In this paper we derive a boundary-constrained analogue of the standard asymptotic expansion for a minimiser of a loss function, in which the deviation of the estimator from the population parameter is decomposed over lower-dimensional subspaces determined by the directional derivatives at the minimiser. Using this decomposition we show that the limiting distribution of the estimator is a mixture of point masses and truncated skew-normal distributions, with mixture probabilities determined by the directional derivative conditions. A consequence of this result is that the constrained and unconstrained coordinates do not separate: the presence of parameters on or near the boundary affects the sampling distribution of the unconstrained parameter estimators. We apply the expansion to obtain the asymptotic distribution of the quasi log-likelihood ratio statistic under a range of null hypotheses, and since the resulting mixture is not pivotal in the quasi-likelihood setting, we propose a simulation-based procedure for approximating critical values. The framework unifies and simplifies several existing results. We illustrate the methodology by testing for interactions in exponential family graphical models, where the parameters are subject to compatibility constraints that ensure a joint distribution exists.
Intermediate subalgebras of cross-product von Neumann algebras arising from weakly compact actions

In this short paper, we establish the following Galois-type property for all measure-preserving, weakly compact actions $G \curvearrowright (X,μ) $ of a non-inner amenable group $G$ on a standard probability space $X$: for any intermediate von Neumann subalgebra $\mathcal L(G)\subseteq \mathcal N \subseteq L^\infty (X)\rtimes G$, there is a factor $G\curvearrowright Y$ of $G \curvearrowright X$ such that $\mathcal N= L^\infty(Y)\rtimes G$. In particular, this holds for all pmp distal actions $G\curvearrowright X$, thereby answering positively an open problem from \cite{BCCMSW24} (which can also be traced back to \cite{CD20}). We also provide an example showing our result is optimal.
Concurrent Space-Based Observer Placement and Scheduling for Cislunar Space Domain Awareness
Dominic K. Amato; Hang Woon Lee

As interest in cislunar space grows, so does the need for space domain awareness (SDA) capabilities to safely support missions. To enhance cislunar SDA capabilities, the use of space-based observers has been proposed. Prior research has explored optimizing observer placement but has not considered scheduling limitations. We propose a mixed-integer linear programming formulation that concurrently optimizes the placement and scheduling of space-based observers for cislunar SDA. Our work considers three aspects of observer scheduling: sensor tasking, communication, and charging. We utilize a scenario-based approach that generalizes observer placement for unknown targets while applying scheduling constraints to each scenario. However, this problem quickly becomes difficult for commercial solvers to handle as the number of scenarios grows. As an alternative, a column generation approach is employed to introduce well-performing schedules into the problem for each orbital slot. A comparative analysis is performed across multiple instances to evaluate the performance of column generation against that of a commercial solver. A case study is then conducted in which the performance of the observers' placement from the concurrent formulation is tested against a set of validation target sets and compared with the performance of two baselines in which placement and scheduling are performed sequentially.
A crystallographic quotient of the framed braid group and associated flat manifolds
Ênio Leite; Oscar Ocampo; Paulo Cesar Cerqueira dos Santos Júnior; Ana Carolina Moura Teixeira

We study the quotient of the framed braid group $FB_n$ by the commutator subgroup of the framed pure braid group $FP_n$. We prove that $$ \frac{FB_n}{[FP_n,FP_n]}\cong\mathbb Z^n\rtimes\frac{B_n}{[P_n,P_n]}, $$ and, for $n\geq3$, that this quotient is a crystallographic group of dimension $n(n+1)/2$ with holonomy group $S_n$. We investigate its finite-order elements and conjugacy classes, prove that it has no elements of finite even order, and construct Bieberbach subgroups with prescribed finite $2$-group holonomy. Starting from suitable Bieberbach subgroups of $\frac{B_n}{[P_n,P_n]}$, we then construct Bieberbach subgroups of the framed quotient whose associated compact flat manifolds are torus bundles over the corresponding unframed flat manifolds. We describe these bundles through the generalized Calabi construction and determine their orientability, first Betti numbers, and the centers of their fundamental groups. As an application, we study a family with cyclic holonomy of odd order, obtaining a criterion for the existence of flat Kähler structures, and indicate how the same construction applies to cyclic holonomy of $2$-power order.
Miklós Dormán; Kamilla Kátai-Urbán; Eszter K. Horváth; Tamás Waldhauser

We study congruence lattices of finite algebras whose basic operations are unary and have exactly two values. We prove that the class of finite lattices representable in this way is closed under taking filters, glued sums and ordinal sums, and direct products with finite distributive lattices, but it is not closed under taking ideals or arbitrary direct products. A classification of lattices with at most seven elements with respect to representability is also presented.
Blind Random Search with Noisy Measurements: Almost Sure Convergence and Convergence Rates

Blind random search is a simple global optimization method that only requires the value of the loss function, without needing gradient information or an explicit loss model. However, its classical formulation assumes that the loss evaluation is noise-free, which limits its direct application to practical problems with noisy measurements. We extend blind random search by combining a vanishing acceptance threshold with the running average of noisy loss measurements. Under the stated assumptions, we prove that the proposed algorithm converges almost surely to the global minimizer. We further analyze the rate at which the loss at the current estimate approaches the minimum loss. For low-dimensional cases, we obtain an almost sure asymptotic upper bound on the difference between the two, and for high-dimensional cases, we prove that this difference, suitably scaled, has an exact Weibull limiting distribution.
On the evenness of coefficients of modular forms

We study the density of primes such that $a_p$ is divisible by a prime above $2$ for modular forms $f = \sum_{n \ge 1} a_n q^n$ of small levels. First, we reduce the problem to low weight and odd level, or a mod $2$ CM type form. Then, we provide calculations for the evenness of particular newforms. In particular, we provide a list of levels where this "evenness" can be computed exactly for all the forms with trivial nebentypus.
On the transformation of unbounded convergent sequences by linear operators on Banach lattices

In this paper, we introduce a weak variant of the concept of unbounded Dunford-Pettis linear operators, which we call unbounded weak Dunford-Pettis operators. We investigate the properties of this new class, establish inclusion and coincidence results involving unbounded Dunford-Pettis operators, and examine its relationship with the class of unbounded absolutely weakly continuous operators.
Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and homoclinic orbits

We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space $\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function $Q$ has bounded support in $\mathbb{Z}$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, where $n$ is the smallest natural number such that $Q(i)=0$ for every $i>n$. For $n=1$, results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of $N\mathbb{Z}$, where $N$ is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.
Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for noncommutative maximal truncated rough singular integrals

We prove a weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for maximal truncations of noncommutative rough singular integrals whose angular kernels satisfy the classical $L\log L$ integrability and cancellation conditions. The main ingredient of the proof is a new linearization method for handling the maximal truncations acting on the bad functions arising from the noncommutative Calderón--Zygmund decomposition.
Minimum orders of clique oddomorphism counterexamples

An oddomorphism to $K_n$ is a proper colouring with $n$ colours in which every vertex is designated odd or even, every vertex has in each other colour class a number of neighbours of its own parity, and every colour class contains an odd number of odd vertices. We prove that an oddomorphism witness to $K_n$ on at most $n+6$ vertices contains a $K_n$ minor with every branch meeting the witness's specified odd set. The conclusion holds inside any graph containing the witness and therefore applies to weak oddomorphisms. The bound is sharp: for every $n\ge8$ the minimum order of a graph admitting a weak oddomorphism to $K_n$ but having no $K_n$ minor is exactly $n+7$. The extremal example is a fifteen-vertex graph with an oddomorphism to $K_8$, obtained from the doubled theta graph of Kriesell and Mohr by adding one vertex adjacent to the seven roots; we give a structural proof that it has no $K_8$ minor, including their counting argument for the rooted case. A separate technical companion records further results on related root-apex graphs, an attachment theorem and a bounded nine-colour statement, together with their computational provenance; none of it is used here. The results do not resolve the unrestricted clique-target problem.
On the Upsilon invariant and the Baldwin-Vela-Vick b-invariant of fibered knots

For a null-homologous fibered knot $K$ in a rational homology sphere, Baldwin and Vela-Vick define a refinement $b(K)$ of the Ozsváth-Szabó contact invariant. We prove that if the Ozsváth-Stipsicz-Szabó concordance invariant Upsilon has slope $Υ'_K(t)=-g(K)$ for some $t\in[0,\frac{2}{n+1})$, where $g(K)$ is the genus of $K$, then $b(K)>n$. This extends a result of He, Hubbard, and the author on the Upsilon invariant and right-veering monodromies. We also prove that the knot Floer homology of a fibered knot in the $g(K)-b(K)$ Alexander grading is nonvanishing. As an application, we give many families of fibered cable knots whose $b(K)$ invariant grows arbitrarily large. Finally, we prove that if a monodromy of a fibered knot is neither right-veering nor left-veering, then the third-to-top term of knot Floer homology is nonvanishing.
Sharp Bounds on Continuous Treatment Effects under Unobserved Confounding

We study partial identification of conditional treatment effects with a continuous treatment under unobserved confounding. We target the conditional average potential outcome (CAPO) E[Y_x|z] and the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) between two treatment levels. We assume a bounded outcome and Lipschitz continuity of the response functions and of the propensity scores given the latent confounder, and show that these conditions imply the smooth treatment response and smooth treatment selection conditions of Kim et al. (2018). The combined bound of Kim et al. uses only two reference points on the identified diagonal and is generally loose. Bounding through every diagonal reference point instead gives explicit bounds whose average is the sharp identified set of the CAPO at every treatment, inside or outside the observational support. Capping the difference between the upper and lower bounds gives sharp causal bounds on the CATE. These bounds are informative without monotonicity or overlap assumptions.
Localized Hybrid Analytical-Finite-Element Thermal Modeling for Laser Powder Bed Fusion
Mohammad Amin Mohammadi Golafshani; Krishnan Suresh

Hybrid analytical--finite-element methods support scan-resolved, part-scale thermal simulation of laser powder bed fusion, but their analytical evaluation cost grows as scan-line contributions accumulate. This work develops a space--time localized hybrid formulation that restricts where and how long each contribution is evaluated analytically. Residual terms and boundary conditions derived from the heat equation allow the finite-element correction to account for the thermal effect of contributions removed from the analytical field. The formulation is assessed using a single-line benchmark against an independent full finite-element solution and multiline comparisons with the conventional hybrid formulation. Localization limits the number of analytical contributions retained while maintaining close agreement with the conventional solution. A comparison with uncompensated temporal truncation demonstrates the importance of the residual correction in retaining the thermal effect of removed contributions. In the 500-line case, analytical and total simulation times are reduced by factors of approximately 25.5 and 3.92, respectively, with a relative nodal 2-norm difference of 0.139%.
Hyperboloidal Initial Data with Prescribed Asymptotic Charges
Károly Csukás; János Östör; István Rácz

A novel method is introduced for constructing hyperboloidal initial data with direct analytic control over asymptotic charges prior to solving the Einstein constraint equations. Using the parabolic-hyperbolic formulation of the constraints together with a Fuchsian-analysis-inspired spectral solver, the asymptotic degrees of freedom, which determine infinite towers of asymptotic charges, including the Bondi energy and angular momentum, are used to prescribe the asymptotic behavior of solutions. As a proof of concept, we explicitly construct hyperboloidal initial data for a spinning black hole with Bondi energy $E_B = 2$ and angular momentum $J_B = 1/2$, starting from seed data induced on a hyperboloidal slice of the non-rotating Schwarzschild spacetime with mass $M=1$.
Not All Mislabels Are Equal: Efficient Task-Aware Auditing with Confidence Sequences
Fangyuan Lin; Noah Krever; Jakub Černý; Lily Xu

We study efficient, adaptive auditing of categorical labels in a fixed dataset, motivated by biodiversity-credit programs in which expert verification of species records is costly and downstream scores (e.g., payment) are more sensitive to errors on certain labels than on others. Our proposed ATLAS framework couples anytime-valid inference with a task-aware adaptive auditing policy. Representing label corrections through a confusion matrix, we prioritize which data points to inspect next based on both label uncertainty and the influence of potential label corrections on the downstream score function. For linear scores such as the mislabel rate, our priority-aware approach certifies the overall label error rate to $\pm 2$ percentage points with 24% and 11% fewer audits than random sampling on biodiversity data from Kenya and a widely used CIFAR-10N benchmark, respectively. For nonlinear scores such as the Hill-Shannon diversity, we exploit a linear-envelope representation that reduces inference to a family of linear-score audits; priority-aware sampling reaches the target precision with 36% fewer audits. When distribution-free guarantees are prohibitively costly, we develop a model-based Bayesian alternative that trades assumption-free validity for substantially fewer audits. Our biodiversity case study highlights a gap between statistical validity and practical feasibility: generic methods such as Serfling's bound and existing confidence-sequence procedures are rigorous but can require prohibitively many expert reviews in practice. Together, these results show task-aware auditing can significantly reduce the number of expert audits needed while providing finite-sample, anytime-valid guarantees.
Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces

We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces. A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a sphere other than the 4-sphere is regular. On even-dimensional spheres other than the 4-sphere we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics of non-constant curvature carrying Besse families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism.
Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin methods for the Keller-Segel model
Silvia Bertoluzza; Gabriella Bretti; Micol Pennacchio; Christophe Prud'homme

We propose a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) finite element method to approximate the solution of the time-dependent Keller-Segel model, a drift-diffusion system describing chemotactic cell movement. We develop and analyze the corresponding HDG scheme, and establish theoretical convergence results for the proposed discretization. Finally, we present numerical experiments that confirm the theoretical findings.
A non-equilibrium thermodynamics formulation of shear set-points in adaptively remodeling vascular networks

Blood vessels remodel in response to wall shear stress while the network operates under a metabolic maintenance budget. For a power-law maintenance cost, minimizing dissipation at fixed budget yields a local shear set-point, and a purely local adaptation rule drives the network towards this optimum. Here we give this result a non-equilibrium thermodynamic formulation. Blood flow is an exactly linear Onsager system, and the slow remodeling of vessel radii is a gradient flow generated by a Rayleigh dissipation functional. This identifies the structural mobility, which scales inversely with the maintenance cost of each vessel and can be measured from radius fluctuations. Enforcing the budget exactly requires a time-dependent metabolic multiplier, which we obtain in closed form; with a fixed multiplier the budget is violated by up to one third during transients. The fluid displaced by remodeling vessels couples flow and structure through a symmetric, non-diagonal mobility, so that Onsager reciprocity becomes a testable statement: neighbouring vessels should show anticorrelated radius fluctuations. With noise, the structural sector obeys a second law and an integral fluctuation theorem. Non-reciprocal signaling between vessels, such as upstream conducted responses, then breaks the time-reversal symmetry of radius fluctuations and produces housekeeping entropy, detectable from time series of realistic length. Finally, we construct a partition function over network topologies with the number of loops as order parameter. Numerical tests show that loop counts do not collapse onto a single curve against an effective temperature, and that they depend strongly on the detection threshold.
Two parametric $q$-supercongruences from Andrews' multi-series transformation

Recently, Guo and Guo (Results Math $76:37, ~2021$) obtained curious $q$-analogues of the following two supercongruences conjectured by Guo and Schlosser \cite[Conjectures $12.6$ and $12.7$]{GuoSclssr ConstApprox 21}: \begin{align*} \sum_{n=0}^{(p-1)/3} (6n+1) \frac{\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)_n^{4}(2n)!} {(n!)^{4}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)_{2n}} \equiv p \pmod{p^{3}} \qquad \text{for primes } p\equiv 1 \pmod{3}, \end{align*} \begin{align*} \sum_{n=0}^{(p+1)/3} (6n-1) \frac{\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)_n^{4}(2n)!} {(n!)^{4}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)_{2n}} \equiv p \pmod{p^{3}} \qquad \text{for primes } p\equiv 2 \pmod{3}, \end{align*} where $(z)_n=z(z+1)\cdots(z+n-1)$ denotes the shifted factorial. In this paper, we establish a one-parameter extension of them. The main ingredients of our proofs are the creative microscoping method developed by Guo and Zudilin \cite{guo2019q} and Andrews' multi-series transformation.
Subgraph Isomorphism, Integer Linear Programming, and Lattices: A Linear Algebraic Framework

The subgraph isomorphism problem (SGI) asks a deceptively simple question: is a graph B found inside a parent graph A? Famously NP-complete and the subject of volumes of study, attempts to practically solve subgraph problems typically require specialized software or the focused application of problem-specific theoretical knowledge. Here we present a straightforward linear framework that neatly joins SGI to lattice theory and constrained satisfiability and, importantly, yields an easily implemented algorithm that naturally leverages consumer-grade hardware and off-the-shelf libraries to compete with state-of-the-art specialized solvers. We additionally show practical realizations in approachable settings, along with some benchmarks that reduce 6+ hour computations to seconds. Aimed at readability, we develop a series of computable algebraic invariants and demonstrate their application to familiar problems such as the Knight's Tour, with a focus on providing an accessible entry point for researchers in graph theory, abstract algebra, and students in general.
Partial Airy ideals and coloured blobbed topological recursion
Gaëtan Borot; Vincent Bouchard; Swagata S. Datta

We define and study the notion of partial Airy ideals, which are certain linear systems of PDEs that may contain less equations than variables. We show that they admit a unique solution of exponential type (the partition function) modulo a choice of initial condition. We construct a large class of examples of partial Airy ideals attached to spectral curves using twisted free-field representations of $\mathcal{W}(\mathfrak{gl}_r)$-algebras at self-dual level. This generalizes the results of Bouchard- Borot-Chidambaram-Creutzig-Noshchenko by significantly enlarging the set of admissible spectral curves, provided they come with additional data that we call colour. We show that the differential constraints on the partition function are equivalent to a set of equations on the associated correlators, which we call coloured loop equations. We find a recursive residue formulation for the solutions of those equations, the coloured blobbed topological recursion}, which is a generalization of the currently known forms of topological recursion. It includes the blobbed topological recursion of Borot-Shadrin as a special case, giving it a natural interpretation within the formalism of partial Airy ideals.
On the stability of rank-one factors for Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions

We prove $C^1$-stability of $C^\infty$ rank-one factors for a large class of higher rank Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions. If the factor is a projection of a smooth fiber bundle and the action contains an element which acts as the identity on the rank-one factor and is Anosov on every fiber, then any sufficiently $C^1$-small $C^\infty$ perturbation of the action will also have a $C^\infty$ rank-one factor. In particular, we prove the $C^1$-stability of the product structure for Anosov $\mathbb Z^2$-actions which are obtained as a (diagonal) product of two $\mathbb Z$-Anosov actions.
Some remarks on polynomial vector fields in $\RR^2$

In this paper, we study planar polynomial vector fields admitting invariant circles. We characterize polynomial vector fields having $m$ concentric invariant circles, and we describe those having three invariant circles whose centers are not collinear. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for the unit circle to be the unique limit cycle of a quadratic vector field. We prove that a cubic or quartic Kolmogorov vector field having the unit circle invariant has no circular limit cycle, and that a quartic vector field with two concentric circular limit cycles has at most three circular limit cycles, this bound being sharp.
Ground-state spaces of generalized stabilizer codes
Cathy Cheng; Nigel Higson; Danilo Polo Ojito; Emil Prodan

In this paper, we determine the complete ground-state spaces for a broad class of generalized stabilizer quantum models defined over CW-decompositions of non-compact manifolds of arbitrary dimensions and topological type. We introduce a $C^*$-algebraic framework in which the quantum spin algebra $\A$ is realized as the twisted group $C^*$-algebra of an infinite discrete Pauli module $P$ endowed with a symplectic structure. We establish a correspondence between stabilizer models and isotropic subgroups of $P$: Every Lagrangian extension of such a subgroup determines a $C^*$-diagonal of $\A$, whose Weyl groupoid encodes the dynamics through a continuous 1-cocycle. This realization yields an explicit family of extremal ground-states for every admissible Lagrangian model, together with their decomposition into sectors. When the sector space is $T_0$, this gives a complete characterization of the ground-state spaces. We also prove that every Lagrangian stabilizer model admits a unique frustration-free ground state with a spectral gap. Our framework applies in arbitrary dimension, including higher abelian quantum doubles, homological codes, and a broad class of stabilizer models.
Explicit strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs using a new graph parameter

A strong blocking set is a set of points in a finite projective space that intersects every hyperplane of the space in a spanning set of the hyperplane. These objects have been studied both in finite geometry and coding theory due to their equivalence with minimal codes. We give an explicit construction of strong blocking sets using expander graphs that improves the explicit construction of Alon et al. (Noga Alon, Anurag Bishnoi, Shagnik Das, Alessandro Neri, Strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs. Transactions of the American Mathematical Society ) by introducing a new geometrically motivated graph parameter that is better suited for this problem. Using this approach, we improve the constant $C$ in the explicit construction of a strong blocking set of size $C (q+1) k$ in the $(k - 1)$-dimensional projective space over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q \geq 7$.
Maximizing Measures for Subadditive and Almost-Additive Potentials on Countable-Alphabet Subshifts

We prove the existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive families of upper semicontinuous, bounded-above potentials $\mathcal F=\{f_n\}_{n\geq1}$ on closed subshifts over countable alphabets. Under a coercivity condition on $f_1$, we prove that every maximizing sequence, that is, $\{μ_k\}_{k\geq1}\subset\mathcal M_σ(X)$ satisfying $\bar{\mathcal F}(μ_k)\toβ(\mathcal F)$, is uniformly tight, preventing mass from escaping to arbitrarily large symbols. As a consequence, a maximizing measure exists.
Absorption probabilities of random walks without symmetry or general position

Let $S_1,S_2,\dots$ be a random walk in $\mathbb R^d$ with independent identically distributed increments. We show that, for every distribution of the increments and for every $n\ge1$, \[ \mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S_1,\dots,S_n)\bigr] = \sum_{m=1}^n\frac1{m!}\sum_{\substack{k_1,\dots,k_m\ge1\\ k_1+\dots+k_m=n}}\frac{1}{k_1\cdots k_m}\,\mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S^{(1)}_{k_1},\dots,S^{(m)}_{k_m})\bigr], \] where $S^{(1)},S^{(2)},\dots$ are independent copies of the walk. No symmetry, general position or moment assumptions are needed. The result rests on a deterministic identity: for arbitrary vectors $x_1,\dots,x_n$, the number of orderings for which the convex hull of the partial sums avoids the origin equals the number of permutations for which the convex hull of the cycle sums avoids it. We derive it from a permutation-averaging identity for valuations obtained in our earlier work. Consequences include the identities of Sparre Andersen and Spitzer, the distribution-free absorption probabilities of Kabluchko, Vysotsky and Zaporozhets, their generating function found by Petrov, Randon-Furling and Zaporozhets, and a formula for the probability that the origin is never absorbed.
$L^\infty$ blow-up in the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation

We investigate the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation \bee u_{tttt}+\al u_{ttt}+\bet u_{tt}-γ\Del u_{tt}-\del \Del u_{t}-\varrho \Del u=(f(u))_{ttt}+(f(u))_{tt} \eee under homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions in a smooth bounded domain $\Om \subset \R^n$ with $n\leq 3$, where $\al \in \R$ and $\bet,γ,\del,\varrho>0$. First, for any suitably regular initial data and assuming that $f\in C^4(\R)$ with $f(0)=0$, we prove that the corresponding initial-boundary value problem admits a unique maximal strong solution $u$ on $(0, \tm)$. Second, by combining three time-integrated formulations with a series of resolvent-regularized energy estimates, we show that gradient blow-up is ruled out in the sense that \be{EE} \tm<\infty \quad\,\, \Rightarrow\quad\,\, \limsup_{t\nearrow \tm}\|u(\cd,t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\Om)}=\infty. \tag{$\star$} \ee Finally, assuming in addition that $f$ is convex and grows superlinearly in the sense that \bee f''(ξ)\geq 0 \;\; \mbox{ for all}\;\;ξ\in\R, \qquad \frac{f(ξ)}ξ\rightarrow +\infty\;\;\mbox{ as}\;\; ξ\rightarrow +\infty , \qquad \int_{ξ_{0}}^{\infty}\frac{dξ}{f(ξ)}<\infty \;\; \mbox{ for some}\;\; ξ_{0}>0, \eee we employ the extensibility criterion (\ref{EE}) to prove that, for a suitable class of initial data, the solution blows up in finite time in the $L^\infty$-norm. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first rigorous description of finite-time blow-up for a genuinely nonlinear equation of fourth order in time.
Dynamics of two-dimensional Bose gases in the focusing case

We prove the propagation of Bose--Einstein condensation and a norm approximation for the dynamics of a Bose gas with localized initial data in two dimensions with singular interactions that may have a small attractive part. We allow the scaling of the interaction to be any polynomial scaling $N^β$ for $0<β<\infty$ and even exponential scaling $e^{N^κ}$ for $0<κ<1/4$. Our approach covers external potentials that are time-dependent, at most quadratic, and bounded below, including the situation without an external potential.
Derivative-Informed Dimension Reduction of Stochastic Differential Equations: A Path-Space Sensitivity Approach
Joanna Zou; Han Cheng Lie; Youssef Marzouk

Uncertainty in the drift of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) induces uncertainty in statistical observables defined as expected functionals on path space. We propose a derivative-informed method for identifying low-dimensional structure in the drift-to-observable map, with the aim of improving the tractability of uncertainty quantification. This approach can be viewed as a generalization of the active subspace method to infinite-dimensional input spaces and to path-space observables of SDEs. Representing uncertainty in the drift by random perturbations in a Hilbert space, we construct a path-space sensitivity operator using first-order Fréchet derivatives of the observable with respect to the perturbation. We establish conditions under which the leading eigenfunctions of this operator correspond to directions of maximum mean squared sensitivity of the observable, thus enabling low-dimensional approximation with certified error bounds. We further introduce a martingale control variate of the Fréchet derivative that reduces error in sample-based estimators of the operator. Using a Galerkin scheme for numerical discretization, we show that reduced representations of the drift from the derivative-informed basis yield more accurate approximations of mean first hitting times of SDEs than the Karhunen-Loève expansion of the same truncation order.
A New Non-Affine Family in the Karlsson-Szollosi Intersection

We show that $K_6^{(2)} \cap X_6^{(2)} = D_6^{(1)} \cup C_6^{(1)}$ up to standard Hadamard equivalence, where $C_6^{(1)}$ is a new non-affine one-parameter family of complex Hadamard matrices. This demonstrates that the intersection of the two-parameter Hadamard families of Karlsson and Szöllősi is strictly larger than the known affine Diţă curve $D_6^{(1)}$. Our new parametrisation of the Szöllősi family $X_6^{(2)}$ in Karlsson coordinates and our constructive classification of the Karlsson-Szöllősi intersection shed light on the intersection of block-reducible forms and hypocycloid constraints. This may support the search for mutually unbiased bases in six dimensions.
Cutoff profile for the coupon collector with many collections

We solve the problem posed by Erdős and Rényi in $1961$ about the limiting distribution of the number of draws $T_{n,m}$ that a coupon collector needs to complete $m$ collections of $n$ distinct types of coupons, when $m$ increases with $n$. For fixed $m$, Erdős and Rényi proved that $\mathbb P(T_{n,m}\leq n\log n+(m-1)n\log\log n-n\log (m-1)!+θn)$ converges to $ \mathcal G(θ)$, for every $θ\in \mathbb R$, as $n \to \infty$, where $\mathcal G$ is the standard Gumbel distribution function, and they asked what happens when $m=m(n)$ increases with $n$. We give a complete answer to this question. More precisely, for every increasing sequence $m=m(n)$, we determine explicit sequences $t_{n,m}$ and $w_{n,m}$ satisfying $w_{n,m}/t_{n,m}\to0$ such that $\mathbb P(T_{n,m}\leq t_{n,m}+θw_{n,m})\to\mathcal G(θ)$ for every $θ\in\mathbb R$. We also determine the corresponding asymptotic behavior of $\mathbb E[T_{n,m}]$. To prove these results, we present a methodology, inspired by Poissonization, that can be applied to determine the asymptotic behaviors of standardized hitting times of discrete-time stochastic processes.
Extensions of a family of Linear Cycle Sets whose underlying group is a product of two cyclic groups
Jorge Guccione; Juan José Guccione; Christian Valqui
We use the linear cycle set cohomology in order to compute extensions of a non trivial linear cycle sets whose underlying additive group is a product of two cyclic groups.
Shengyang Zang; Yingyu Zhao; Yunhao Zhao; Chen Zhou

We prove that four cosines with distinct positive integer frequencies have the same sign on at least $1/33$ of a period, with equality precisely for positive integer dilates of $\{1,3,11,33\}$. If both odd and even frequencies occur, the optimal proportion is $1/24$; equality holds precisely for odd positive integer dilates of $\{1,3,4,12\}$ and $\{2,4,5,15\}$. For arbitrary $n$, we establish the universal lower bound $4^{1-n}$ and construct frequency sets for which this proportion is at most $16n^\theta4^{-n}$, where $θ=\log_2(3/2)$. These bounds determine the optimal exponential decay rate $1/4$.

Motivated by Teleman's study of gauged topological quantum field theories, our main result is an analog of Elmendorf's theorem in the setting of simplicial group actions on $\infty$-categories. In particular, we prove that if $G$ is a simplicial group, there is a Quillen equivalence between the homotopy category of $\infty$-categories with $G$-action and the homotopy category of $\infty$-category-valued presheaves on the orbit category of $G$. We also show an analog of Whitehead's theorem in this setting.
Kernelised covariance matrices, dimension reduction and imbalanced spectral clustering
Xiaoyu Dong; Subhro Ghosh; Soumendu Sundar Mukherjee; Himasish Talukdar

The Gaussian Mixture Model (abbrv. GMM) is a classic generative model for clustered data, for which spectral clustering based on dimension reduction via PCA has been an effective framework. In this work, we investigate kernelised covariance matrices as an alternative mechanism for dimension reduction and spectral clustering, focusing on truncation kernels that select pairs of data points with suitable separation constraints. The structure of these matrices is motivated by considerations from statistical mechanics of repulsive particle systems. Our approach is particularly relevant for the setting of imbalanced clusters, where the sizes of the largest and smallest clusters have a diverging ratio with the problem size, and existing PCA-based methods turn out to be of limited effectiveness. We demonstrate efficient dimension reduction and clustering performance of these modified covariance matrices, substantiated by quantitative bounds. In particular, they achieve superior dimension reduction guarantees compared to PCA for a wide range of parameters in the regime of imbalanced clusters. For spectral clustering, our approach exhibits improvements over PCA in the imbalanced setting, in particular guaranteeing accurate clustering in a much larger regime of intra-cluster separations. Our theoretical guarantees reflected in a range of simulation experiments that exhibit these improvements for unbalanced clustering problems. Our analytical approach, based on kernel Laplacians, provide a toolbox as well as a relevant conceptual ingredient for clustering problems at large. We believe that our work will motivate the application of such kernelised covariance matrices for related classes of statistical problems, as well as spur new investigations in the theory of random matrices.
A Gaussian Process State Space Formulation for Materials Constitutive Modeling: Application to Quasi-brittle Materials
Houlin Xu; Chenyang Li; K. T. Ramesh; Michael D. Shields

Constitutive models for history-dependent, path-dependent materials typically encode this dependence in prescribed functional forms through internal variables such as damage or plastic strain that are phenomenological, model-dependent, and not directly observable. These rigid forms lack flexibility to match observations, make calibration potentially non-unique, and complicate uncertainty quantification. This paper develops a Gaussian-process state-space model (GP-SSM) that replaces the fixed form of the constitutive model with a flexible GP regression, and the prescribed internal variables with latent state variables learned directly from observable stress-strain histories. As a GP, the model is naturally endowed with a measure of uncertainty and can be constrained to satisfy physical principles. We demonstrate this framework for quasi-brittle materials under triaxial compression, where the latent variable evolution is driven by the current-state stress invariants and the increment of equivalent strain to reflect irreversible, pressure-sensitive history. A sparse multi-output GP then maps the latent state and current strain tensor to the six-component stress response, trained by variational sparse inference. The trained model is exported into Abaqus/Explicit through a user material subroutine. Four verification cases are reported: (1) offline rollout on validation and test histories; (2) a single element under changing confinement; (3) a frozen-memory unloading-reloading extension; and (4) a multi-element structural model compared against the Karagozian and Case Concrete (KCC) model. These results show that the learned state-space update reproduces held-out RVE-scale histories in closed-loop rollout, tracks evolving confinement, supports unloading without violating the irreversibility of the learned history state, and reproduces structural-level behavior consistent with KCC.
Variational relaxation and gradient flows for degenerate elliptic conductivity problems
Jan Haskovec; Peter Markowich; Stefano Zampini

We develop a convex-analytic $L^2$-framework for gradient flows of pumping-energy functionals coupled with elliptic state equations and an evolving nonnegative conductivity $a\geq 0$. The main difficulty is that the conductivity may be merely square-integrable, or degenerate, and formal differentiation need not produce an $L^2$-subgradient. After imposing the strictly positive lower cutoff $r+a\geq r>0$, we define the pumping-energy functional by a variational formula, prove convexity and lower semicontinuity, and show that its $L^2$-subdifferential is nonempty if and only if the pressure gradient belongs to $L^4$. We also obtain a unique maximal-monotone $L^2$-gradient flow satisfying an energy identity. Moreover, we prove Mosco convergence of the pumping-energy functionals as the cutoff vanishes. An inverse-moment conductivity constraint provides a weak alternative to a uniform positive lower bound. For nonlinear laws $a=μ(b)$, primal and flux representations distinguish two complementary regimes. If $μ$ is concave, the pumping-energy functional remains convex, and we characterize its $L^2$-subdifferential and the induced gradient flow. If $1/μ$ is concave, the pumping-energy functional is concave, and therefore its negative is convex. We construct its pointwise gradient flow on a uniformly elliptic box. Admissible stationary points for power laws yield $p$-Laplacian equations with $p>2$ and $1 < p < 2$, respectively.
Flocking with finite communication speed: a Doppler-inspired Lyapunov approach

We study the Cucker--Smale model with state-dependent transmission delays arising from finite-speed information propagation. Our main contribution is a Lyapunov functional inspired by the Doppler effect, combining a delay potential with a logarithmic correction involving the receiver velocity. Its dissipation yields uniform delay bounds without relying on velocity contraction estimates. For two agents in one spatial dimension, we prove asymptotic flocking for arbitrary compatible subluminal initial histories, assuming only that the influence function has a divergent integral at infinity. A bounded geometric correction extends this result to arbitrary spatial dimension when all values of the initial velocity histories lie on one common affine line. For multiple agents in one dimension, we obtain uniform delay bounds, and thus flocking, provided that a fixed agent is leftmost for all sufficiently large times. In all these flocking regimes, the spatial diameter remains uniformly bounded and the velocity diameter decays exponentially. We also derive a conditional criterion involving logarithmic sums when the leftmost agent changes infinitely often. Finally, we construct a multidimensional analogue of the Doppler-inspired functional and identify an additional assumption needed to obtain delay bounds in the general case.
Construction of holomorphic SCFTs with minimal index

It has been an open question whether there exist holomorphic VOAs with N=1 supersymmetry and Witten index 1 for any positive central charge c. The existence of such a theory with c=288 is closely related to the 576-periodicity of the TMF spectrum via the Segal-Stolz-Teichner conjecture. Here we report the construction of thousands of such theories by extending the approach initiated by Gaiotto and Johnson-Freyd via ternary codes. In addition, for every positive integer k, we also construct holomorphic N=1 VOAs of central charge c=12k with index 24/gcd(24,k) -- conjectured to be the minimum -- in a computer-aided search carried out by AI coding agents. We overcome the exponential-time barrier by using chains of smaller cells to build ternary codes, whose indices can then be evaluated via a transfer-matrix technique, and we use a symmetric orbifold construction to reduce the problem of k=12 and 24 to that of k=6. Along the way, we also establish several results on ternary codes and their indices. Using an observation relating codes and Landau-Ginzburg orbifold models, we argue that the non-chiral doubles of the ternary code VOAs can always be gapped supersymmetrically.
One ring to rule them all: syzygy maximization for Argyres-Douglas
Monica Jinwoo Kang; Craig Lawrie; Jaewon Song

We propose a uniform construction of affine schemes encoding the Higgs branches and Macdonald indices of the Argyres--Douglas theories $\mathcal{D}_p(ADE)$, with $\gcd(p,h^\vee)=1$. The construction captures conjectural OPE decoupling relations via the Jacobian ring of a single invariant polynomial potential, obtained from a polynomial twisted period of the corresponding Coxeter orbit space. We show that these potentials are ``syzygy-maximizing'' in the first jet schemes and recover the Higgs branches as their reduced critical loci. We obtain closed determinant expressions for the classical types and explicit potentials for $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$. Powers of the nilradical define an intrinsic filtration on the resulting Jacobian rings, from which we compute candidate Macdonald indices with the correct Schur and Hall--Littlewood limits, in the examples studied. Restricting the potentials to Slodowy slices extends the prescription to nilpotently Higgsed theories. We further conjecture that these Jacobian rings are isomorphic to Zhu's $C_2$-algebras of simple affine VOAs at boundary admissible levels and their quantum Drinfeld--Sokolov reductions.
A Stationary Mean-Field Model for Carbon Market Stability Reserve
René Aïd; Federico Cannerozzi; Giorgio Ferrari

We formulate the design of a market stability reserve as a stationary mean-field singular control problem. The allowance balance follows a regime-switching diffusion, while the regulator injects or withdraws allowances through bounded-variation controls. The objective trades off the average allowance balance, its stationary dispersion, deviations from a long-run target, and intervention costs. The optimal policy is a regime-dependent band rule characterized by four reflecting thresholds. Its computation reduces to a scalar fixed-point problem combining a coupled variational inequality with the invariant distribution of the reflected process. A calibration to the EU ETS yields thresholds of the same order of magnitude as the existing Market Stability Reserve rule. Comparative statics show that volatility is the main determinant of the intervention band, whereas the frequency and duration of crisis regimes have limited effects. A simpler two-threshold policy based on average regime dynamics closely reproduces the optimal regime-dependent policy in terms of liquidity and intervention volumes.
Jan Kristian Haugland; Nadia S. Larsen; Tron Omland; Henrikke G. Rustad

We give a new checkable criterion to ensure that a one-dimensional cellular automaton on a finite alphabet is locally eventually onto. In this setting, openness is equivalent to being n-to-1 for some n and therefore implies surjectivity. Bipermutive cellular automata are known to be locally eventually onto, while open cellular automata that are neither bipermutive nor bijective appear to have received less attention. Building on Sutner's work with de Bruijn graphs, we describe a method for deciding openness and at the same time determining n. We then introduce the notion of block-regularity of local rules as a generalization of bipermutivity and prove that it implies openness. We further identify two conditions that, together with block-regularity, ensure that every nonempty cylinder set is mapped onto the whole configuration space after a finite number of iterations, and hence that the cellular automaton is locally eventually onto. The appendix provides the algorithms that check these finite criteria and then presents examples of locally eventually onto, non-bipermutive cellular automata for small diameters.
A new family of deformed trigonometric functions and their corresponding Pythagorean-like relations: application to the nonlinear harmonic oscillator
P. R. Gordoa; A. Pickering; D. Puertas-Centeno; E. V. Toranzo

In this work we present an extension of the classical trigonometric functions which include, amongst others, the Lindqvist p-trigonometric functions. Additionally, we show their relevance in the study of certain versions of the nonlinear harmonic oscillator equation. Furthermore, we study their more important mathematical properties and obtain their corresponding Pythagorean-like relations. We also define a new extension of the Beta and Ateb sine functions using these new $χ$-trigonometric functions. Indeed, these new Beta and Ateb functions are involved in the closed form expressions obtained for the solutions of the nonlinear oscillator under certain constraints.
Spatial symmetry invariance of three-dimensional Navier-Stokes turbulence

Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) of the deterministic Navier-Stokes (NS) equations is widely used to provide benchmark solutions of turbulent flow, but its accuracy and reliability have not been rigorously inspected from a mathematical viewpoint. Here we prove a spatial symmetry invariance theorem (SSIT) of three-dimensional NS equations whereby an exact solution of deterministic NS equations under periodic boundary conditions maintains the same spatial symmetry as its symmetric initial flow, forever. SSIT provides an absolute benchmark test for computational fluid dynamics (CFD). It is shown herein that traditional DNS of NS turbulence quickly violates SSIT, revealing that the spatiotemporal trajectory of NS turbulence predicted by DNS soon becomes badly polluted by numerical noise. Importantly, it is found that even the statistical results of DNS might be unstable, i.e., exhibit sensitivity dependence on the initial flow conditions. In other words, the loss of spatial symmetry in traditional DNS of NS turbulence is not a physical instability but instead a numerical artifact caused by the chaotic nature of the flow. Using the SSIT, it is straightforward to deduce several key properties of NS turbulence, including `ultra-chaos', the so-called `noise-expansion cascade', `permanent memory of symmetric initial flow conditions', and so on. Note that permanent memory of symmetric initial flow conditions suggests that NS turbulence governed by deterministic NS equations subject to symmetric initial flow should have no `mixing', corresponding to non-ergodicity, although ergodicity is one of the most fundamental assumptions of turbulence theory.
Some new criteria for the uniqueness of limit cycles in Rayleigh--Lienard systems
Hebai Chen; Dongmei Xiao; Rui Zhang

In this paper, new uniqueness criteria for Rayleigh--Liénard systems with damping of positive odd degree in the velocity are established. Under suitable conditions, any limit cycle is unique and hyperbolic, with its stability determined by the damping signs. Neither symmetry nor monotonicity of the damping and restoring functions is required. Changes of variables and time yield further criteria for generalized Kukles systems. Applications to three polynomial families yield uniqueness and nonexistence results. In particular, we resolve an open uniqueness problem for a hybrid van der Pol--Rayleigh oscillator left open by Chen et al. (Phys. D, 2021). We also give an alternative uniqueness proof for a system with homogeneous components and obtain uniqueness and nonexistence results for a modified hybrid van der Pol--Rayleigh oscillator.
Foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic

This paper studies foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic. We provide an explicit description of all smooth foliations, linear and turbulent, and establish criteria for being $p$-closed. We explicitly determine the moduli spaces of such foliations. We give an application to the construction of $p$-closed foliations, with mild singularities, on Kummer $K3$-surfaces in positive characteristics.
Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
François Gay-Balmaz; Tudor S. Ratiu; Cesare Tronci

While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defect and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincaré variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects. While the latter allows us to overcome certain ambiguities in definition of the defect density, the Euler-Poincaré method provides a unified modeling approach in the absence of defect reconnection.
On the continuity of conditional distributions and stratification for derivative pricing

Stratification can reduce the estimator variance in Monte Carlo simulations by partitioning the sample space according to a low-dimensional factor and sampling separately within the resulting strata, making it well suited to the valuation of path-dependent claims in high-dimensional financial models. Its performance, however, depends critically on the choice of the stratification factor, and effective low-dimensional factors are generally difficult to identify in complex continuous-time models. Neural networks provide a flexible approximation class for this purpose and have proved useful in related variance-reduction problems in quantitative finance. In this paper, we study the construction of neural stratification factors for derivative pricing under proportional allocation in continuous-time models. Since the numerical construction of a stratification factor typically involves approximation, we establish continuity results for the associated conditional expectations and, more generally, conditional distributions, and provide several counterexamples showing the limits of this continuity theory. Combined with density results for neural networks, our findings yield a universal approximation theorem for admissible stratification factors. We conclude with numerical experiments involving a constant-maturity-swap range accrual in a two-factor Gaussian short-rate model and a worst-of autocallable in a Wishart stochastic covariance model, where the learned factors outperform all considered benchmarks.
Acyclic 2-edge-coloured graphs: polynomial-time linkages and colouring hardness
Jørgen Bang-Jensen; Stéphane Bessy; Amadeus Reinald

A path or cycle in a $2$-edge-coloured graph is alternating if consecutive edges have different colours. These objects are natural analogues of paths and cycles in graphs, and even more so in digraphs. A well-studied class is that of acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs, that is, those forbidding alternating cycles. In particular, (acyclic) $2$-edge-coloured graphs generalize directed (acyclic) graphs (DAGs), but the complexity of problems on DAGs is much better understood than that of the corresponding problems on acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs. We investigate the complexity of two such problems, whose directed counterparts are well-known. Our first result is an $n^{O(k)}$-time algorithm for the alternating $k$-linkage problem on acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs. This problem asks for $k$ vertex-disjoint alternating paths joining $k$ prescribed pairs of vertices. This generalizes the directed $k$-linkage algorithm for DAGs. For every fixed $k$, this also yields a polynomial-time algorithm for finding $k$ internally vertex-disjoint alternating $(s,t)$-paths, solving an open problem by Abouelaoualim et al. from 2008. We then consider the alternating chromatic number of $2$-edge-coloured graphs, defined as the minimum number of parts in a vertex partition such that each part induces an acyclic subgraph. This notion is analogous to the dichromatic number of digraphs, where it is known that deciding dichromatic number $2$ is NP-complete even on tournaments. Our second result is that deciding alternating chromatic number $2$ is NP-complete on complete $2$-edge-coloured graphs. Equivalently, deciding whether a graph can be partitioned into two induced threshold graphs is NP-complete.
The Verra involution on special cubic fourfolds
Augustinas Jacovskis; Reinder Meinsma; Riccardo Moschetti

We present a detailed study of the Hodge theory, geometry and derived categories of Verra fourfolds, and their relationship with twisted K3 surfaces and cubic fourfolds. We classify Brauer classes of Verra type on K3 surfaces of degree 2, and use this to derive an explicit counting formula for Fourier--Mukai partners of a large class of Verra fourfolds. We develop the basic theory of cohomology of Verra fourfolds and apply it to prove a derived Torelli theorem for a large class of Verra fourfolds. As an application, we prove that L-equivalent Verra fourfolds in this class are Fourier--Mukai partners, and conjecture that this implication holds for all Verra fourfolds. We then give a construction of cubic fourfolds birational to Verra fourfolds. The construction yields examples of cubic and Verra fourfolds whose associated twisted K3 surfaces have non-trivial Brauer classes. Therefore, these fourfolds are expected to be irrational.
A Central Limit Theorem for the Driver Site Frequency Spectrum
Armaan Ahmed; Jasmine Foo; Kevin Leder

We consider a supercritical two-type continuous-time linear birth-death process with mutation and selection, in which wild-type individuals give rise to mutant offspring with a larger net-growth rate. We previously had obtained first-order law of large number results for the driver site frequency spectrum. We return to obtain a second-order central limit theorem, in which we show stable convergence of a scaling of the deviation of the SFS from its first-order limit. We provide a central limit theorem at both large detection times and sizes. Then, we apply these results to obtain confidence intervals for a class of consistent estimators for the fitness advance.
Modified scattering for the 3D Hartree equation with singular external potentials

We establish modified scattering for the three-dimensional Hartree equation with Coulomb interaction and singular external potentials, including repulsive Coulomb and inverse-square potentials. In the defocusing case, the result holds for arbitrary initial data in $H^{0,1}(\mathbb R^3)\cap H^{1,0}(\mathbb R^3)$. In particular, we obtain large-data modified scattering for the flat defocusing Hartree equation. For the focusing problem with repulsive Coulomb potential $V(x)=κ|x|^{-1}$, we prove radial modified scattering under the sharp mass condition $|λ|\|u_0\|_2^2\leq 2κ$, including the endpoint, and construct standing waves at every larger mass. Our argument obtains strong $L^2$ convergence from rescaled energy and comparison with a frozen-field evolution.
Rational Points on Affine Varieties over Finite Fields and Polygonal Number Sequences
Sakshi Gupta; Anit Kuckian; Indranath Sengupta

Authors, in an earlier work, proved that prime power subsequences of the polygonal numbers corresponding to $4$, $6$, $8$, and $10$ arise naturally as the numbers of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points of certain double Danielewski surfaces. In this work, authors generalize the previous construction and give a new family of affine varieties over finite fields such that the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points of these varieties give the prime power subsequence of every polygonal number sequence.
Vertex operator algebra realizations of untwisted Haagerup--Izumi centers

Probabilistic ultraviolet renormalization of the two-dimensional Sine-Gordon model
Benjamin Bonnefont; Hermanni Rajamäki; Vincent Vargas

We give a probabilistic approach to the ultraviolet renormalization of the two-dimensional Sine-Gordon model. The model is formally described by the density $\exp(α\int \mathopen{:} \cos(βX) \mathclose{:} )$, where $X$ is a log-correlated Gaussian field. Our construction applies on bounded convex domains for every particle activity $α\in\mathbb R$ and throughout the subcritical range $β^2\in[0,4)$, below the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless threshold. We apply the martingale method introduced by Lacoin, Rhodes and Vargas to two dimensions by using refined estimates based on charge conjugation symmetries. A direct proof of the equivalence of the A2 and the Helson--Szego conditions
Christos Grigoriadis; Michail Paparizos; Georgios Psaromiligkos

We give a direct proof of the equivalence between the Muckenhoupt $\mathcal{A}_2$ and the Helson--Szegő conditions on the unit circle $T$. The classical proof combines the Helson--Szegő theorem with the Hunt--Muckenhoupt--Wheeden characterization of weighted boundedness of the Hilbert transform. Hot Spots: From Smooth to Nonsmooth Simply Connected Planar Domains

Assuming the absence of interior local extrema for first positive Neumann eigenfunctions on bounded smooth simply connected planar domains, as reported in \cite{SmoothInput}, we extend the hot spots conclusion to simply connected domains of finite area with compact Sobolev embedding and simple first positive Neumann eigenvalue. The supremum and infimum are approached in arbitrarily thin boundary layers. For bounded domains and eigenfunctions continuous up to the boundary, both extrema are attained on the boundary. We also transfer polynomial Neumann heat-kernel bounds uniformly along a conformal exhaustion and construct explicit bounded and unbounded examples, including domains with cusps and a domain with infinitely many corners and bottlenecks. Some of these examples admit no polynomial Neumann heat-kernel bound.
Stationary bistable fronts on a periodic necklace graph: existence, stability and multiplicity
Yoichiro Mori; Toshiyuki Ogawa; Chanoknun Sintavanuruk

We study stationary fronts for a bistable reaction-diffusion equation with the McKean reaction on a periodic necklace metric graph. For profiles that agree on each pair of parallel edges, the problem reduces to a scalar equation on the real line with a periodic, piecewise constant diffusion coefficient. The diffusion contrast of the necklace is not small, so the coefficient cannot be treated as a small perturbation of a constant. Because the McKean reaction is piecewise linear, the equation is affine between threshold crossings and coefficient interfaces, and a front is determined explicitly by its crossing points. For each fixed interior threshold, one decreasing front is Lyapunov stable and the other is unstable in the $W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R})$ norm, among mild solutions with one continuously moving threshold crossing. There are then exactly $2^m$ fronts with one threshold crossing in each chosen period and none elsewhere. Varying the chosen periods gives infinitely many inequivalent fronts with $m$ crossings.

A Higgs bundle on a smooth complex projective variety is curve semistable if its pullback to every smooth projective curve is semistable. A 2008 conjecture asserts that this is equivalent to slope semistability for some polarization plus vanishing discriminant. One direction is known, the converse holds in rank two, and Huang recently gave a rank-four counterexample. We prove the conjecture for rank three nilpotent Higgs bundles in any dimension. Variance of relative entropy over random states

Average relative entropy over major generic random states is recently studied. In this work, the investigation is extended by deriving the variances of relative entropy over the Hilbert--Schmidt and Bures--Hall ensembles, which characterize its fluctuations around the average value. Exact results for the variances of relative entropy between independent states drawn from the same ensemble and from two different ensembles are obtained. These results further indicate that the average relative entropy is typical in the considered limiting regimes. In addition to the matrix-level calculations similar to the average relative entropy, eigenvalue correlation functions of the ensembles are involved in the variance computations through the use of zonal polynomials.
Polyhedral RIS Architecture with Quantum-Assisted Facet Selection for Uniform Coverage

Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) direct coverage toward moving user equipment (UE), but practical deployments involve discrete phase control, uncertain facet positions, and UE mobility, which require the problem to be re-solved continually. For a precoded multi-user downlink, each facet-selection subproblem of the max-min rate design is shown to be an exact quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem, suited to repeated time-constrained solving. The deployment of the base station in relation to the RIS allows the polyhedral surface to bring down the percentage of dead zones in vertical planar panels from 77% to 0.3% and increase the minimum rate by 34% relative to the STAR panel.
