This density is equal to $(|a_1|+|a_2|)^p$ on rank-one matrices $a\otimesν$, $|ν|=1$, and exceeds its convex envelope by a quantity comparable to $|\det A|\,|A|^{p-2}$, with constants of order $(2-p)^{-1}$. Consequently, although the original energy density is convex, the limit density is quasiconvex but neither convex nor polyconvex: quasiconvexity is generated by the geometry of the constraint. For $p\ge2$ the constraint survives in the limit as $\det
abla u=0$, and the $Γ$-limit is the degenerate energy $\int_Ω(|
abla u_1|+|
abla u_2|)^p\, m{d} x$, that is, the $p$-energy of $u$ considered as a map into the normed plane $(\mathbb{R}^2,|\cdot|_1)$, the metric limit of the networks.
$L$-tauberian operators and subspaces with equi-integrable unit ball

We introduce the class $LW_+$ of $L$-tauberian operators and its dual counterpart, the class $MW_-$ of $M$-cotauberian operators. We obtain sequential, perturbative, and algebraic characterizations of these classes. As a consequence, every $T\in LW_+(E,Y)$ is disjointly non-singular, and the converse implication holds if and only if every dispersed subspace of $E$ has equi-integrable unit ball. For $E=L_p$, the latter property depends on $p$. For $1\leq p<2$, equi-integrability of the unit ball is equivalent to dispersedness, and $L$-tauberian operators coincide with disjointly non-singular operators, while for $p\geq 2$ these equivalences fail. Moreover, $LW_+(L_p)$ is neither open nor stable under composition. Applying a result of Haydon, Odell, and Schlumprecht, we show that for $2<p<\infty$ every infinite dimensional dispersed subspace of $L_p$ contains an infinite dimensional subspace with equi-integrable unit ball. However, we give an example showing that this is not true for $p=2$.

Every nonempty connected finite-dimensional CW topological semigroup admits a continuous associative multiplication on its universal cover that lifts the multiplication of the base. Such a multiplication is unique up to a deck transformation: in fact, any two associative lifts are conjugate whenever they exist. We show that the finite-dimensional hypothesis cannot be dropped in general: a connected, countable, infinite-dimensional CW topological semigroup is constructed for which continuous lifts of multiplication exist, but none is associative. The counterexample has nonabelian fundamental group isomorphic to Thompson's group $F$. Thus finite dimensionality is sufficient for associative lifting in the CW setting, whereas the unrestricted infinite-dimensional statement fails.
On the homeomorphism group of the Cantor set: monotone and measure preserving maps

Let $E$ be the Cantor set, $G=\operatorname{Homeo}(E)$, let $P\le G$ be the group of order preserving homeomorphisms and $L\le G$ the group of homeomorphisms preserving the Cantor--Lebesgue measure $λ$. We study how $G$ is built from these two subgroups. In 2003, Glasner and Weiss stated that $G=LP=PL$. We show that this is not the case, in fact $PL$ and $LP$ are two different proper subsets of $G$. On the other hand, $PL$ is a dense $G_δ$ subset of $G$, the multiplication map $P\times L\to PL$ is a homeomorphism, and $G=PLP=LPL$. In particular, every homeomorphism of $E$ is conjugate to an element of $PL$. We classify the double cosets $PgL$ using special clopen values set. There are continuum many of them, and $PL$ is the only one which is not meager. We prove that $G$ is topologically generated by one element of $P$ and one element of $L$ and these two generators produce the Thompson's group $V$. We also show that the generic homeomorphism of $E$ is the product of a generic element of $P$ and a generic element of $L$. The equality $G=PL$ fails also if $λ$ is replaced by any other full nonatomic measure.
On the Limits of Stochastic Push-Pull over Time-Varying Digraphs
Feiming Wang; Yutong He; Sulaiman Alghunaim; Kun Yuan

Stochastic Push-Pull achieves linear speedup with respect to the network size $n$ on static strongly connected digraphs, but whether this speedup persists on time-varying networks remains unclear. In this work, we construct a quadratic decentralized problem on period-two networks showing that stochastic Push-Pull may fail to attain linear speedup over time-varying digraphs. For $p$-periodic networks, we identify an effective node count $n_{\mathrm{eff}}\le n$ that governs the leading stochastic term. Specifically, for smooth nonconvex objectives, we establish convergence upper bounds and matching lower bounds for stochastic Push-Pull with constant stepsizes, both exhibiting the leading-order dependence $Θ(1/\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{eff}} T})$. When $p=1$, the identity $n_{\mathrm{eff}}=n$ recovers the usual linear speedup for static digraphs. However, periodic networks can have $n_{\mathrm{eff}}=o(n)$, demonstrating the loss of linear speedup under temporal variation. Numerical experiments illustrate effective-count scaling and the separation between static and periodic networks, consistent with our theoretical findings.
Motivic local density of isolated singularities of algebraic varieties

The goal of this paper is to compute the motivic local density of an isolated singularity of an algebraic variety, in order to explain its link with algebraic multiplicity. We compute the density as the residue in 1 of a Zeta function associated to normalized local volumes and we use a resolution of the singularity to get the formula.
An improved upper bound on the chromatic number of the n-dimensional sphere
A. I. Bikeev; V. A. Voronov; A. M. Raigorodskii

In this short note, we obtain upper bounds on the chromatic numbers of spheres using recent improvements in bounds for Euclidean space. We show that $χ(S^n_{R}) \leq (ξ_R + o(1))^n$, where $ξ_R = \frac{3\sqrt 3}{2}(1-1/(4R^2)) $ and $χ(S^n_R)$ denotes the chromatic number of the $n$-dimensional sphere of a fixed radius $R$.

An $\mathrm{ISK}_4$ is a graph that is isomorphic to a subdivision of $K_4$; a \textit{diamond} is $K_4$ minus one edge; and a \textit{bowtie} consists of two triangles sharing exactly one vertex. Lévêque, Maffray, and Trotignon~(2012) conjectured that every $\mathrm{ISK}_4$-free graph is $4$-colorable. Chen, Chen, Cui, Feng, and Liu~(2021) proved this for $\{\textup{diamond},\textup{bowtie}\}$-free graphs. We prove this conjecture for diamond-free graphs. Moreover, the bound is optimal.
Stable Set Reconfiguration in Dense Digraphs
Sarah Houdaigoui; Nacim Oijid; Matthieu Petiteau; Alexandre Vigny

In a directed graph, a stable (or acyclic) set is a set which does not induce a directed cycle. Given a directed graph and two acyclic sets of the same size, the Acyclic-Set-Reconfiguration with Directed Token Sliding (ASR) problem asks whether one can, by iteratively replacing a vertex by an adjacent one, transform the first set into the second one, while maintaining acyclicity during the transformation. In this work, we present a study of the complexity of ASR and provide an FPT algorithm for semi-complete digraphs, when parametrized by the size of the sets being reconfigured, the directed pathwidth (or equivalently, the directed treewidth) of the instance, and a newly introduced parameter called the iteration of the reconfiguration sequence. To the best of our knowledge, the reconfiguration of stable sets has only been studied on undirected graphs, or (more recently) on sparse directed graphs.
MIACE and Monotone Tracking: Exact Tuning for First-Order Plants and Positive Cascades with Pure Delay

The Module of Integral Absolute Complex Error (MIACE) was created by me 23 years ago. It gave very nice behaviour to the transient response of the controlled systems I tested. It combines absolute tracking-error and equilibrium-centered command areas. For a stable unit-gain plant with known pure delay, an exact identity separates squared MIACE excess into a negative-area penalty and a weighted area imbalance. The resulting lower bound depends on the plant's first low-frequency moment and the delay. Every attaining response of a positive cascade is monotone, independently of controller structure. For a first-order plant, output variation and peak overshoot also admit quantitative bounds. Exact conditions identify the unique positive PI controller attaining the delayed bound; filtered PID extends attainment beyond this PI range. For cascades of arbitrary order, Hermite interpolation and a finite-support delay remainder construct proper rational controllers of the same order, with internal exponential stability proved by positive convolution representations. An exponential-moment characterization then closes the attainment question when internal delay blocks are allowed: an ordinary command attains the bound if and only if $α>μ+δ-1$. An explicit internal-model controller realizes every feasible weight and delay. A sharp amplitude-cap condition determines the least command peak among all attaining responses and the complete capped sign-preserving area front. A small-gain estimate supplies an explicit MIACE deviation bound under delay error. A storage balance also extends the exact MIACE identity and monotone attainment to a nonlinear first-order class without delay. Independent physical integrations retain delays exactly; quadratic comparisons provide complementary benchmarks.
Quivers with Involutions and Shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$Quantum groups via Coulomb Branches
Yaolong Shen; Changjian Su; Zichang Wang; Rui Xiong

We give a formula for quasi-minuscule monopole operators in $K$-theoretic quantized Coulomb branch algebras of cotangent type. We then study signed quivers with involutions, with orthogonal or symplectic gauge factors at the involution-fixed vertices. We construct a GKLO-type homomorphism from the corresponding shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$quantum group to an algebra of $q$-difference operators and prove that it factors through the quantized Coulomb branch algebra. These homomorphisms give geometric realizations of the shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$quantum groups in terms of dressed minuscule and quasi-minuscule monopole operators.
The Malt'sev condition for groups is not categorical

In this paper we prove that the Mal'tsev condition expressing the existence of group operations is not equivalent to a categorical property. More precisely, using pseudo-invertible idempotents, we construct two varieties $\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{V}(f)$ which are equivalent as categories, and such that $\mathcal{V}$ admits group operations, whereas $\mathcal{V}(f)$ does not. We also show that those Mal'tsev conditions which are equivalent to a categorical property have a trivial spectrum.

We characterise the existence of expectation-preserving embeddings of reduced amalgamated free product $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras into norm ultrapowers of the first factor, fixing its diagonal copy pointwise, in terms of complementary compression relations on Hilbert space ultrapowers. This yields new characterisations of Robert's notion of selflessness, selfless inclusions, and relative selflessness with respect to conditional expectations. We also characterise Ozawa's notion of complete selflessness, including its extension to inclusions. We then illustrate the usefulness of these characterisations by establishing complete selflessness for suitable reduced (amalgamated) free products, free Araki--Woods $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras, certain Hecke $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras, and $q$-Gaussian $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras. Finally, we obtain dynamical characterisations of (complete) $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-selflessness of discrete groups and establish relative selflessness for suitable reduced crossed products.
Optimality of finite field dimension expanders

We show that random tuples of matrices over a finite field are uniform dimension expanders for every expansion coefficient below the optimal one, using elementary counting arguments. The same holds for the optimal coefficient along a set of dimensions of density 1. By contrast, along Fibonacci dimensions random pairs of matrices fail to be optimal dimension expanders with probability bounded away from zero.
Fuglede's theorem in the Heisenberg group
Davide Massenz; Roberto Monti; Julián Pozuelo

We prove a Fuglede-type quantitative isoperimetric inequality for the Pansu sphere, the conjectured isoperimetric set in the sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^1$. We show that, among suitable volume-preserving normal perturbations of the Pansu sphere that are small in a weighted $C^2$-norm, the difference between the sub-Riemannian perimeters of the perturbed and unperturbed regions is bounded below by a positive constant times the square of their $L^1$-distance. The proof is based on a Riemannian approximation argument with uniform estimates.
Global injectivity and real Jacobian conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^n$
Xinhao Hu; Jaume Llibre; Yilei Tang

In this paper, we study the global injectivity of local diffeomorphisms in $\mathbb{R}^n$, extending the criterions of Braun and Llibre in [{\it Pacific J. Math.} {\bf 333} (2024) 1--15] from the planar radial case to arbitrary dimension. Then we extend the results of Llibre and Mello in [{\it Bull. Sci. Math.} {\bf 213} (2026) 103889] to arbitrary dimension, obtaining two necessary and sufficient conditions for the real Jacobian conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^n$ by qualitative theory of differential equations. Finally, using weighted Poincaré compactification in $\mathbb{R}^n$, we provide a sufficient condition for the real Jacobian conjecture.
Meromorphic approximation of holomorphic maps into algebraically elliptic projective varieties

We show that holomorphic maps from a neighborhood of a compact set in a Stein space to an algebraically elliptic smooth projective variety can be approximated by meromorphic maps, provided that the map extends continuously to the whole space and the compact set is convex with respect to a submonoid of the Picard group. The proof uses algebraic sprays and their polynomial lifts to affine cones, which we call conic lifts. Rational sprays, which generalize algebraic sprays, extend the result to maps avoiding the exceptional set of a rational spray. We also show that, for smooth projective varieties, the existence of an algebraic spray which is dominating at some point is a birational invariant.
A Robust Control Architecture for Multirate Systems and their Interconnections

We introduce a framework for analyzing and designing linear multirate control systems and their interconnections through the lens of robust control. The proposed approach models multirate systems as impulsive systems with multiple independent jump maps and corresponding jump-time sequences. We tackle analysis and design problems with stability, dissipativity, and robustness objectives, relying on a multi-clock-dependent Lyapunov function parameterization. Further, we develop a compositional approach for analyzing interconnections of multirate systems based on individual dissipativity properties. The theoretical conditions can be verified via linear matrix inequalities and they require weak assumptions on the sampling rates, allowing for asynchronous and time-varying sampling rates with or without separated time scales. The practicality of the framework is demonstrated with numerical examples.
Josef v. H. Doyle; Wesley Fussner

We show that each of the infinitely many extensions of the basic inquisitive logic has the Craig interpolation property, and deduce from this that each of these extensions also has the Beth definability property. These results stand in contrast to existing characterizations of interpolation within lattices of extensions, in which the distribution of logics with interpolation is sparse.
Long-time stability and convergence of a BDF3 method for a parabolic equation with fading memory

We analyze the long-time stability and convergence of a third-order backward differentiation formula (BDF3) for parabolic equations with exponentially fading memory. The BDF3 scalar resolvent has oscillatory coefficients, so the monotonicity argument used for lower-order formulas in [Math. Comp. 62 (1994) 477-496] does not apply. We instead control memory feedback by the absolute mass of its discrete Green sequence and establish the rigorous stability-constant bounds $23/20<Λ_3<579/500$. A causal third-order memory quadrature with nonnegative assembled weights then yields exponentially weighted stability without a parabolic step-size restriction. With third-order starting values, we prove a uniform-in-time third-order temporal error estimate and extend it to conforming finite elements. Numerical tests confirm the predicted convergence orders and the long-time behavior.
Shintani Cocycle Decomposition of Topological Polylogarithms for Totally Real Fields

We compare two cohomological constructions computing special values of partial zeta functions of totally real number fields at nonpositive integers: the Shintani cocycles arising from polyhedral cone decompositions, and the Eisenstein classes obtained from the topological polylogarithm. In particular we prove that the specialization of the topological polylogarithm at a nonzero torsion point coincides in cohomology with the Shintani class up to an explicit sign and error term, and obtain Siegel and Klingen's classical rationality Theorem.
Bilinear Strichartz estimates on the hyperbolic space and the cubic NLS

We prove bilinear Strichartz estimates for the Schrödinger equation on the hyperbolic space. These bilinear estimates are then applied, as part of an I-method argument, to establish global well-posedness for the cubic defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the hyperbolic plane for regularities above 4/7. The I-method is implemented in physical space using a heat-based modified energy.
Mapping Academic Sports Analytics: A Content Analysis of JQAS and JSA

Sports analytics has expanded rapidly in professional sports and mainstream culture, yet defining its academic core remains a challenge. In this paper, we provide an empirical map of the academic sports analytics landscape based on a systematic content analysis of approximately 700 papers published in two leading dedicated journals, the Journal of Quantitative Analysis in Sports (JQAS) and the Journal of Sports Analytics (JSA), between the years 2005 and 2024. We classify each paper by sport discipline, mathematical method, and core research area, identify recurring themes, and examine macro trends. We find game tactics, player evaluation, team ranking, result forecasting, and tournament design to be the most studied research areas in sports analytics. We highlight selected papers in each area, illustrating the wide range of mathematical methods used and sports disciplines analyzed. Our work offers a comprehensive overview of the questions, methods, and disciplines that characterize the field, serving as a foundational reference for practitioners and researchers in sports analytics.
Saturation in three-uniform Berge hypergraphs: the five-star spectrum and the $K_4$ saturation number
XuanYu Cao; Yuan Lai; Chunxiang Wang

For a graph \(G\), a hypergraph is Berge-\(G\)-saturated if it contains no Berge copy of \(G\), but adding any missing hyperedge creates one. We determine the complete saturation spectrum of three-uniform Berge five-stars for every order. For \(n\ge7\), every integer from \(\lceil4n/3\rceil-3\) to \(2n-5\) occurs; the additional values depend only on \(n\) modulo five. The structural ingredient is a sharp bound on the remainder after deleting all complete five-vertex components: for an \(n\)-vertex, \(m\)-edge Berge-five-star-saturated hypergraph, this remainder has at most \(15(2n-m)/7\) vertices. We characterize all equality cases. We also prove that every three-uniform Berge-\(K_4\)-saturated hypergraph on \(n\ge7\) vertices has at least \(n\) edges. Together with known constructions, this determines its saturation number for every order and settles the conjecture of Chen, He, and Xie; the new lower bound covers the previously unresolved orders \(9\le n\le95\). Both arguments use the distinct representatives forced by saturation to obtain local incidence constraints. For five-stars these constraints bound the size of the remainder and characterize equality. For \(K_4\), they reduce a putative counterexample to a configuration on at most eight vertices; incidence estimates and a sharp bound on the vertices covered by short cycles in a bipartite graph exclude all remaining cases.
Cofinite integral braces and crystallographic groups
Rafał Lutowski; Andrzej Szczepański; Anna Zamojska-Dzienio

A left brace is cofinite integral (CIB) if its additive group is free abelian of finite rank and its quotient by the socle is finite. Rump introduced such braces and showed that the multiplicative group of every CIB is a crystallographic group. We study CIBs from the point of view of crystallographic groups. We prove an analogue of the Bieberbach theorems: in each dimension there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of CIBs. For a fixed crystallographic group, we show that its CIB structures correspond to the orbits of a finite group action on a set of bijective 1-cocycles. We use this description to develop algorithms that enumerate them. Finally, we give a complete census of CIBs on crystallographic and Bieberbach groups up to dimension 6.
Cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$
Xue Wang; Jun-Jie Huang; Da-Wei Yang

A graph is edge-transitive if its automorphism group acts transitively on its edge set. This paper is devoted to a systematic study of cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$, where $p$ is a prime and $\ell$ is an even integer. We first show that either $Γ$ is the unique cubic edge-transitive graph of order $18$, or its full automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(Γ)$ contains a normal Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ which is isomorphic to either $Z_{p^2}$ or $Z_{p}^2$. For the case $P\cong Z_{p^2}$, we prove that $Γ$ is either arc-regular or edge-regular, and provide a complete classification of such graphs. For the case $P\cong Z_{p}^2$, we prove that $Γ$ is a normal cover of certain known graphs. This work generalizes previous classifications by Zhou and Feng (2024), Lu et al.~(2004), and others. As an application, we obtain a classification of cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$ in the case where $\ell$ is square-free.
Angle cocycles, Euler characteristic, and simplicial volume of smooth manifolds
Michelle Bucher; Stefano Francaviglia; Grazia Rago

A celebrated conjecture of Gromov states that for closed aspherical manifolds, the vanishing of simplicial volume implies the vanishing of the Euler characteristic. We prove Gromov's conjecture for closed convex projective manifolds and, more generally, for closed orientable smooth manifolds admitting an immersed straightening. Generalising the straightening of simplices in properly convex domains in real projective space, we introduce the notion of immersed straightening and prove that, for every integer $d\geq 1$, there exists a constant $C_d>0$ such that every closed orientable smooth $d$-manifold $M$ admitting an immersed straightening satisfies $|χ(M)|\le C_d||M||$.
A domain-decomposition reduced-order model for two-phase CO$_2$ sequestration with moving wells
Xin He; Xianda Shen; Lei Zhang

We present a domain-decomposition reduced-order model for two-phase geological CO$_2$ storage with fixed and moving wells. The approach builds on a nonoverlapping Schur formulation of a conservative RT0--P0 discretization solved by a sequential pressure--transport algorithm. The distinctive feature of the formulation is that local reduced models are coupled through physically meaningful interface variables: pressure traces for the pressure solve and inflow saturation traces for the transport solve. To address moving wells, we introduce a well-aware strategy that combines source-response enrichment, HAPOD-based far-field compression, and hybrid full-order/reduced-order treatment of well and near-well subdomains. We also formulate conservation-oriented hyper-reduction rules where interface fluxes, boundary terms and source terms are protected. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate accuracy, computational efficiency, robustness of the overall methodology.
The elastic figure-eight knot is not planar
We prove that every elastic knot in any non-torus twist knot class is not planar. In particular, this disproves a numerically motivated planarity conjecture for elastic figure-eight knots.
Dynamics of a Harvested Predator-Prey Model with a Generalized Holling Type~III Response Capturing Group Defense
Wael El Khateeb; Farjana Akter; Chanaka Kottegoda; Muner Mustafa Abou Hasan

We investigate a predator-prey model with constant prey harvesting and a generalized Holling type III functional response, focusing on the biological and dynamical consequences of allowing the parameter $b$ to be negative. In this regime, predation efficiency declines at high prey densities, potentially reflecting group defense. This change permits an additional coexistence equilibrium and introduces new bifurcation mechanisms affecting population persistence. We establish the existence of a codimension-three Bogdanov--Takens bifurcation, derive a codimension-three nilpotent-saddle unfolding, and investigate a codimension-two generalized Hopf bifurcation and the emergence of multiple limit cycles. Our analysis show that moderate harvesting weakens the protection conferred by high prey abundance; excessive harvesting leaves too few prey to sustain predator growth; and low harvesting preserves strong group defense, requiring high predator density for population persistence.
Peaking self-similar solutions and continuation after blow-up for a quasilinear Hardy-Hénon equation
Razvan Gabriel Iagar; Ariel Sánchez; Erik Sarrión-Pedralva

We consider the quasilinear Hardy-Hénon equation $$ u_t=Δu^m+|x|^σu^p, \quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,T), $$ in the range of exponents and dimension $$ N\geq3, \quad σ\in(-2,\infty), \quad m>1, \quad p>p_S(σ)=\frac{m(N+2σ+2)}{N-2}. $$ We establish sharp ranges of exponents $(m,p,σ)$ guaranteeing existence of \emph{peaking solutions} in backward self-similar form $$ u(x,t)=(T-t)^{-α}f(|x|(T-t)^{-β}). $$ By peaking solutions we understand solutions blowing up at a finite time $T\in(0,\infty)$ but allowing for a continuation after the blow-up time. As a remarkable outcome, a number of ranges of exponents $σ$ and $m$ for which peaking solutions exist for any $p>p_S(σ)$ are deduced, contrasting to the previously considered exponent $σ=0$, where a Lepin-type critical exponent $p_L$ provides an upper bound for $p$.
A stochastic mirror descent algorithm for mean-field control problems

We develop a stochastic mirror descent method for continuous-time McKean-Vlasov control with measure-valued controls and general Bregman regularisation. The dependence on the state law leads to a coupled Wasserstein-Bregman stability problem and to a McKean-Vlasov adjoint equation, which have no counterpart in classical stochastic control. We establish a first-order representation of the cost and prove its relative smoothness in two regimes: nonlinear dynamics with bounded cost derivatives, and affine state-law dynamics with linearly growing cost derivatives, the latter covering linear-quadratic (LQ) and more general nonquadratic models. Our regularity conditions in the control measure are formulated through directional finite increments and do not require second-order flat derivatives. We further introduce relative semiconvexity along admissible forward-backward trajectories, allowing compensation between the dynamics, running cost, and terminal cost beyond pointwise Hamiltonian convexity. This yields energy dissipation, an O(1/n) convergence rate at the convexity threshold, and geometric convergence when regularisation dominates relative nonconvexity. Explicit LQ criteria and numerical experiments illustrate the scope of the results.
Prime Numbers of the Form $24m+1$ and Erdös-Straus Conjecture

In 1948, Erdös and Straus formulated a conjecture on Egyptian fractions. One only needs to prove the conjecture for any prime number $n$ such that $n\equiv 1\;(\mbox{mod}\;24)$. In this article, we give a necessary and sufficient polynomial condition for a number of the form $24m+1$ to be a prime number. Then we present 56 solvability polynomials consisting of our earlier tame solutions, wild solutions and the polynomials for composite numbers of the form $24m+1$. Numeric test shows that they imply the conjecture. Moreover, we give a list of 36 exponential-polynomial functions consisting of our earlier 28 tame solutions and the polynomials for composite numbers, whose numeric test shows that Howerton's conjecture on fourteen wild primes holds. Furthermore, we find a version of Goldbach conjecture modulo 24.
Continuous-Time Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection Reinforcement Learning Problems for a Markov Regime-Switching System with No-Shorting Constraints
Minghui Zhang; Xun Li; Xin Zhang

This paper is the first to study the continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection problem with no-shorting constraints in a Markov regime-switching market using reinforcement learning (RL). The main challenge stems from the interaction between random regime shifts and portfolio non-negativity constraints, which typically causes the coupled Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations to lose smoothness across different state regions. Additionally, directly imposing no-shorting constraints on randomized policies disrupts their analytically tractable Gaussian structure, complicating both exploratory modeling and reinforcement learning. To address these challenges, we propose an auxiliary exploratory approach that limits the policy to a Gaussian distribution and applies the no-shorting constraint solely to its mean. We explicitly characterize the optimal policy for this auxiliary problem and demonstrate that, by appropriately selecting the exploration variance, its optimal mean policy exactly matches the optimal policy of the original constrained mean-variance problem. Building upon this analytical framework, we develop a model-free reinforcement learning algorithm that learns the optimal portfolio policy directly from trajectory data. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results and show that the proposed method can effectively recover the optimal no-shorting portfolio in a regime-switching market.

Junfeng Chen; Yongchen Fan; Zhonghua Qiao; Kailiang Wu

High-fidelity Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) simulations remain a standard tool for aerodynamic analysis, yet each solve on an unstructured mesh is computationally expensive, making many-query tasks such as design exploration, optimization, and multi-condition evaluation costly. Neural operators provide mesh-flexible surrogates for mapping geometry and operating conditions to flow fields; however, in many existing architectures, global parameters such as the freestream state and design variables are concatenated with pointwise inputs, leaving their influence on intermediate features implicit. This paper proposes CoPiT, a \textbf{Co}nditional \textbf{P}osition-induced \textbf{T}ransformer that builds on the Position-induced Transformer (PiT) as its geometric backbone and injects a global condition vector through multi-stage feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), thereby making parametric modulation explicit while preserving geometry-based attention weights. Matched ablations show that FiLM conditioning generally improves upon input concatenation, while the preferred placement is task-dependent. CoPiT thus provides a practical operator-learning surrogate for parametric aerodynamics on unstructured meshes.
Optimal time decay of the Boltzmann equation with cutoff soft potentials in the whole space
Yuanjie Lei; Xiongju Wei; Tong Yang; Huijiang Zhao

Since Strain's work \cite{Strain-2012-KRM} on almost optimal time decay rates for the microscopic part of perturbative classical solutions to the Boltzmann system with soft potentials via the time-velocity splitting method, how to obtain the optimal decay of the microscopic part has remained unsolved. In this paper, we resolve this problem by developing a nonlinear energy estimate method different from the time-velocity splitting approach. The proof relies on a combination of a hierarchy of time-weighted energy estimates, the damping factor \(e^{-ν(v)(t-τ)}\), and a dyadic decomposition of velocity space.

We consider the Ising spin-glass model on Migdal--Kadanoff (MK) hierarchical lattices, characterized by the fractal dimension $d=1+\log s/\log b$, where $s$ and $b$ denote the number of parallel branches and the number of bonds in series within each branch, respectively. Conversely, we prove the absence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for fractal dimensions $d<1+\log17/\log6\approx2.58$, as well as in the large-$b$ limit for any fixed $d<3$. Our results provide a complete characterization of finite-temperature spin-glass order on MK hierarchical lattices.

Chaopeng Tan; Qiongdan Hu; Meng Wang

Max-pressure (MP) traffic signal control selects phases using pressure scores computed from estimated traffic states, but these states are uncertain and their consequences depend on whether they alter phase ranking and how much pressure is lost. This paper develops a decision-oriented Regret-Based Max-Pressure framework that represents uncertainty through phase-selection regret, defined as the pressure loss of a candidate phase relative to the pressure-maximizing phase under each plausible latent state. We propose Stochastic Regret MP, which minimizes expected regret under a calibrated residual distribution, and Distributionally Robust (DR) Regret MP, which minimizes worst-case expected regret over a Wasserstein ambiguity set. Robustifying regret rather than absolute pressure makes the formulation invariant to state-dependent pressure components shared by all candidate phases, thereby focusing robustness on relative phase quality. We further derive an explicit queue-linear pressure-loss bound and establish strong queue stability when the net-service reserve exceeds the resulting loss coefficient. Numerical experiments show that both methods reduce normalized true-state pressure regret by about 70% relative to Point-estimate MP, while DR Regret MP yields lower network queues than direct robustification of absolute pressure. In microscopic SUMO experiments on a 28-intersection real-world network, Stochastic Regret MP and DR Regret MP reduce mean delay by 18.9% and 14.9%, respectively, and retain benefits under detector undercount and failure. The results show that representing uncertainty through its decision consequences can improve reliable traffic control under imperfect state information.
Geometry property of stochastic parabolic equations and Prékopa-Leindler inequality on bounded domains

We study the preservation of spatial concavity and log-concavity for stochastic parabolic equations posed on bounded convex domains. For the linear noise, by using Minkowski convolutions, we establish the convexity preservation of solution almost surely. For the nonlinear noise, by using Itô formula, the impact of noise is given. Moreover, we establish the relationship between the weighted (stochastic) Prékopa-Leindler inequality and properties of (stochastic) parabolic equation on bounded domain, which is new even for deterministic case.
Empirically Calibrated Differential Games for Simulating Driver Interactions
Amirmohammad Khakpour; Nachuan Li; Pedram Beigi; Yu; Nie

Game-theoretic models can resolve vehicle interactions without hand-written priority rules, but whether they describe human drivers once calibrated has rarely been tested. This study formulates a general-sum differential game of vehicle interactions at urban intersections, calibrates it to observed driving, and evaluates it on data not used for calibration. Each vehicle minimizes a cost that combines speed tracking, adherence to a map-derived lane route, control effort, gap keeping based on the intelligent driver model, a predictive conflict term, and a contact barrier, while perceiving the other vehicles with a delay. The game is solved with a feedback iterative linear-quadratic algorithm, and ten behavioral parameters per vehicle are calibrated by Bayesian optimization on trajectories recorded at four intersections in Washington, D.C. The calibrated game reproduces the trajectories of 819 vehicles with a mean position error of 1.00 m. When only each vehicle's route is known, as in a simulator, it is the most accurate of the compared models on 96 held-out vehicles (7.42 m), and ten-fold cross-validation shows that it is significantly more accurate than calibrated SUMO (by 3.61 m), an inverse reinforcement learning model (by 0.93 m), and independent and cooperative variants of the same model (by 0.33 and 0.32 m). The solutions, computed in 2.1 s for a typical interaction, are verified approximate equilibria. Finally, the conflict and steering weights, which the data do not identify, can be set from safety and comfort targets; together with a stiffer contact barrier, this removes the collisions that otherwise occur in 43% of tight closed-loop conflicts.
Semilinear Schrödinger equation with harmonic potential and combined power-type nonlinearities
Jiangbo Han; Runzhang Xu; Chao Yang

We study the Cauchy problem for the semilinear Schrödinger equation with a harmonic potential and combined power-type nonlinearities. The goal is to classify initial data that lead to either global existence or blowup solutions by using an enhanced cross-constrained variational theory. First, we review and analyze this variational approach, pinpointing the main issue for our specific problem. We then introduce new variational structures by carefully selecting terms in the energy functional and adjusting their weights, enabling us to create eight cross-constrained variational combinations and related manifolds to distinguish initial data that result in global solutions or finite-time blowup. Using these structures, we examine three initial energy levels: negative, non-negative low, and high energy. Notably, we prove that for any initial data with negative energy, solutions blow up in finite time regardless of their size. Throughout the study, we utilize these new variational frameworks and functionals to systematically classify initial data for global existence or finite-time blowup. We highlight the comprehensiveness of our approach as we analyze numerous combinations of the energy and mass terms, despite the complexity involved. Interestingly, we find that when initial energy is minimized, classifications based on different functionals coincide. For high initial energy, an unresolved issue even for the standard Schrödinger equation, we develop a strategy controlling bounds of energy to classify the solution dynamics, including global existence or blowup, for our model. We also provide a complete proof for the standard case addressing this open problem.
On the Algebraic Structure of Lewis Carroll's Logic -- Behind the Looking Glass: A Mathematical Perspective

Charles Ludwidge Dodgeson, better known by his literary pen name `Lewis Carroll', has a number of well known and cherished literary works to his credit, for example "Alice in Wonderland" and "Through the Looking Glass". Apart from this he is known to have a strong professional interest in mathematics and logic with an inclination towards an educational and recreational perspective. In this work we consider the algebraic structure behind Lewis Carroll's approach to classical logic and his logical puzzles. Starting with the arithmetic of $0$ and $1$, we develop the connections between Boolean-valued functions, sets and predicates, which we refer to as the "entangled trinity". This provides a common setting in which Carroll's approach and Boole's perspective can be understood. Particular attention is given to what is meant by "the conclusion" of a logical problem. We suggest a precise interpretation of a complete conclusion in terms of largest lower bounds involving only the predicates to be retained, thereby sharpening Carroll's approach. The role of natural language in choosing a suitable universe and identifying these predicates is discussed through a variety of examples. Finally, we present computerised solution methods, including the use of Boolean satisfiability solvers for larger puzzles.
An energy-stable parametric finite element framework for surface diffusion with moving contact lines on curved substrates
Harald Garcke; Robert Nürnberg; Rong Tang

We develop energy-stable parametric finite element methods for surface diffusion of solid films with moving contact lines on curved substrates. Discretizing both the film surface and the substrate patches allows the introduction of linear schemes that are unconditionally energy stable. A nonlinear variant of the schemes ensures that, in addition, the vertices of the substrate approximations remain attached to the true substrate throughout. Moreover, our framework can incorporate anisotropic surface energy densities, for both the film surface and the substrate, as well as different tangential motions. Numerical experiments in two and three space dimensions illustrate the practicality of the introduced methods.
Conway polynomials of $Th(p,q)$ and $Th(q,p)$: a proof of Takemura's conjecture

Takemura conjectured that the Conway polynomials $\sum a_\ell z^\ell$ of the Turk's head link $Th(p,q)$ and $\sum b_\ell z^\ell$ of $Th(q,p)$ satisfy $a_\ell=b_\ell$ for $\ell\equiv0,1\pmod 4$ and $a_\ell=-b_\ell$ for $\ell\equiv2,3\pmod4$, and proved it for $q=2,3$. We prove it for all $p,q\ge1$, knots and links. Equivalently, $
abla_{Th(q,p)}(z)=c\,
abla_{Th(p,q)}(iz)$ with $c=1$ if $\gcd(p,q)$ is odd and $c=-i$ if it is even. The proof combines a product formula $
abla_{Th(p,q)}(z)^2=\prod_{j=1}^{p-1}\prod_{k=1}^{q-1}(z^2+2\cos rac{2πk}{q}-2\cos rac{2πj}{p})$, which comes from the reduced Burau representation, with the leading coefficients, read off the Seifert surface of the closed braid.
Distributed Attacker Assignment and Interception Control in Multi-Agent Target-Attacker-Defender Games
Pengyang Fan; Shaoqing Zhang; Chao Zhai; Weiguo Xia

This paper addresses the Target-Attacker-Defender (TAD) game within a planar environment, focusing on the protection of a stationary target against incoming threats. To compensate for potential speed disadvantages of the defenders, we leverage geometric pre-positioning within an annular defense perimeter. The problem is formulated as an area interception problem, for which we propose a distributed multi-agent algorithm consisting of two primary modules: target allocation and interception control. For target allocation, an equitable region partitioning strategy is employed to divide the defense area into annular sectors and assign defenders to attackers. Under specified angular-separation and parameter conditions, the proposed partitioning mechanism ensures that each defender is assigned at most one attacker, thereby reducing the complexity of multi-agent assignment. For the control layer, movement protocols based on zero-sum differential games and coverage optimization are designed, achieving Nash equilibrium strategies while maintaining effective barrier coverage. Numerical simulations show that the proposed method enables slower defenders to intercept faster attackers through proactive deployment and maintains nearly constant local computation time as the swarm size increases.
Value-distribution of Euler--Zagier type multiple zeta-functions with identical arguments on the critical line

We consider the value-distribution of the Euler--Zagier type multiple zeta-functions with identical arguments on the critical line. Mishou showed that the set of the values of the Euler--Zagier double sum with identical arguments on the critical line is dense in the complex plane under the Riemann Hypothesis. In this paper, we generalize Mishou's result to the $r$-fold Euler--Zagier multiple zeta-functions with identical arguments for $r geq 4$.
Nadler Theorem on Generalized Metric Spaces with Weighted Graphs

We introduce a generalized metric space endowed with a weighted graph and establish sufficient conditions for the existence of fixed points for set-valued mappings that satisfy a contractive condition only along the links of the graph. To demonstrate the applicability and significance of our results, several illustrative examples are presented. As an application, we establish the solvability of a class of integral problems involving set-valued data.
A counterexample to Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions
Yansong Feng; Hao Jiang; Guancheng Li; Tianyi Li; Lili Tang

It is well known that the sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^n$ has algebraic degree at most $n/2$ for even $n\ge 4$. Tokareva conjectured that the converse holds: every Boolean function with degree at most $n/2$ can be written as a sum of two bent functions. The conjecture has been verified for even $n\leq 6$ and for several special classes of Boolean functions. We disprove this conjecture by showing that $x_1x_2(x_3x_4+x_5x_6+x_7x_8)$ is not a sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^8$. We extend this construction to obtain counterexamples in every even dimension $n\ge 8$. Using Shaporenko's reduction, we also obtain explicit counterexamples to Tokareva's derivative conjecture in every even dimension $n\ge 10$.
Averages of traces and ratios of characteristic polynomials of random unitary matrices
Ada Bendel; Rhys Cahill; John Brian Conrey; Gregor Harrison Barraclough; Ayesha Irfan; Nina Claire Snaith; Leonid Tyulenev

In this work we explore the extent to which the Ratios Theorem for averages over $U(N)$, with respect to Haar measure, of ratios of characteristic polynomials can be used to evaluate averages of traces of unitary matrices. We derive concrete expressions for all averages involving up to 4 traces, valid for any matrix size, $N$. We also calculate the so-called zero-swap and one-swap contributions to an average with any number of traces, which amounts to determining general trace moments in a range double the size of the renowned result of Diaconis and Shahshahani. The expression is tractable enough to use in applications, for example to determine the parameter range where certain trace averages assume negative values.
Weak-$L^\infty$ and BMO with Hausdorff Content
Hao Guo; Long Huang; Yangzhi Zhang; Ciqiang Zhuo

The space of weak-$L^{\infty}$ on measure space was introduced by Bennett et al. (Ann. of Math., 113(1981), 601-611) and proved to contain the space of $L^\infty$ and possess the appropriate interpolation property. In this paper, we are aimed to continue this line of research on the Euclidean space $\mathbb R^n$ endowed with Hausdorff content, which is a low-dimensional outer measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and fails to be additive or absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measures. But low-dimensional subsets, such as fractals, of $\mathbb{R}^n$ are Hausdorff capacitable. Precisely, in the setting of Hausdorff content, an analogue of weak-$L^\infty$ is defined and proved to possess an improved Marcinkiewicz interpolation theorem. Moreover, we show that the space of functions with bounded mean oscillation associated to the Hausdorff content is embedded into this new weak-$L^\infty$ space by establishing a key estimate for the distribution via a packing condition. As a by-product, the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood operator on the space of weak-$L^{\infty}$ is established.
Performing a Quantum Subroutine Using Cluster States
Sakibul Islam Rayhan; Karima Hassan; Md Rasedujjaman; Md Mohsinur Rahman Adnan

Quantum subroutines, like their classical counterparts, serve as essential components of larger algorithms. They can be realized using gate based architectures or measurement based quantum computation (MBQC), where computation proceeds through adaptive measurements on highly entangled cluster states. In this work, we implement a phase oracle as a reusable subroutine within the MBQC framework using experimentally feasible cluster states. Unlike prior demonstrations of Grover's algorithm in MBQC that omit explicit oracle construction, our approach provides a transparent formulation of the oracle subroutine, including its measurement patterns, byproduct correlations, density-matrix simulations, and corresponding MBQC measurement circuits.
A Sharp Upper Bound for the Frobenius Number
Lin Chen; Tingwei Hu; Yuchen Mao; Guochuan Zhang

Let $0<a_1<\cdots<a_n$ be integers with $n\ge 2$ and $\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=1$. Their Frobenius number $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ is the largest integer that cannot be expressed as a nonnegative integer combination of $a_1,\ldots,a_n$. Erdős and Graham proved the classical bound $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le 2a_{n-1}\lfloor a_n/n\rfloor-a_n$, which depends on the two largest generators. Dixmier subsequently proved their conjecture $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le a_n^2/(n-1)$, a bound depending only on $a_n$ and $n$ that removes the factor $2$ from the corresponding quadratic estimate. Following the Erdős--Graham approach, we remove the factor $2$ while retaining the dependence on $a_{n-1}$, and prove $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le a_{n-1}\lceil a_n/(n-1)\rceil-a_n-1$. This bound can be substantially smaller than Dixmier's when $a_{n-1}$ is small relative to $a_n$. For every $n\ge3$, we also construct infinitely many instances satisfying the reverse inequality, which shows that the bound is sharp.
Wasserstein bounds for invariant measures in the Smoluchowski-Kramers approximation with stable noise

We study invariant position distributions in the Smoluchowski-Kramers approximation for Langevin equations driven by rotationally symmetric \(α\)-stable noise, with \(α\in(1,2)\). Under global Lipschitz continuity and dissipativity of the drift, we establish a Wasserstein-1 bound of order \(m^{1/α}\) between the invariant position distribution of the underdamped system and the invariant distribution of its overdamped limit, where $m>0$ is the mass parameter. The proof combines a corrected-position test function with a regularized Stein equation. Cancellation of the transport and friction terms reduces the comparison to a first-moment estimate for the stationary velocity.
Coefficient duality and interpolation of Euclidean flag Besov spaces

The main purpose of this paper is to develop the duality theory of the homogeneous Besov spaces associated with the Euclidean flag, using the discrete Littlewood--Paley--Stein analysis. We first establish an exact discrete sampling formula together with bounded analysis and synthesis maps, by which the space is identified with a sequence space of coefficients. The continuous dual is then computed through a coefficient norm. In this computation the geometry of the sampling rectangles plays an essential role: when the spatial exponent is below one, the volume of a dyadic rectangle forces an explicit shift of both smoothness indices. We devote particular attention to the supremum sequence exponent. At that endpoint the closure of the flag test functions is characterized by vanishing scale tails, and the limiting tail is comparable to the distance to this closure; every continuous functional on the full space decomposes into a canonical regular part and a part that annihilates the closure, and the latter may be nonzero. For finite exponents the dual is again a flag Besov space. As applications, finite Calderón sums give a quantitative approximation theorem, and the common analysis and synthesis framework yields real and complex interpolation as well as the lifting property. The arguments are based on the exact sampling formula, scalar maximal estimates and the transpose of one bounded coefficient projection.
Rough path lifts of multifractional Brownian motions

We show that multifractional Brownian motions (mBms) can be lifted to geometric rough paths. One of the main ingredients in the proof is a decomposition of mBms via the Lemarié-Meyer orthogonal wavelet basis, which is introduced in the context of multiresolution analysis. As a consequence, we are able to construct solutions to rough differential equations driven by mBms.

An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid 3.12.12, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid 4.8.8, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid 3.6.3.6, the elongated triangular grid $3^3.4^2$ and the snub hexagonal grid $3^4.6$. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid 4.6.12, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid 3.4.6.4, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid $3^2.4.3.4$.
Freeform Programmable Liquid Crystal Elastomers via Monolithic Integration of Co-Optimization and 4D-Printing
Yibo Wang; Asad Farooq Ahmed; Weichen Li; Weiyun Xu; Xiaojia Shelly Zhang

Liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) are active materials capable of large, reversible thermally induced actuation, offering significant potential for applications such as artificial muscles and soft robotics. However, their broader deployment is hindered by the lack of a unified design-to-fabrication framework, the strong coupling among geometry, director fields, and manufacturing constraints, and the difficulty of reliably translating complex designs into physically realizable architectures. Here, we present an autonomous and monolithic integration of co-optimization and 4D printing that enables the end-to-end design-to-realization of versatile programmable LCE architectures with superior precision, complexity, and versatility. The proposed framework establishes a unified design strategy that co-optimizes the freeform multilayer geometry and fully continuous layer-specific director distributions, and subsequently translates the optimized fields into fabrication-ready DIW toolpaths through an automated manufacturing-aware pipeline. To bridge computation and realization, we develop an optimization-centered 4D printing approach with automated, fabrication-aware toolpath generation tailored for direct ink writing of LCEs. With the proposed design-to-fabrication paradigm, we experimentally realize architectures that exhibit complex, non-intuitive thermo-mechanical behaviors. Experiments achieve highly challenging prescribed functionalities beyond the reach of intuition-based approaches and show excellent agreement with numerical simulations across all samples. This work establishes a generalizable inverse design and physical realization of freeform programmable LCE systems, enabling function-oriented and optimization-driven intelligent LCE applications for next-generation soft robotic and responsive material engineering.
An exploration of plug-and-play flow matching for full-waveform inversion on breast imaging
Cristina Garcia-Cardona; Siting Liu; Fatma Terzioglu; Shanyin Tong; Lu Zhang

Full-waveform inversion (FWI) reconstructs sound-speed fields from measured waveforms, by solving an optimization problem that minimizes the discrepancy between measured waveforms and those predicted by a numerical wave-propagation model. However, choosing suitable regularization for this optimization is challenging because it must stabilize the inversion while preserving relevant structures, prompting us to investigate whether priors learned from representative sound-speed images can improve reconstruction. In this work, we adapt plug-and-play flow matching (PnP-Flow) to FWI by alternating waveform-misfit updates with updates from a pretrained flow prior. We explore the effectiveness of PnP-Flow reconstruction by comparing it with total-variation (TV) regularization using noiseless transmission-only plane-wave data. Separate flow priors are trained on two circular-inclusion model families with constant and spatially varying backgrounds. We evaluate the method both on these in-distribution circle models and under substantial distribution shift by transferring the Gaussian-circle prior and reconstruction settings to breast phantom patches without retraining or retuning. Using the same number of waveform-misfit updates, the proposed PnP-Flow framework generally improves circle reconstruction accuracy and recovers breast lesion contrast more accurately than TV baselines.
Well-posedness for the Cubic Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation With Nonlinearity Supported on a Hypersurface

We prove that the 2-d cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with nonlinearity supported on a line or a sphere is globally well-posed in \(H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\). For higher dimensions, we prove that the equation with hyperplane-supported nonlinearity is locally well-posed in suitable anisotropic Sobolev spaces. We also prove that the equation with sphere-supported nonlinearity is globally well-posed in \(H^1(\mathbb{R}^n)\) for radial data.
Gagliardo--Nirenberg extremals on manifolds with small holes

We study the sharp homogeneous Dirichlet Gagliardo--Nirenberg quotient on a closed Riemannian manifold with holes of small capacity and connected complements. For each fixed exponent $2<q<2^*$, the nonnegative $L^2$-normalized extremal exists and is unique when the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $λ_D$ is sufficiently small. If the ambient volume is $V$ and $β=n(q-2)/2$, the sharp constant satisfies $C_D=V^{1-q/2}λ_D^{-β/2}(1+O(λ_D))$. For the normalized first eigenfunction $φ_D$, we obtain $\|u_D-φ_D\|_{H^1}=O(λ_D^{3/2})$ and $C_D/W_{M_D}(φ_D)=1+O(λ_D^2)$, together with a quantitative stability estimate in terms of the relative deficit. The constants depend only on the ambient manifold and the exponent. On general compact manifolds with Dirichlet boundary conditions, we prove compactness above the Euclidean sharp constant and describe concentration at equality. Positive scalar curvature at one interior point implies attainment. For the $L^2$-critical nonlinear Schrödinger energy, the mass threshold for negative energy tends to zero as the capacity of the holes tends to zero, whereas the threshold for unboundedness below is unchanged.
Coupling perturbations of the conformal Einstein-Dirac system on round spheres
Ke Xu; Tian Xu; Minbo Yang

We study the conformal Einstein-Dirac system on the round sphere $S^m$, $m\geq3$, with coupling coefficient $1+\eps k$, where $k\in C^2(S^m,\R)$ and $\eps$ is small. Morse and degree conditions yield solutions with positive scalar component, and a generic nondegeneracy condition gives multiplicity modulo spinorial symmetries. For a suitable fixed coefficient, we obtain a noncompact solution sequence with infinitely many distinct energy values. A Kazdan-Warner identity gives nonexistence for a smooth Morse potential and its small $C^2$-perturbations, even with positive coupling. The existence proofs use a local reduction in the interior of the positive cone, accommodating the negative powers occurring when $m\geq5$.
Encoding-Sensitive Nullstellensatz Certificates for Syndrome Exclusion in LDPC Codes: Sharp Local Bounds and a Linear Separation
Malihe Aliasgari; Hassan Khodaiemehr; Khadijeh Bagheri

Certifying that a parity-check matrix has no nonempty set of at most t variable nodes leaving at most b checks unsatisfied arises in minimum-distance and trapping-set analysis. Such absence is the infeasibility of a polynomial system, provable by an independently checkable Nullstellensatz certificate. The degree of these certificates depends strongly on how the two cardinality constraints are encoded, although the encodings have identical solutions. For a local encoding with inclusion-exclusion and cardinality obstructions, we construct explicit certificates of degree at most t + b + K + 1, with K logarithmic in the maximum check degree; this bound is independent of the block length and cannot be improved in general. For a standard counting encoding, a generalized planted-knapsack theorem, which pulls back a knapsack functional with an arbitrary target, gives lower bounds linear in the block length for cycle codes, regular codes of girth at least six near the feasibility boundary, array-based quasi-cyclic codes and minimum-distance certificates for arrays of circulant permutation matrices, where the local degree stays bounded. On array codes and regular codes of girth at least eight, planted column pairs extend these bounds to odd column weight with no unsatisfied checks. The planting argument is optimal among such pullbacks. All computed degrees and certificates are verified in exact rational arithmetic; bounds are distinguished from exact minimum degrees. Local certificates for quasi-cyclic matrices, including a lifted fifth-generation New Radio base graph, pass two independent verifiers.
Block Toeplitz Operators, Matrix Valued Truncated Toeplitz operators, and Conjugations

In this paper, we characterize the complex symmetry of block Toeplitz operators on the Hardy-Hilbert space H2(E) with conjugation C_{u,λ}, where E is a finite dimensional Hilbert space. We also extend the application of this conjugation to matrix valued truncated Toeplitz operators.
Weak adversarial tensor neural network for high-dimensional Fokker-Planck equations

Solving high-dimensional stationary Fokker-Planck (SFP) equations remains challenging. Recently, deep learning methods have shown great potential for solving high-dimensional SFP equations due to their universal approximation and mesh-free training. However, the high-dimensional integrals involved in loss computation and normalization can be expensive to approximate accurately using Monte Carlo integration. To address this issue, we propose a weak adversarial tensor neural network (WATNN) method for solving high-dimensional SFP equations, which combines a weak adversarial (WA) formulation with the tensor neural network (TNN). The WA formulation avoids the cross terms introduced by squaring the strong residual, reducing the number of integrals to be computed. When both the primal network and the adversarial test network are set as TNNs, the TNN quadrature scheme provides accurate and efficient normalization and loss computation with relatively few fixed quadrature points, avoiding the statistical sampling error that arises when using Monte Carlo integration. We demonstrate the effectiveness numerically on four high-dimensional SFP equations. For the 6D unimodal, 6D multi-modal, 10D multi-modal and 20D multi-modal problems, WATNN achieves the mean relative errors of 1.50%, 1.13%, 1.20% and 7.93% respectively, in only a few minutes.
Solving and Learning Navier-Stokes Dynamics with the Neural Basis Method
Yuhe Wang; Zhu Wang; Min Wang

Physics-informed machine learning has become a major direction in predictive modeling of fluid dynamics, combining governing physics with learned representations. Yet prevailing formulations neither guarantee that small PDE-residual losses imply small solution errors nor scale effectively with increasing problem size. Here we present the neural basis method (NBM) as a new approach for Navier--Stokes dynamics. NBM is built on a ``representation-then-projection'' principle: fixed neural bases define the representation space, while projection of the governing equations determines the expansion coefficients. The same bases define common coordinates for the parametric solution manifold, recasting operator learning as a parameter-to-coefficient mapping and enabling scalability by removing explicit spatial dependence. For incompressible flow, NBM yields a velocity-only formulation whose residual provides an a posteriori velocity-error estimate, establishing a certified, data-free training objective for coefficient learning. Theoretical analysis and numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency, generalization, and scalability of NBM, with substantial improvements over baselines.
A branch-and-filter method for mixed-integer linear programming

We develop a new tree-search framework for mixed-integer linear programming problems, which incorporates a filter mechanism as a node-acceptance device. The introduced branch-and-filter algorithm combines proper branching actions with a filter on integrality violation and an incumbent-dependent objective coordinate. Inspired by classical filter methods in nonconvex constrained optimization, the proposed method moves to a restoration phase whenever sufficient progress cannot be provided by the filter and funnel mechanisms, the latter of which is anchored at global relaxation lower bounds. Under mild assumptions, the introduced method either certifies infeasibility in finitely many iterations, or converges to global optimality. Moreover, we establish a total outer iteration complexity bound of order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1})$ to certification of an $\varepsilon$-optimal mixed-integer solution through fixed-integer linear programming recovery. We finally perform several numerical experiments to study the performance of branch-and-filter against benchmark solvers, under a branch-and-bound, a branch-and-cut, and a novel cell-deletion realization of the proposed restoration oracle.

We simplify and improve OpenAI's proof of the propeller conjecture of Khot and Naor from 2008: the sum of the squared lengths of the Gaussian moments of any partition of Euclidean space is at most $9/(8π)$. We show equality only occurs for three 120 degree sectors in the plane (up to symmetries, measure zero changes, and taking orthogonal cross products with Euclidean space). We also remove computer assistance from the three-dimensional case of the conjecture, which previously used an epsilon net traversal.
Spin Toda systems and N-point spherical Whittaker functions

We define and study a spin version of the open Toda integrable system, using the Iwasawa decomposition of a connected split real Lie group. We study spherical Whittaker functions as solutions of the spin Toda system. We also construct their N-point version and find the corresponding factorisation of the Casimir element, which yields asymptotic boundary KZB type equations.
Covariance-Informed Ensemble Score Filtering: Embedding Localized Covariance Geometry into Score-Based Transport
Siming Liang; Peter Jan van Leeuwen; Hristo G. Chipilski; Zezhong Zhang; Feng Bao; Guannan Zhang

Background-error covariance models are central to atmospheric data assimilation because they spread partial observational information across space, variables, and dynamically coupled scales. Ensemble and variational methods exploit this covariance geometry efficiently, but their standard analysis formulations are largely built around Gaussian or locally quadratic approximations. Score-based ensemble filtering provides a framework for nonlinear distributional transport, but existing Ensemble Score Filter (EnSF) formulations lack an intrinsic covariance-mediated pathway for propagating likelihood information from observed to unobserved state components. We introduce a covariance-informed ensemble score filter (CI-EnSF) that embeds localized forecast-error covariance geometry directly into the forward diffusion and reverse transport. The proposed forward diffusion is covariance-shaped in standardized state space and becomes isotropic under the corresponding control-variable transformation. This covariance structure continuously propagates observational information from observed to unobserved state components throughout the reverse transport analysis trajectory. Experiments with Lorenz-96 and surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) dynamics show a clear regime dependence. For linear observations, a well-tuned LETKF is more accurate, while CI-EnSF maintains stable cycling and effective covariance-mediated information propagation. Under strongly nonlinear observations and under climatological initialization, CI-EnSF achieves lower analysis error and greater cycling robustness than Gaussian ensemble benchmarks such as the LETKF, with improvements extending across spatial scales in the nonlinear SQG experiment. These results suggest that the principal benefit of CI-EnSF arises from combining nonlinear distributional transport with the mature covariance geometry used in conventional data assimilation.
Implicit Neural Representations for Variational Problems on Graphons
Taeyoung Kim; Jineon Baek; Joonkyung Lee; Hongseok Yang

We propose a neural exploratory framework for variational problems over graphons, i.e., symmetric measurable functions $[0,1]^2 \to [0,1]$, that arise as limits of dense graph sequences. Such problems are central to two parts of the mathematical literature: extremal graph theory, which studies graph parameter optimisation under given restrictions, often for those graphs with a large number of vertices, and the large deviation theory of dense random graphs, which characterises the structure of rare events through constrained graphon optimisation. We represent graphons by implicit neural networks and optimise graphon objectives by gradient descent. Our design combines three ingredients: a multi-scale sinusoidal residual architecture biased toward sharp, step-like graphons; an embedded solver that enforces a single empirical density constraint and is differentiated by implicit differentiation; and symmetry-aware Monte Carlo estimators. On generalised Turán problems that previously required substantial human effort, our framework rediscovers known optimal graphons without human intervention. Applied to open instances, it produces candidate optima, including a previously unreported family of extremal structures. Applied to the variational problems from the large deviation theory of Erdős--Rényi random graphs, the framework produces new candidate optimal graphons across both upper- and lower-tail regimes for multiple pattern graphs; for the case of the triangle graph and the upper-tail regime, these candidates improve upon the best-known reference construction of Lubetzky and Zhao. The structures found by our framework have also led to new theorems on the optimal graphons for both families of problems.
Linear Stability and a Turning Point Principle for Barotropic Liquid Stars with a Free Boundary in General Relativity

We study the linear stability of spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat steady states of the Einstein-Euler system describing a liquid star surrounded by vacuum. The equation of state has positive surface density, positive causal sound speed, and an asymptotically linear high-density limit. We construct the equilibrium family and derive the linearized equation with a Robin boundary condition. The linearized operator has discrete real spectrum, and its negative Morse index equals the number of growing modes. We prove that the linearized operator around steady states with large central redshift admits a growing mode, while such growing modes do not exist for steady states with small central redshift. A parameter derivative of the equilibrium family provides a regular interior zero solution of the linearized equation, whose boundary defect is a nonzero multiple of the parameter derivative of the total mass. This gives a turning point principle: the kernel is one-dimensional precisely at mass critical points, and the sign of the crossing eigenvalue is determined by the bending of the mass-radius curve.
Graph distance and percolation dimension of three-dimensional Brownian motion

We prove that the minimum Hausdorff dimension of a continuous curve joining $W_0$ to $W_1$ within the range $W([0,1])$ of a three-dimensional Brownian motion is almost surely a deterministic constant $γ_3\in(1,5/3]$. Moreover, we construct continuum many simple curves with pairwise distinct images that attain this minimum. Each curve has box dimension $γ_3$ and admits a parametrization that is $β$-Hölder for every $0<β<1/γ_3$. To identify $γ_3$, we partition Brownian time into $n$ equal intervals and form a graph by joining pairs with intersecting ranges. We show that its endpoint graph distance and diameter have a common deterministic almost sure growth exponent $θ$ and that $γ_3=2θ$. We also establish $n^{pθ+o(1)}$ growth for their $p$-th moments, for every $p>0$.
Divisorial ideals and $v$-class semigroups of strictly closed domains

We study divisorial ideals and the $v$-class semigroup of a Noetherian domain satisfying Serre's condition $(S_2)$. We prove that strict closedness is equivalent to Clifford $v$-regularity and describe the structure of the associated $v$-class semigroup. We use these results to characterize finite generation of the class semigroup and Boole $v$-regularity. We also construct prime ideal decompositions of integrally closed divisorial ideals and clarify the relationship between these decompositions and local Boole $v$-regularity. Finally, we study polynomial extensions and use them to construct Boole $v$-regular and locally Boole $v$-regular domains in arbitrary dimension.
Dirac eigenvalues and the hyper-hemispherical radius

On a connected compact Riemannian spin manifold with boundary, we prove an upper estimate for the smallest eigenvalue of the Dirac operator under the boundary condition associated with a chirality operator. This upper bound is expressed in terms of the hyper-hemispherical radius. Moreover, the upper bound is realized if and only if the manifold is a hemisphere. As an application, we get a scalar curvature rigidity result for the hemisphere in the case of Lipschitz maps whose differential has a prescribed trace-norm bound. Our estimate extends Bär's result for closed manifolds, where the upper bound is given in terms of hyperspherical radius.
Minimal Surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with Three Planar Ends II: Symmetry and Nonexistence

In this paper, we study complete minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with three embedded planar ends parallel to those of the union of the Lagrangian catenoid and the plane containing its waist circle. We prove that no such complete embedded minimal surface of genus $g\geq 2$ with finite total curvature admits at least $4(g+1)$ symmetries. This contrasts sharply with the genus-one case, where highly symmetric examples do exist and are uniquely determined up to scaling and rigid motion.
Timed Recovery Safe Gradient Flows for Constrained Nonlinear Programming
Tianxi Luo; Yue Wu; Fei Chen; Hongsheng Qi

This paper studies how to relax pointwise feasibility in continuous-time dynamics for inequality-constrained nonlinear programming while retaining a quantitative feasible-recovery guarantee. Existing safe gradient flows enforce forward invariance of the feasible set, which yields an anytime-feasible dynamics but can be overly restrictive for optimization because it suppresses transient infeasible motion that may be essential for effective descent. To address this limitation, we propose a timed recovery safe gradient flow that replaces pointwise feasibility with fixed-horizon feasible recovery. The proposed construction augments the state with a timer that records the elapsed infeasible duration and computes a minimum-norm correction to the nominal gradient flow through a pointwise convex quadratic program. We show that the resulting augmented safe set is forward invariant and that every trajectory initialized from the feasible set returns to it within every time window of length \(τ\). We further show that, in a strict interior inactive regime, the closed-loop dynamics reduces exactly to the nominal gradient flow and recovers the corresponding local convergence behavior. Numerical examples illustrate how the recovery horizon shapes the closed-loop behavior and corroborate the theoretical analysis.
Pinned configuration sets and slicing theorems via Fourier integral operators
Allan Greenleaf; Eyvindur Ari Palsson; Minh-Quy Pham; Georgios Psaromiligkos

Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_X}$ and $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_Y}$ be open, where $d_X,d_Y\geq2$ and $1\leq p\leq\min\{d_X,d_Y\}$. Let $Φ:X\times Y\to\mathbb R^p$ be a smooth mapping, and suppose that $D_xΦ$ and $D_yΦ$ have rank $p$. For compact sets $A\subset X$ and $B\subset Y$, we give lower bounds on $\dim_H A+\dim_H B$ ensuring that the pinned configuration set \[Δ_Φ^y(A)=\{Φ(x,y):x\in A\}\] has positive Lebesgue measure or nonempty interior for some $y\in B$. The dimensional thresholds are expressed in terms of uniform $L^2$-Sobolev estimates for the generalized Radon transforms associated with $Φ$. Our results extend the Fourier integral operator approach developed by Greenleaf, Iosevich, and Taylor for unpinned $2$-point configuration problems to the pinned setting. We also prove a nonlinear projection theorem that remains valid even when the Peres-Schlag transversality condition fails. Under the smoothing hypotheses used for the pinned configuration theorem, we obtain lower bounds for the Hausdorff dimensions of the corresponding slices of $A$ by the level sets of $Φ$. Applications include distances from points to hyperplanes, spheres and lines; multiparameter distance sets; and a restricted projection family introduced by Harris.
The number of Tverberg partitions beyond prime powers
Matija Blagojević; Pavle V. M. Blagojević

Sierksma's conjecture asserts that every affine map $a\colonΔ_{(d+1)(r-1)}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^d$ has at least $((r-1)!)^d$ unordered Tverberg partitions into $r$ parts. Until now, lower bounds growing with $d$ were known only when $r$ is a prime power. As one of our main results we prove that for every integer $r\geq3$, every decomposition $r=kq+s$ into $q=p^α$ a prime power, $k\geq1$ and $s\geq0$, and every affine map $a$, the number $\operatorname{Tv}(a)$ of unordered Tverberg partitions satisfies \[ \operatorname{Tv}(a)\ \geq\ \frac{q}{r!}\,\Big(\frac{q}{α+1}\Big)^{\big\lceil\frac{(r-1-2s)(d+1)}{2}\big\rceil}. \]
Well-posedness for $p(x)$-Laplacian parabolic equations under a multiple-regime setting on an annulus
Yitian Wang; Runzhang Xu; Chao Yang

This paper proposes an energy-variational framework for the well-posedness of the initial boundary value problem of the parabolic equation with variable exponents on an annulus, under the multiple-regime setting consisting of the subcritical, critical and supercritical regimes of the variable exponents. The multiple-regime setting leads to the appearance of the critical and supercritical regions of positive measure, which cause the failure of the classical Sobolev embedding and the lack of compactness. To address the challenges posed by multiple regimes to well-posedness within the energy framework, we recover the compact Sobolev embedding for a class of radially symmetric functions by the Strauss inequality and obtain the local existence of the solution via the combination of the subdifferential technique and the Principle of Symmetric Criticality for any given radially symmetric initial data. Additionally, the uniqueness result is also given with the recovered Sobolev embedding.
