Compact stencil RKDG, introduced by Chen et al. in [15], is a variant of standard RKDG method which is known for its smaller stencil size and parallel efficiency. The main challenge is that the cRKDG method has to be expressed in Butcher form and not every Runge-Kutta method of this form is a convex combination of forward-Euler steps. Therefore, in order to establish this property we leverage the bound preserving framework of the cRKDG schemes [8], an entropy bounded limiter [6] and the classical positivity preserving limiter. In the last section numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the robustness of the method.
Optimal Multitask Representations Under a Rate Constraint: An Information Bottleneck Analysis

Which pretraining objective yields the best representation for downstream tasks under an information budget? We formalize this problem as a multitask information bottleneck, using a mutual information constraint to model incomplete information retention. For Gaussian inputs and tasks, we characterize optimal representations and show that a weakly task-aligned specialist can outperform a reconstruction generalist at low rates but lose at high rates. We also construct task families for which every fixed Gaussian prediction objective incurs arbitrarily large relative regret, driven by reversals in optimal allocation priorities. Conversely, the average task information matrix defines an objective with a uniform relative-regret bound controlled by maximum task SNR. CelebA and dSprites experiments illustrate that compression can change which pretraining objective performs best, and even task-aware training can reverse which downstream task is better preserved as rate increases.
Discovery of Singularities in Partial Differential Equations Using Adaptive Numerical Discretizations
Allen Yang; Lucas Amoudruz; Petros Koumoutsakos

We compute self-similar singularity profiles of partial differential equations (PDEs) using adaptive numerical discretizations based on optimizing a discrete loss (ODIL). The fields are represented in overlapping local Chebyshev patches joined with a mapped asymptotic patch. After factoring out the leading power laws of solution ansatzes, their limiting amplitudes at infinity are determined by the optimization, eliminating domain truncation and prescribed far-field conditions. Adaptive refinement is guided by Chebyshev-coefficient decay, and the nonlinear least-squares problem is solved using automatically differentiated Gauss--Newton iterations with Levenberg--Marquardt damping. The method achieves O(10^{-14})-level accuracy for Burgers profiles, residuals of O(10^{-14}) to O(10^{-10}) for the generalized De Gregorio family, and of O(10^{-8}) in a local region for the two-dimensional Boussinesq equations. These results demonstrate that ODIL can identify singularity profiles for PDEs with high accuracy using adaptive numerical methods, complementing ongoing efforts that rely on artificial intelligence.
A note on the proof of Barnette's conjecture

Barnette's conjecture states that every cubic 3-connected bipartite planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. We present a digested exposition of OpenAI's generated proof of Barnette's conjecture \cite{openai-barnette}.
Comb Tensor Network Finite-Difference Time-Domain Algorithms for 2D and 3D Electromagnetic Simulations
Jonathan Tabares; Erika Ye; Yang Liu

This paper presents efficient 2D and 3D finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithms augmented by the comb tensor network (CTN) representation of the field and auxiliary quantities. The proposed CTN-FDTD algorithm leverages superior compressibility of CTN compared with quantized tensor train (QTT), and rank-reduction strategies including local and global smoothing techniques to achieve logarithmic memory requirement and computation (per time step) cost. Numerical examples validate these complexities and demonstrate the applicability of CTN-FDTD using a variety of source excitation, frequency and permittivity profiles in both 2D and 3D. Remarkably, CTN-FDTD can simulate 35 trillion spatial grid points in 3D with low memory and computation costs on one computation node, whereas standard FDTD would require 281 TB memory to store each of its 31 3D arrays. Moreover, CTN-FDTD was applied to realistic 2D photonic crystal structure simulation with one million grid points and 3D scattering analysis with 8.6 billion grid points.
Finiteness theorems for Cayley permutation classes

We prove that every hereditary Cayley permutation class with finitely many simple members has a finite basis and an algebraic generating function. We first show that every simple Cayley permutation of length at least two contains a simple pattern obtained by deleting one or two letters, and that the only exceptional Cayley permutations are the simple parallel alternations and their symmetries. We then characterize substitution-closed classes by the simplicity of their basis elements and show that classes with finitely many simple members are partially well ordered. Given the simple members and the basis of such a class, we construct a finite system of functional equations and compute an annihilating polynomial.
Petar Bakić; Wee Teck Gan; Gordan Savin

We study the exceptional theta correspondence for dual pairs of the form $\SL_3\times G$ inside $p$-adic groups of type $E_n$, $n=6,7,8$. We establish Howe duality for lifts of all Whittaker-generic unitarizable representations of $\SL_3$. Our dual pair is in a see-saw relationship with a dual pair of the form $G_2 \times H$ such that $G/H$ is a rank-two symmetric space. Using the theta correspondence for $\SL_3 \times G$, we prove a multiplicity-one result for $H$-invariant functionals on representations of $G$.
An explicit elementary proof of no Landau--Siegel zeros

We give an elementary proof of the absence of Landau--Siegel zeros with the explicit constant $c=1/100$. For every primitive quadratic Dirichlet character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge3$, each real zero $β\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,χ)$ satisfies $(1-β)\log q>c$. The proof combines integer coefficient counting, polynomial congruences, a paired-tail hyperbola estimate, and a logarithmically weighted comparison of positive sums. All required constants are explicit, and one choice of parameters covers every conductor. The argument uses elementary arithmetic and real summation and integration, without separate zero computations for small conductors.
Normal Matrix Model and Hyperelliptic Curves

We present a two-matrix model with a normal matrix with eigenvalues confined to contours in the upper half plane coupled to a Hermitian matrix. This generalizes the matrix model proposed by Jens Hoppe which corresponds to a single horizontal line. We solve the saddle point equations for several lines and show that the large-N free energy can be expressed in terms of hyperelliptic integrals. We show that the model describes a Coulomb gas in the presence of an infinite conducting boundary.
Classification of compatible left-symmetric conformal algebras on solvable Lie conformal algebras of rank two

In this paper, we give a complete classification of compatible left-symmetric conformal algebra structures on solvable Lie conformal algebras which are free of rank two as $\mathbb{C}[\partial]$-modules up to isomorphism. We obtain ten mutually non-isomorphic normal-form types and determine the precise equivalence relations among the parameters within each family. Moreover, we also characterize the Novikov conformal algebras among the classified left-symmetric conformal algebras, thereby obtaining a complete classification of compatible Novikov conformal algebra structures in the same setting.
Conformal geodesics and the hyperboloid at timelike infinity
Achilleas V. Koukas; Mariem Magdy; Juan A. Valiente Kroon

A description of scattering in asymptotically flat spacetimes that includes both radiation and massive asymptotic states requires control of the relation between null and timelike infinity. Motivated by this problem, we use the properties of conformal geodesics to construct an extended representation of timelike infinity in Minkowski spacetime. The construction exploits the fact that every non-null metric geodesic in an Einstein spacetime is, up to an explicit local reparametrisation, a conformal geodesic. It replaces the point $i^+$ by a hyperboloidal boundary $\mathcal{H}^+$ meeting future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ at a corner $\mathcal{C}^{+}$, while fixing the location of $\mathscr{I}^+$ in the associated conformal Gaussian gauge. In this gauge, we derive the equations governing massless scalar and spin-$2$ fields. In particular, we obtain a transport equation for the scalar field along future null infinity and analyse the asymptotic behaviour of its spherical-harmonic modes near timelike infinity. We also derive the explicit massless spin-$2$ equations in this gauge. Finally, we examine the relation to projective extensions and to the hyperbolic base of the extended Carrollian space $\mathrm{Ti}$. Our results provide a geometric framework for studying the connection between late-time and null asymptotics which is a prerequisite for scattering constructions relevant to flat space holography.
A smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres with Bernoulli geodesic flow
Keith Burns; Tomas Gedeon; Yuping Ruan
We construct a smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres whose geodesic flow is Bernoulli with respect to the Liouville measure.
Local Optimality of the d-cube for Laplacian Eigenvalues

For each $d \ge 2$ we prove that the unit $d$-cube $\square_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is, on the class $\mathcal{P}$ of convex polytopes combinatorially equivalent to a $d$-cube, (i) a strict local minimizer of the scale-invariant isoperimetric ratio $I(Ω) = \tfrac{P(Ω)^d}{|Ω|^{d-1}}$, with $P$ the perimeter, (ii) a strict local minimizer of the volume-normalized first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\barλ(Ω) = |Ω|^{2/d}λ_1(Ω)$, and (iii) a strict local maximizer of the volume-normalized first Neumann eigenvalue $\barμ(Ω) = |Ω|^{2/d}μ_1(Ω)$. The method is a shape-derivative Hessian analysis adapted to the hyperoctahedral symmetry of the cube. In symmetry-adapted coordinates on the parameter space --- the decomposition into irreducible representations of the hyperoctahedral group --- each Hessian is block-diagonal, with four scalar eigenvalues, which we give in closed form in $π$, rational coefficients, and a few universal series-constants. The first Neumann eigenvalue is not differentiable at $\square_d$, since its lowest cluster splits under perturbation. The Neumann case therefore works with a smooth auxiliary functional, whose Hessian is computed by second-order perturbation theory of the cluster; the coupling to modes outside the cluster enters at the same order. Finally, we show that extremality of $I$, $\barλ$, and $\barμ$ does not hold in high dimensions for a particular multilinear perturbation that leaves $\mathcal{P}$ by breaking convexity. All results are local; we discuss why a global statement, available for quadrilaterals (Endo and Osting, 2026), appears out of reach for $d \ge 3$.
Fefferman--Chang-type atomic decompositions for product Hardy spaces associated with Schrödinger operators

We establish a geometric (Fefferman--Chang-type) atomic characterization of the two-parameter Hardy space associated with a pair of Schrödinger operators $L_i=-Δ+V_i$ on $\mathbb R^{n_i}$, $i=1,2$. The space is defined by the product conical square function. We assume comparability of neighbouring covering cubes, a local bound on the potentials, and decay of the semigroup mass at large scales. We prove that the Hardy norm is equivalent to a sum of classical local product Hardy norms at scales determined by the adapted coverings. This localization formula yields an atomic decomposition whose atoms satisfy size and partial cancellation conditions, with cancellation required only below the corresponding local scales. Both the atoms and their rectangular components remain supported inside fixed enlargements of the covering rectangles. The proof combines one-parameter Schrödinger Hardy space characterizations with standard vector-valued arguments and a localized product atomic decomposition with uniform control of scales and supports. The assumptions cover the model case of reverse Hölder potentials $V\in RH_q$, $q>n/2$, as well as potentials outside every $RH_q$ class, $q>1$, including half-space indicators and exponential potentials.
Polynomial pathwidth for graphs vertex-coverable by few shortest paths and algorithms for quasi-shortest path covers
Li-Hsuan Chen; Florent Foucaud; Ling-Ju Hung; Ralf Klasing; Lucas Lorieau; Peter Rossmanith

We study how covering a graph by a small number of shortest or approximately shortest paths/walks constrains its treewidth and pathwidth. A path or walk is $(α,β)$-quasi-shortest for $α\geq1$ and $β\geq 0$ if each contiguous segment has length at most $α$ times the distance between its endpoints plus $β$. For graphs vertex-covered by $k$ shortest paths, we establish the first known polynomial pathwidth bound of $O(k^3)$. For edge-coverage, we improve the previously known $O(k^4)$ upper bound to $O(k^2\log k)$. As a main ingredient of the proofs, we first show that if the vertices of a graph can be covered by $k$ $(α,β)$-quasi-shortest paths or walks, then its treewidth is $O_{α,β}(k^2)$; this is a consequence of the fact that such graphs have linear metric growth and the technique developed in [Campbell et al., E-JC 2023]. To obtain the above pathwidth upper bounds, we combine this result with techniques from the literature in a nontrivial way. On the other hand, we show that there exist connected bipartite cubic graph whose edges can be covered by $k$ shortest paths and whose pathwidth is $Ω(k\log k)$, providing the first superlinear lower bound. For graphs covered by $k=2$ $(α,0)$-quasi-shortest paths with $α>1$, we show that, unlike treewidth and unlike the case $α=1$ and $β=0$ of exact shortest paths, the pathwidth may be unbounded. Finally, for every fixed rationals $α\geq1$ and $β\geq 0$, we give XP algorithms with a running time of $n^{f(k,α,β)}$ for some function~$f$ that decide whether the vertices of a graph can be covered by at most $k$ $(α,β)$-quasi-shortest paths or walks. The algorithms combine our treewidth upper bounds with an algorithmic meta-theorem from [Dreier et al., LICS 2025]. [abstract shortened to meet the arXiv requirements]
Energy-rate equidistribution for adaptive SSAV--BDF2 integration of gradient flows

We develop an adaptive time-stepping strategy for scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) schemes combined with variable-step BDF2 discretization for gradient flows. The strategy selects step sizes based on the instantaneous energy dissipation rate and enforces monotonicity of a computable symmetric energy through a step rejection mechanism. We show that the step-size rules used in practice correspond to equidistributing a monitor function along the energy curve, connecting energy-adaptive time stepping to the classical theory of r-adaptive mesh methods. The monitor $g = |\dot{E}|$ is asymptotically optimal as it minimises the leading-order maximum symmetric-energy discrepancy for a given number of steps. A combined monitor that switches to $g = \sqrt{|\dot{E}|}$ near equilibrium caps step growth without degrading this error bound. The arclength parameter $β$ used in prior work is shown to be the ratio of the largest permitted step to the energy-error tolerance. The controller is paired with the SSAV--BDF2 discretization. Accepted steps satisfy monotonicity of the symmetric energy, from which we deduce a bound on the physical energy that is uniform in the number of steps, $\sup_n E(u^n) \le E(u^{0}) + τ_1 + O(Δt_{\max}^2)$, and the scheme achieves second-order global accuracy under standard step-ratio restrictions. Numerical experiments on Cahn--Hilliard, Ohta--Kawasaki, Phase--Field Crystal, and functionalized Cahn--Hilliard models confirm the theory and demonstrate the method's efficiency.

It is known, by works of Werner and Carneiro, that the type theory of Lean (and indeed of CIC plus a version of choice) is equiconsistent with ZFC plus "there are infinitely many strongly inaccessible cardinals". We prove a finer connection between these two formal systems; namely, given any formula in the language of second order arithmetic, that formula is provable in the aforementioned extension of ZFC if and only if the same formula, when viewed as a type in Lean, is inhabited.
A remoteness formula for generalized Wythoff games

Smith's remoteness function records how long an impartial game lasts when the winner wins as quickly as possible and the loser delays defeat. For the generalized Wythoff game $\mathrm{WYT}(a,b)$, in which two positive integer parameters $a$ and $b$ determine which simultaneous removals from the two piles are allowed, we give a formula for the remoteness of every position, building on the known values at losing positions. The formula depends on two indices: a local index determined by the coordinates of the losing positions in a window of length $b$ ending at the smaller pile, and the integer part of the pile difference divided by $a$. When $b=1$, complementary Beatty sequences make the local index explicit, which gives an explicit formula for $\mathrm{WYT}(a,1)$, including classical Wythoff's game. We also show that if each attempted move in a finite impartial game independently fails with a fixed probability and passes the turn, the probability that the player to move wins under optimal play is an explicit exponential function of remoteness. For every success probability strictly between $0$ and $1$, the optimal attempts are exactly the moves that reduce remoteness by one.
Injectivity and continuity of the intersection form in infinite type

We study two fundamental properties of the intersection pairing between geodesic currents on infinite-type surfaces which are classical in the finite-type closed setting: injectivity of the marked length spectrum and continuity of the intersection form. We show that geodesic currents on infinite-type surfaces of the first kind are determined by their intersection numbers with closed curves, extending Otal's marked length spectrum rigidity argument from finite-type to infinite-type surfaces. In contrast, we prove that the intersection pairing is not continuous in general for the natural topologies by constructing explicit counterexamples. We then prove sufficient criteria for continuity of intersection numbers for infinite-type surfaces.
New criteria for upper bounds on the number of limit cycles in Liénard systems
Chen Cao; Hebai Chen; Yilei Tang

We establish criteria for at most one or at most two limit cycles of generalized Liénard systems in a single potential well. Two independent uniqueness tests use modified quotients of the damping and restoring forces; both allow a degenerate restoring force, and one extends to continuous potential profiles with corners. Opposite convexity of the two branches of the damping quotient in the potential coordinate gives an upper bound of two. Further criteria apply to weak damping with an analytic normalized profile on a bounded potential interval under an explicit smallness condition, to small profile perturbations vanishing near the equilibrium on a bounded range of half-widths, and to parameter families satisfying curvature, monotonicity and boundary conditions. Applications give another proof of the classical quartic bound. For Selkov systems, we obtain a two-cycle bound in a specified negative-parameter region and prove existence and uniqueness in a positive-parameter region. We also prove Conjecture~2.1 in [J. Math. Anal. Appl., 2025]. Examples attain the two-cycle bound.
The Serrin exponent for Lane-Emden inequalities driven by sums of fractional p-Laplacians
Leandro M. Del Pezzo; Bryan Pichucho; Alexander Quaas

We study positive weak super-solutions of the Lane-Emden inequality $\mathcal{L}u := \sum_{i=1}^{n}(-Δ_{p_i})^{s_i}u \ge u^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, where each $(-Δ_{p_i})^{s_i}$ is a fractional $p_i$-Laplacian of order $s_i\in(0,1]$ and exponent $p_i\in(1,\infty)$, and $\max_i s_ip_i<N$. Let $κ_i := (N-s_ip_i)/(p_i-1)$ be the decay exponent of the fundamental solution of the $i$-th operator, and let $\overlineκ := \max_iκ_i$. We show that the Serrin exponent of $\mathcal{L}$ is $\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}} = N/\overlineκ$. More precisely, for $0<q<\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}}$ the only non-negative continuous weak super-solution is $u\equiv 0$, while for every $q>\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}}$ we construct explicit positive weak super-solutions of the form $A(λ+|x|)^{-κ}$. In other words, the Serrin exponent of the sum is the smallest of the Serrin exponents $N/κ_i$ of the single operators, that is, the one of the operator whose fundamental solution decays fastest. No structural assumption relating the different operators is needed. The endpoint $q=\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}}$ is left open. The local order $s_i=1$ is treated together with the nonlocal orders, and all the arguments are carried out in the weak setting.
Outage Analysis and Bilevel Resource Optimization in RIS-Assisted Clustered UAV-NOMA Networks
Masoud Ghazikor; Ly V. Nguyen; Morteza Hashemi

This paper investigates RIS-assisted downlink UAV communications based on NOMA. Since conventional NOMA becomes difficult to scale as the number of UAVs grows, we develop a cluster-based UAV-NOMA framework in which a BS serves multiple UAV groups with the aid of partitionable RISs. Within this framework, we consider direct, RIS-only indirect, and composite links, and develop an analytical model for the received SNR and outage performance under Nakagami-$m$ and double Nakagami-$m$ fading with imperfect SIC. To enable scalable transmission, we introduce a greedy RIS-aware (GRIS) clustering method, which groups UAVs according to spatial and channel-related features. Based on the resulting clusters and RIS assignment, we formulate an efficiency-reliability bilevel optimization problem that jointly optimizes inter-cluster BS power allocation, intra-cluster NOMA power coefficients, and RIS element assignment. Specifically, the outer efficiency problem maximizes the average throughput across clusters, while the inner reliability problem minimizes the worst-UAV outage probability within each cluster. To solve the formulated problem, we propose a two-level iterative framework consisting of an inter-cluster outer-efficiency solver (IOS) and an intra-cluster inner-reliability solver (I2S), where I2S combines a grid-based progressive search (GPS) for NOMA power refinement with reliability-guided RIS element reassignment, and IOS updates the BS power weights. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of GRIS clustering, while pre-optimization analysis reveals efficiency-reliability trade-offs in power allocation. Baseline comparisons illustrate the ability of IOS-I2S to balance efficiency and reliability, while ablation studies highlight the importance of joint optimization.
The symplectic leaves of the affine Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme associated with a singular subalgebroid

Every singular subalgebroid, and in particular every singular foliation $\mathscr{G}$, determines a universal Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$, which is the analogue of the linear Poisson structure on the dual of a Lie algebroid. We show that the underlying space $X_{\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G})}$ of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$ decomposes as a disjoint union of symplectic manifolds. Furthermore, we extend the Helffer-Nourrigat cone to a singular subalgebroid and show that it is an embedded Poisson $C^\infty$-subscheme of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$.
Robust topology optimization of isogeometric Kirchhoff--Love shells by the Speed Method
Philipp Eisenhardt; Fernando Hübner Scherer; Barbara Wohlmuth; Andrei Constantinescu

This paper presents a framework for robust topology optimization of Kirchhoff-Love (KL) multi-patch shells using isogeometric analysis and non-matching meshes and provides a CAD-compatible method. The material distribution is optimized via a NURBS-based level set method, enabling accurate boundary representation and seamless export to standard CAD/CAM workflows. The shape derivative is computed using the speed method, yielding a volume-based formulation that avoids boundary approximations and aligns with the isogeometric principle of coarse, high-order discretizations. This eliminates the need for local refinement, adaptive quadrature, or trimming as the descent direction for the compliance and volume objectives are obtained through a biharmonic equation. The framework is extended to robust optimization under uncertainty, accounting for stochastic loading and material properties via Monte Carlo sampling and Gaussian Random Fields. Numerical examples demonstrate the method's efficiency and robustness across single- and multi-patch shells, reproducing literature results with fewer elements than traditional FEM or refined IGA approaches. The developed methods and tools can be directly extended to problems involving stress-based optimization and risk-averse metrics. The numerical implementations are open-source and available on GitHub.
A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions
Qian Zhang; Shanqing Liu; Jerome Darbon; George Karniadakis

We address the problem of real-time multi-agent path planning under prescribed initial and final configurations, formulated as a high-dimensional optimal control problem subject to inter-agent collision avoidance and obstacle constraints. Classical solvers based on the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation or Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) become computationally intractable as the number of agents grows, due to the curse of dimensionality and the non-convexity introduced by interaction constraints. We propose OCFormer, a transformer-based neural network that parameterizes the inverse of a coordinate transformation mapping a simple, analytically tractable latent space, in which agents evolve independently under a decoupled Hamiltonian, to the physical space of the coupled, interacting system. The model is trained by minimizing a physics-informed loss comprising the Hamiltonian ODE residual from the PMP and a boundary matching term, without requiring pre-computed trajectory data. The self-attention mechanism endows OCFormer with permutation equivariance over agents, a structural symmetry that prior symplectic network approaches do not natively enforce. When trained on a distribution of boundary conditions, the amortized OCFormer produces near-optimal trajectories for unseen initial and final configurations in a single forward pass ($\sim$220ms), enabling real-time inference without retraining. We further introduce a lightweight transfer learning framework that adapts a pretrained OCFormer to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds via L-BFGS fine-tuning. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional multi-agent navigation with up to 128 agents demonstrate the scalability and efficiency of the proposed approach.

We prove that every complex finite-dimensional simple binary Lie superalgebra with non-zero odd part is either a simple Lie superalgebra, and hence is one of the superalgebras of Kac's list, or the two-dimensional non-Lie superalgebra $B_2$. This confirms the Grishkov--Shestakov conjecture and, together with the theorems of Grishkov and Filippov on simple binary Lie algebras, gives the answer to Shestakov's question from the Dniester Notebook (Problem 3.100(d)) over the field of complex numbers.
Bayesian Fixed-Confidence Best-Arm Identification with Abstention
Yuqi Huang; Yunlong Hou; Vincent Y. F. Tan

We study the Bayesian fixed-confidence best-arm identification problem in which a learner can abstain from making a terminal recommendation. Subject to a target error probability $δ$ and an abstention budget $α$, we propose Screen-and-Confirm (S&C) and analyze its expected stopping time. We further derive the minimum expected stopping time for any algorithm that satisfies these constraints. For Gaussian priors and rewards, as $(δ,α)\downarrow(0,0)$, we establish matching upper and lower bounds up to multiplicative constants, with rate $κ_ν^2[1+\log((α+δ)/δ)]/(α+δ)$, where $κ_ν$ is the prior density of the top-two gap at zero, highlighting that nearly tied instances govern the sampling cost. When abstention is disallowed ($α=0$), S&C yields the optimal $Θ(1/δ)$ dependence for fixed model parameters, removing the additional $\log(1/δ)$ factor in the upper bound of Jang et al. (2024) under our Gaussian assumptions. We further characterize the exact multiplicative constant of the minimum expected stopping time for practical regimes including (i) fixed $α\in (0,1)$ and (ii) $α/δ\to\infty$, which are also achieved by S&C.
The longest increasing subsequences of Luce permutations and permutons

We investigate the longest increasing subsequences (LIS) of random permutations distributed under the Luce model with weights $θ_1^{(n)} \ge \ldots \ge θ_n^{(n)}$. Our first main result provides a general formula for the growth rate of the LIS. For example, we get that the LIS of Luce permutations with Sukhatme weights $θ_k^{(n)} = n-k+1$ grows like $\sqrt{n}$. We also give simple conditions for the LIS to be of order $n^β$, for any given $β\in[1/2,1)$. Our second main result states that, if the weights are of the form $θ_k^{(n)} = f\big( (k-1)/n \big)$ for a sufficiently regular function $f$, then the LIS divided by $2\sqrt{n}$ converges in probability to a constant $K(f)$ described by a variational problem. Throughout, we make extensive use of coupling techniques; in particular, to prove our second main result, we argue that Luce random permutations behave similarly to random permutations sampled from the ``Luce permuton''.
Source integrability and the frontier $α=\tfrac12$ in time-fractional diffusion
Edison A. Vásquez-Martínez; Mauricio A. Londoño-Arboleda

Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, let $α\in(0,1)$, and let $\partial_{t}^α$ denote the Caputo derivative. For $\partial_{t}^αu-\nabla\cdot\bigl(A(x)\nabla u\bigr)=f$ with homogeneous Dirichlet condition and initial datum $g\in L^{2}(Ω)$, we identify which of the thresholds appearing in the energy method belong to the method and which to the equation. We compare $f\in L^{2}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$ and $f\in L^{r}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$ with $r>2/α$; in the subdiffusive range the second implies the first and not conversely. Existence is not at issue and we claim none of it: it is known, for both hypotheses and under weaker ones, from the work of Zacher. What we determine is the exact set of exponents each route admits and what the exponents left outside it cost. Under the weaker hypothesis the construction below reaches $α\in(\frac12,1)$, under the stronger one every $α\in(0,1)$, and in both cases the solution lies in $L^{\infty}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$, by the mode representation and not by the energy route, which yields no such bound under the weaker hypothesis. The restriction $α>\frac12$ comes from the compactness criterion, whose admissible exponents form $[1,2α)$; the exponent $r>2/α$ is exactly what the Grönwall step consumes. A concentrating family shows that nothing weaker suffices along that route, and the mode representation lowers the requirement to $1/α$. The frontier $α=\frac12$ belongs to the equation: for every $α\in(0,\frac12]$ there is $f\in L^{2}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$ whose weak solution leaves $L^{\infty}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$. Uniqueness and Hadamard well-posedness follow.

We construct and describe the moduli stack $\mathrm{Isog}$ of isogenies between oriented elliptic curves. We show that $\mathrm{Isog}$ is a spectral Deligne-Mumford stack and a relative spectral algebraic space over $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}}^{\mathrm{or}}$, and give a fiber product decomposition of $\mathrm{Isog}$ corresponding to a connected-étale factorization on oriented elliptic curves. In the process of proving these results, we construct a theory of duality and quotients for spectral abelian varieties, prove a higher-algebraic version of Nakayama's lemma, and lift the rigidity theorem for morphisms of elliptic curves to the setting of spectral algebraic geometry.
Asymptotical results on the automorphism groups of canonical double cover of graphs
Bartłomiej Bychawski; Ademir Hujdurović; Đorđe Mitrović; Gabriel Verret

The canonical double cover $BX$ of a graph $X$ is the direct product $X\times K_2$. A graph $X$ is stable if every automorphism of $BX$ is induced by automorphisms of $X$ and $K_2$, and unstable otherwise. We prove several asymptotic results on stable and unstable graphs. In particular, we show that the automorphism group of the canonical double cover of almost every graph has order $2$, and consequently that almost all graphs are stable. We also prove that the dominant sources of instability are having twins and being disconnected, in that order, and that graphs arising from a known construction are the next step in this hierarchy.
Permutation classes need not have proper growth rates

By the Marcus-Tardos Theorem (formerly the Stanley-Wilf Conjecture), every permutation class other than the class of all permutations has a finite upper growth rate, meaning that the $n$th root of the number of permutations of length $n$ in the class has a finite limit superior. It has long been conjectured that this limit superior is in fact always a proper limit. We disprove this by constructing a permutation class whose upper and lower growth rates differ. The construction uses grid classes with cubic row-column graphs of increasing girth, obtained from Haar graphs of finite 2-groups. The corresponding hereditary property of ordered graphs also disproves an analogous 2006 conjecture of Balogh, Bollobás, and Morris. Along the way, we show that every proper permutation class with a D-finite generating function has a proper growth rate. We also establish refined enumerative bounds for grid classes, which lead to a short proof of Albert and Vatter's generalization of Bevan's Theorem on the growth rates of grid classes.
Relative Hitchin fibrations and endoscopy for Unitary Friedberg--Jacquet varieties

We prove a relative fundamental lemma for the unitary symmetric variety $GL_n(k')\backslash U_{2n}$, proving a conjecture of Leslie, Xiao, and Zhang. Our proof reduces to the Lie algebra and argues over function fields in positive characteristic, using methods from Ngo-Laumon and Ngo. In particular, we reinterpret orbital integrals in terms of the cohomology of relative affine Springer fibers and globalize this using unitary versions of Hitchin moduli spaces for symmetric pairs via a product formula. As the main global input, we prove a matching of perverse sheaves between relative Hitchin moduli spaces and their corresponding endoscopic variants.
The Porous Medium Equation and Convexity

We show that root convexity of the pressure is preserved by the porous medium equation if the initial data is root convex, positive, smooth, bounded below by a quadratic function and has bounded Laplacian. This complements a result of Daskalopoulos-Hamilton-Lee on root concavity of pressure.
A unified variational framework for augmented Lagrangian preconditioning of saddle point systems: applications to mixed-dimensional and fictitious domain methods
Michele Benzi; Marco Feder; Luca Heltai; Federica Mugnaioni

We present a general framework to derive augmented Lagrangian preconditioners for saddle point systems arising from mixed finite element discretizations. Our approach is based on augmenting the variational formulation at the continuous level prior to discretization, providing a unified strategy for designing efficient preconditioners that are robust under mesh refinement for a broad class of problems leading to symmetric saddle point systems. The robustness of the proposed preconditioners is established through a detailed spectral analysis. This framework is applied to different model problems, focusing on mixed-dimensional and fictitious domain formulations involving Lagrange multipliers, with some configurations featuring large coefficient jumps. Extensive numerical experiments on different test cases and geometries are presented, validating the effectiveness and robustness of our preconditioners when used in conjunction with flexible GMRES.
Partial Breakdown of Integrability in Nearly Integrable Systems

We study the persistence of integrable structures in real-analytic nearly integrable systems under perturbations that may destroy some, but not all, of these structures. Specifically, we establish upper bounds on the numbers of real-analytic first integrals -- quantities conserved by the motion -- and commuting vector fields -- infinitesimal generators of continuous symmetries -- that can persist under the perturbation. These bounds are expressed in terms of Melnikov-type functions, which quantify the breakdown of the corresponding integrable structures. Unlike classical Melnikov theory, our conditions occur even in the absence of zeros of the Melnikov functions, so they do not necessarily imply the existence of homoclinic tangles. We give a geometric interpretation of these conditions in the context of the Arnold diffusion problem, showing that they imply micro-diffusion. We also obtain a criterion for higher-dimensional nearly integrable systems in which the dimension of the span of the Melnikov vectors restricts the numbers of possible first integrals and commuting vector fields. This shows that the geometry of the Melnikov vectors provides a new mechanism for detecting the breakdown of integrability. We give several applications to integrable Hamiltonian systems subject to forcing and dissipation.
Optimal CLT error bounds in the second order Wasserstein metric via Stein's method for weakly dependent sequences

We use Stein's method to prove general upper bounds on the second order Wasserstein distance in the CLT for general dependent partial sums $S_N=X_1+\ldots +X_N$. Then we use these estimates to provide optimal $O(N^{-1/2})$ rates for a variety of chaotic dynamical systems and $ϕ$- and $ψ$-mixing sequences. Our results for $ψ$-mixing sequences are obtained under the fourth moment condition, which matches the best known results in the iid case. This is the first time that optimal CLT rates of any kind are obtained for unbounded weakly stationary variables under general mixing conditions. We then apply this result and obtain optimal CLT rates $O\left((\text{Var}(S_N))^{-1/2}\right)$ for non-stationary $ψ$-mixing sequences without any growth rates on $\text{Var}(S_N)$. We also obtain close to optimal CLT rates for nonconventional sums and some classes of random dynamical systems with non-uniform decay of correlations
On the Adversarial Vulnerability of Neural Receivers with Unrolled LDPC Decoders
Aakash Saini; Jafar Aco Mohammadi; Wolfgang Gerstacker

Neural receivers for 5G New Radio (NR) match classical model-based receivers in link-level performance, but their robustness to adversarial perturbations at the receiver input remains underexplored. We show that standard gradient-based attacks applied end-to-end through an unrolled low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoder fail to significantly outperform a matched-power Gaussian perturbation. We identify the failure as gradient masking caused by tanh saturation in the boxplus operation of the belief-propagation (BP) check-node update, with a per-iteration gradient norm decay of more than four orders of magnitude across ten unrolled BP iterations. Based on this finding, we propose two structurally independent loss functions that restore attack efficacy. L_BP routes the gradient through the unsaturated early iterations via per-iteration supervision, while L_LLR is a margin loss on pre-decoder log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) whose gradient bypasses the LDPC decoder entirely. Both loss functions increase the block-error rate (BLER) by one to four orders of magnitude at matched perturbation power, with the results reproduced on both the Sionna NeuralReceiver and DeepRx. At low PSR, L_LLR-optimized perturbations achieve up to three orders of magnitude higher BLER on unseen channel realizations than LBP-optimized perturbations.
A note on functional non-central limit theorem for periodic regime-switching stable-like processes

In this paper, we establish a functional non-central limit theorem for regime-switching stable-like processes with periodic coefficients. Our approach relies on stochastic analysis methods, in particular semimartingale characteristics, combined with the ergodic theory of Markov processes. If the set on which the order function achieves its minimum value $\underlineα$ has positive Lebesgue measure, then the limit is a rotationally invariant $\underlineα$-stable Lévy process. Otherwise, the limit is the zero process.
Simultaneous popular polynomial differences in higher dimensions

We extend the simultaneous popular polynomial difference theorem of Conlon, Dong, and the author to polynomial shifts along prescribed directions in $\mathbb{F}_p^D$. Let $P_1,\ldots,P_k\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be linearly independent polynomials with zero constant terms, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_k\in\mathbb{Z}^D\setminus\{0\}$. We show that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently large prime $p$, and every $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^D$ of density $α$, there exists a nonzero $d\in\mathbb{F}_p$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}_{\underline{x}\in\mathbb{F}_p^D} \mathbf{1}_A(\underline{x}) \prod_{\substack{1\leq i\leq k\\ ω_i=1}} \mathbf{1}_A\bigl(\underline{x}+P_i(d)v_i\bigr) \geq α^{\,1+\sum_{i=1}^kω_i}-\varepsilon \] simultaneously for every $ω\in\{0,1\}^k$. The main new ingredient is a directional arithmetic regularity decomposition adapted to mixed directional box norms.
Finite time implosions of the multidimensional compressible Euler equations with a finite far-field cutoff
Jack Luong; Reed Spitzer; Scott D. Ramsey; Andrea L. Bertozzi; Roy Baty

We study the problem of finite time singularities in the isentropic compressible Euler equations in multiple dimensions with radial symmetry. Our initial data consists of the radially symmetric Kidder self-similar implosion with a continuous constant density cutoff. Motivated by our recent work on the one-dimensional problem, we present high-resolution radially symmetric adaptive mesh refinement simulations that when combined with asymptotic similarity solution analysis present a full picture of the ensuing dynamics of the implosion. From the cutoff point in the initial data, an expanding wave emerges. The endpoints of the wave follow the "imploding" and "exploding" characteristic speeds associated with the system of hyperbolic conservation laws. This wave has much more complex structure than the exact non-centered rarefaction wave that emerges in the one-dimensional problem. As in the one-dimensional case, the inner Kidder solution is swallowed up by the expanding wave as time approaches the singularity time. However, unlike the one-dimensional case, a blowup occurs along the point where the `imploding' side of the expanding wave attaches to the Kidder solution. This composite blowup has an asymptotic self-similar form that has an interpretation in terms of the Gurderley-type self-similarity structure. The numerical method for the PDE necessitates a Lagrangian scheme to avoid the numerical diffusion inherent in Eulerian methods. We use a leapfrog method coupled to recursive refinement of the mesh near the blowup, which allows for very high resolution simulations, resolving many orders of magnitude of the self-similar blowup. Consistent with prior rigorous results for these equations, the blowup does not involve mass concentration and exhibits a critical $L^p$ space for the concentration of the density, depending on the dimension of space.
Scattering of plane waves and a modified Pompeiu criterion

In this paper we prove that plane waves always scatter from bounded, strictly convex planar inhomogeneities with constant material parameters. Our approach involves the introduction of a modified Pompeiu property, whose failure corresponds to the vanishing of the Fourier transform of the indicator function of the inhomogeneity on a complexified circle not centered at the origin. We then show that such vanishing is impossible for bounded, strictly convex planar sets.
Covering lemmas associated to maximal operators of weak type
Paul Hagelstein; Fedor Nazarov; Blanca Radillo-Murguia

Building on the work of A. Córdoba and R. Fefferman, we provide a necessary and sufficient covering condition on a basis $\mathcal{B}$ on a separable metric space $X$ with a Borel measure $μ$ so that the associated \mbox{geometric} maximal operator $M_\mathcal{B}$ satisfies for all $α> 0$ the weak type estimate $$μ\left(\left\{x \in X : M_\mathcal{B}f(x) > α\right\}\right) \leq \int_{X}Φ\left( γ_\mathcal{B} \left|\frac{f}α\right|\right)\,dμ\;,$$ where $Φ: [0, \infty) \rightarrow [0, \infty)$ is an everywhere finite Young's function.
Dynamic Active Fleet Sizing of Heterogeneous UAV Relays for Post-Disaster Communication Networks

Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems are increasingly used to provide temporary connectivity when ground communication infrastructure is damaged by disasters such as hurricanes and wildfires. However, the amount of aerial support required changes as ground networks recover and communication demand evolves. We focus on dynamically adjusting the number and allocation of actively deployed UAVs within a fixed available fleet. We develop a model predictive control (MPC) framework for dynamic fleet sizing of heterogeneous UAV relays during post-disaster communication recovery. The framework accounts for communication demand, ground network recovery, heterogeneous UAV operation, UAV energy availability, and backhaul capacity, which limits how much relayed traffic can be transmitted to the external communication network. The resulting formulation is a convex quadratic program that supports efficient online fleet sizing and deployment decisions. We evaluate the framework using seven historical disaster recovery case studies based on Federal Communications Commission reports, together with four backhaul scenarios and sensitivity analyses. Results show that required active UAV fleet size varies considerably throughout recovery, while backhaul capacity and fleet composition affect communication performance, highlighting the value of adapting active fleet size over time.
Rational limit of Rains integrals of type $A_n$

We deduce the rational analogue of the elliptic Rains identity of type $A_n$ arXiv:0309252. We also derive reductions of the rational analogue and present the connection of them with well-known integrals in literature.
Automorphisms of Twisted Chevalley Groups over Commutative Rings
Elena I. Bunina; Deep H. Makadiya

We classify all abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full twisted Chevalley groups of types ${}^2A_\ell$ ($\ell\geq3$), ${}^2D_\ell$ ($\ell\geq4$), ${}^2E_6$, and ${}^3D_4$ over arbitrary commutative rings, for every invariant isogeny type. The coefficient automorphism $θ$ has order dividing that of the diagram automorphism. We assume that $2$ is invertible and, for triality, that $3$ is invertible as well. Three features distinguish the answer from the usual inner--diagonal and coefficient decomposition. The elementary groups of types ${}^2A_3$ and ${}^2A_4$ admit an additive family of exceptional automorphisms supported at $θ$-fixed maximal ideals with residue field $\mathbb F_3$. In type ${}^2D_4$, diagram automorphisms may vary on idempotent components, subject to compatibility with the involution and the isogeny lattice. In triality, the coefficient automorphisms preserve the trace operator $r\mapsto r+θ(r)+θ^2(r)$ but need not commute with $θ$. We determine which elementary automorphisms extend to the full groups and describe the remaining central factors. A nonzero exceptional unitary factor extends precisely in the simply connected type ${}^2A_3$, giving a classification for the hyperbolic group $\operatorname{SU}_4(R,θ;Q_4)$. The proof glues uniquely determined normalization data for a finite root frame and then recovers the coefficient action from root-subgroup relations.
Matrix-Free Local Multigrid for $C^1$ Hermite Discretizations on GPUs

I present a matrix-free local multigrid method for $C^1$ tensor-product Hermite discretizations on adaptively refined Cartesian meshes, using the clamped biharmonic problem as the model problem. Extending a cell-wise primal-dual formulation to Hermite elements, I enforce continuity through a constraint operator that is never formed. At refinement edges, geometric prolongation supplies both the trace and its normal derivative, so the local V-cycle needs no edge operator and no hanging-node machinery. For the cubic element, an even-odd decomposition based on the signed reflection symmetry of the Hermite basis, applied along two axes, splits the element matrix into four dense $16\times16$ blocks and reaches 85% of peak memory bandwidth. Chebyshev-Jacobi and vertex-patch smoothers both preserve conformity by construction. In three dimensions on one NVIDIA A100 in double precision, conjugate gradients preconditioned by the Chebyshev-Jacobi V-cycle need five or six iterations on uniform meshes and solve at up to 4.23 million cells per second. On locally refined meshes the count rises to at most sixteen, ordered by the fraction of cells on a refinement edge and nearly equal for both smoothers.
Structure-Preserving Dimension Reduction and Surrogates for Partially Linear Bayesian Inverse Problems
Ziheng Zhang; Dingcheng Luo; Thomas O'Leary-Roseberry; Umberto Villa; Omar Ghattas

Many Bayesian inverse problems are characterized by two parameter vectors with distinct roles. A medium property, operator coefficient, or geometry block enters the forward model nonlinearly, whereas a volumetric, initial condition, or boundary condition source enters linearly. General-purpose nonlinear surrogates must relearn this known source dependence from data and may not preserve the correct source scaling outside the training regime. We introduce a structure-preserving partially linear (SPPL) framework that constructs separate reduced spaces for outputs, (linearly appearing) sources, and (nonlinearly appearing) medium variables and represents the reduced forward map as an affine function of the retained source coordinates, with coefficients that depend on the medium variables. Here, "affine" refers to the retained, mean-centered source coordinates: the physical forward map remains linear in the source, while the affine offset is induced by the source-prior mean and vanishes when that mean is zero. The analysis first identifies the optimal blockwise ridge approximation and then derives the optimal affine-in-source approximation under independent medium and source priors. A direct decomposition of the forward error into output, source, medium, and surrogate contributions yields blockwise spectral criteria and prior-predictive expected-KL control. For a Gaussian source prior, the optimal affine-in-source approximation coincides with the optimal blockwise ridge approximation. In a coseismic numerical example, a three-model controlled ablation on common block-reduced coordinates separates the effects of coefficient-matrix supervision and structure-preserving affine-in-source parameterization. Reduced-space surrogate MCMC provides orders-of-magnitude online acceleration relative to high-fidelity posterior sampling.
On Borodin-Gorin presentation of Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function

We prove that Borodin-Gorin presentation for Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function by interlacing integrals is equivalent to two other integral presentations studied in arXiv:2508.18864. We also consider related Baxter operators and the corresponding limiting procedure from the Ruijsenaars hyperbolic model.
Continuous-time analysis and algorithms for linear and convex quadratic programs via exactly solvable differential inclusions
Gabriel P. Langlois; Akwum Onwunta; Jérôme Darbon

Linear and convex quadratic programs are fundamental problems in optimization. While many methods have been developed for solving these programs in large-scale applications, to our knowledge none have attempted to solve their continuous-time gradient flow, a differential inclusion, in full generality without assumptions beyond feasibility. Recent work solved the gradient flows in two special cases, basis pursuit and the lasso, and obtained competitive algorithms. Motivated by these results, we solve the general case exactly. Using the minimal selection principle for monotone differential inclusions, we show that the trajectory of the gradient flow consists of finitely many pieces, each obtained from one nonnegative least-squares problem. Its final piece yields an optimal solution or a certificate of unboundedness. This analysis leads to two algorithms. The first algorithm is exact, terminates after finitely many steps, and applies to linear programs and projections onto polyhedra. The second algorithm, which we call minimal selection descent, discretizes the gradient flow for general convex quadratic programs. Its iterates converge to an optimal solution when one exists and otherwise certify unboundedness. We apply both algorithms to a positivity-preserving limiter for a discontinuous Galerkin scheme and to optimal control problems for the Poisson and heat equations. In the limiter, the first algorithm conserves the total mass more accurately than the state-of-the-art Douglas--Rachford splitting method. On the control problems, minimal selection descent reaches the optimal value to machine precision and is competitive in time with commercial and open-source solvers.

For a graph $G$, let $\text{cg}(G)$ be the maximum $k\in \mathbb N$ for which $G$ contains a $k$-vertex cograph as an induced subgraph. The Erdős-Hajnal conjecture asserts that for every proper hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$, there exists $γ\in(0,1]$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G\in\mathcal{G}$ satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n^γ$. This is still open; however, for some hereditary classes, one may guarantee much stronger bounds. For instance, every chordal graph $G$ on $n\geq 2$ vertices satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n/(2\log n)$. Paul Seymour asked whether this bound is optimal up to a constant factor. We answer this affirmatively, even for interval graphs: For every integer $n\geq 2$, we construct an $n$-vertex interval graph $G$ with $\text{cg}(G)<64n/\log n$.
Generalized Images for Brownian First Passage to Monomial Boundaries

We study the first passage of Brownian motion to a monomial moving boundary. For every integer degree at least two, we construct a time-independent signed image measure whose heat potential is the killed Brownian transition density on a nonzero interval of the natural Brownian time scale. The image density is determined by a second-kind Volterra equation in the image coordinate, not by the classical Volterra equations in time for the hitting density. Its kernel is an explicit Wright function, and the first-passage density is recovered afterwards from the boundary flux. Exponential bounds establish convergence, while a beta-moment transform connects the Wright kernel with the finite-order differential hierarchy previously obtained from transported moving zeros. A cubic numerical experiment independently checks the resulting density against simulated Brownian paths.
Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
Niklas Garner; Martijn Kool; Jan Manschot; Yuuji Tanaka

These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. The lectures centred around algebraic structures arising from twists of supersymmetric quantum field theories, correlation functions of topologically twisted supersymmetric gauge theories, and their mathematical counterparts as intersection-theoretic invariants associated to moduli spaces of instantons, semistable sheaves, or Higgs sheaves on four-manifolds or complex projective surfaces.

We give a matroid-theoretic analogue of Gaussian elimination and use it to construct, for every matroid M, the syzygy matroid Syz(M) on the collection of circuits of M. Dualizing the construction yields the combinatorial adjoint Adj(M) on the collection of maximal proper flats of M, and the two are related by Adj(M) \simeq Syz(M*). Neither construction depends on a realization. We determine Syz(M) when M is U_{k,k+3} or the Vamos matroid V_{8}. We also show that Adj(M) is an adjoint of M when M has rank 3. When M has rank 4 and V_{8} is a restriction of M, Adj(M) has rank 3 and is not an adjoint of M.
Global well-posedness for the modified dispersion-generalized Benjamin-Ono equations
Mikaela Baldasso; Simão Correia; Thyago S. R. Santos

In this short note, we prove the global well-posedness of the modified dispersion-generalized Benjamin-Ono equation with dispersion $1<α<2$, $$\partial_t u + D^α\partial_x u + u^2\partial_x u=0,$$ over the Sobolev space $H^s(\mathbb{R})$, for any regularity $s$ greater or equal than the sharp analytic well-posedness regularity. As a byproduct, we also derive nonlinear smoothing estimates and give a simple proof of local well-posedness.
Denominators of Hodge integrals and Minkowski numbers

We prove that the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals is the Minkowski number $T_{2g}$ or, equivalently, the Bhargava factorial $(2g+1)!_{\mathbb{P}}$ associated to the set of primes $\mathbb{P}\subset\mathbb{N}$. As a corollary, we prove a conjecture of Liu-Xu on the multiplicity of $3$ in the least common denominators of certain descendant integrals, and generalise their result on a conjecture of Itzykson-Zuber to Hodge integrals with $λ$ classes. Namely, the order of the automorphism group of any pointed stable curve of genus $g'\le g$ divides the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals. We also comment on the use of generative AI via IMProofBench, which played a fruitful part in the development of this (entirely human-written) paper.
Summation-by-parts operators for general function spaces: Flux differencing, entropy stability, and accuracy
Henry M. Haase; Andrew R. Winters; Jan Glaubitz

Summation-by-parts (SBP) operators are a cornerstone of provably stable high-order methods for hyperbolic conservation laws. For nonlinear problems, the flux-differencing framework of Fisher and Carpenter combines such SBP operators with entropy-conservative two-point fluxes to obtain semi-discretizations that are conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff and discretely entropy-conservative or stable. So far, this framework has been developed exclusively for operators that are exact for polynomials. Function-space SBP (FSBP) operators lift this restriction by being exact on a general finite-dimensional function space that can be tailored to the problem at hand. In this work, we extend flux differencing to FSBP operators for general (potentially non-polynomial) function spaces. We prove that, whenever the operator has a diagonal norm and its function space contains the constants, the resulting semi-discretization is conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff, semi-discretely entropy-conservative within a single element, and entropy-stable across element interfaces. We also provide the first theoretical accuracy analysis of FSBP operators: We characterize their design order through an algebraic criterion on the underlying function space, prove that suitable non-polynomial spaces achieve the same design order as polynomial spaces of equal dimension, and show that the flux-differencing semi-discretization retains this order. Notably, the entropy-conservative two-point flux is reused unchanged; only the underlying function space differs from the polynomial case. Numerical experiments for the Burgers' equation and the compressible Euler equations in one and two dimensions confirm these properties.
3D de Sitter from complex Virasoro TQFT: Observers and knots
Jeevan Chandra; Diego Liska; Boris Post

The Euclidean saddles of 3D Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant are spherical three-manifolds. When one adds a heavy observer, the backreacted saddles are spherical cone manifolds, with a conical singularity along the observer worldline. We propose exact gravitational partition functions at fixed topology on a class of spherical cone manifolds that undergo hyperbolic-to-spherical transitions as the cone angles increase. Our construction relies on a careful analytic continuation of the product of two Virasoro TQFT partition functions. We test the proposal by showing that the exact partition functions exponentiate in the semiclassical limit to the spherical volume, in agreement with the gravitational on-shell action. This leads to a spherical volume conjecture for the product of continued Virasoro TQFT amplitudes. As further evidence, we relate the theta and tetrahedron graph amplitudes to the two-point function and out-of-time-ordered four-point function of operators on a massive observer's worldline. In appropriate limits, we recover the static patch scalar two-point function with finite observer backreaction and the semiclassical effects of observer recoil. In addition, we analyze examples with knotted worldlines and reproduce their spherical volumes. We also apply our prescription to Seifert manifolds, which are off-shell in AdS$_3$ gravity but admit dS$_3$ saddles, and find agreement with their spherical volumes semiclassically. Finally, using Dehn surgery on torus knots and links, we obtain partition functions on smooth spherical three-manifolds.
Defect flows from functional relations in the asymptotic semiring
Federico Ambrosino; Anatoly Konechny; Ingo Runkel; Gérard M. T. Watts

We study perturbations of topological defects by a relevant holomorphic defect field in two-dimensional conformal field theory. This produces translation invariant defects and these necessarily flow to topological defects in the infrared. Translation invariant defects form a monoidal category which extends the fusion category of topological defects. We argue that the renormalisation group flow defines a semiring homomorphism from the semiring of translation invariant defects to an "asymptotic semiring" which we construct from topological defects. The semiring homomorphism preserves functional relations, and we illustrate in the example of Virasoro minimal models that the resulting relations in the asymptotic semiring constrain the defect flow endpoints. The companion paper [1] contains a detailed study of such defect flows in several minimal models, both numerically and analytically.
DBDSVDMR3: An MRRR-Based Bidiagonal SVD Solver Built from DSTEGR
James Demmel; Inderjit Dhillon; Sai Surya Duvvuri; Julien Langou; Osni Marques; Ryan Schneider

The optimal algorithm for the symmetric tridiagonal eigenvalue problem is Multiple Relatively Robust Representations (MRRR or MR$^3$), which is capable of computing $k$ eigenvalue/eigenvector pairs in only $O(kn)$ floating-point operations. While MRRR is nearly 30 years old, it has never successfully been adapted to the bidiagonal SVD. This is not for lack of trying; two previous attempts produced implementations that were considered for LAPACK but eventually abandoned, a result of the fact that neither was reliable enough when run on test problems. The question therefore remained: is there a problem with the theory of MRRR for the bidiagonal SVD or were there simply bugs in the previous implementations that went undetected? This paper resolves this question by presenting DBDSVDMR3 -- a new implementation of the MRRR-based algorithm for the bidiagonal SVD originally proposed by Willems and Lang [ETNA 2012], which, for the first time, performs well on a variety of test problems while achieving significant speedups over both LAPACK's bisection-based solver and, in certain cases, divide-and-conquer for the bidiagonal SVD (thereby indicating that the theory is sound). DBDSVDMR3 will be available in the next release of LAPACK. In this paper, we discuss the design of our implementation, which was obtained with the help of Claude Code, and exhibit its performance on a diverse set of test problems.
Ergodic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control with Stochastic Coefficients

We investigate ergodic linear-quadratic optimal control problems with stochastic coefficients and introduce the associated stochastic ergodic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, in which the classical ergodic constant is replaced by a random process $λ$. We establish well-posedness of the equation and show that $λ$ characterizes the optimal ergodic costs for a general class of averaging kernels, including those corresponding to normalized finite-horizon and discounted costs. For random-periodic coefficients, we construct a random-periodic solution and show that the optimal ergodic costs associated with all admissible averaging kernels coincide. We also establish stability of the optimal ergodic costs under perturbations of the coefficients.
Relaxation and $Γ$-Convergence of Stretch Energy on Surface Homeomorphisms

Area-preserving parameterization of triangular meshes is an essential task in geometry processing, yet an exactly area-preserving simplicial mapping may not exist in general. In this paper, we study area preservation of simplicial mappings in the limit of mesh refinement by establishing the $Γ$-convergence of the discrete stretch energy, a functional that measures their area distortion. We first introduce its limit functional, the relaxed stretch energy on surface homeomorphisms, defined through the pushforward of the area measure, and show that it is the relaxation of the stretch energy of diffeomorphisms with respect to uniform convergence. Then, to compare simplicial mappings with homeomorphisms, we construct a geometric lift that requires no shape-regularity assumption on the image mesh. Finally, we establish the $Γ$-convergence and show that the minimal discrete energies converge to the continuum minimum. Moreover, any homeomorphism arising as a limit of lifted discrete local minimizers in fixed-radius balls is area-preserving.
Bridge change-of-measure for propagator estimation of diffusions

The propagator of one-dimensional diffusions has relevant applications in statistical inference and across many disciplines. Yet it is obtained in closed form only for very few simple models. Here we analyze an importance sampling strategy based on a bridge change of measure to estimate propagators: paths are generated under an auxiliary diffusion whose bridge between the two fixed boundary points is easy to generate, and the target propagator is recovered through a Radon-Nikodym derivative or likelihood ratio correction derived from Girsanov's theorem. This method overcomes the main limitations of the crude Monte Carlo estimator, which relies on binning in state space, introducing bias and becoming inefficient with rare transitions. We apply the method to a range of benchmark processes and show that the bridge-based estimator matches the accuracy of crude Monte Carlo with orders of magnitude fewer sample paths. Finally, we elaborate on discretization schemes for the Radon-Nikodym derivative and on approximations to the best-in-class change of measure, both of which increase the efficiency of the method.
Finite zero products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols
Youqi Liu; Jie Qin; Sui Huang

We study finite products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Fock space over the complex plane. If every symbol has the form $f+\overline g$, where $f$ and $g$ are entire functions of exponential type, we prove that a finite product vanishes if and only if one symbol vanishes identically. It suffices to test the product on reproducing kernels. The proof represents the product by a two-variable entire function and transforms the equation for a left factor by $\exp(-\partial_z\partial_w)$. A Fock norm identity then permits cancellation of each nonzero factor.
Higher-order tangent and secant numbers, special-value integrals, and a common zero attractor

We study two families of coefficients associated with powers of the tangent function and with products of the secant and tangent functions, and develop a unified treatment of the corresponding higher-order tangent and secant numbers. The first part establishes a common identity for even derivatives of $\tanh x$ and odd derivatives of $\operatorname{sech}x$. Combined with integral formulae for these derivatives, this yields finite power-integral representations for the normalized values $ζ(2n+1)$ and $β(2n)$ and naturally introduces two polynomial families $P_n$ and $Q_n$. We determine several arithmetic and structural properties of these polynomials. In particular, we identify the exact content of $P_n$, prove that $Q_n$ is primitive, establish strict log-concavity and unimodality of their coefficient sequences, and describe their real zeros. For even indices each family has a unique negative real zero, and the two sequences of real zeros have the same limit. We also derive differential recurrences and generating functions for $P_n$ and $Q_n$. The generating functions lead to a global complex-singularity analysis. We construct a compact Jordan curve $Γ$ and prove that the complex zero sets of both $P_n$ and $Q_n$ converge to $Γ$ in Hausdorff distance. The normalized zero-counting measures converge weakly to the same equilibrium measure on $Γ$. We determine the logarithmic capacity of the enclosed compact set, give an explicit arclength density for the limiting measure, and compute its first moments. Numerical plots for $P_{20}$, $P_{50}$, $P_{100}$ and $P_{150}$ illustrate the zero-attractor theorem.
Triple Products of Correlated Multivariate Hermite Polynomials

Stochastic Galerkin schemes (SGS) are used to approximate solutions to differential equations with stochastic parameters. In particular, they express the solution with an infinite orthogonal functional basis of the parameter space and derive a deterministic system of PDEs; the solution of this deterministic system can be used to produce a {surrogate} approximation of the original stochastic equations. When the parameters are correlated, the infinite series representation of the solution does not provably converge for all joint distributions; further, classic decorrelating transformations (e.g., Roseblatt) often introduce known numerical instabilities. Rahman (2017) established convergence in probability and distribution for correlated {Gaussian} parameters when the basis functionals are {multivariate Hermite polynomials} (MHPs), where these polynomials are only {weakly orthogonal} with respect to the underlying joint density. Due to weak orthogonality, the $N$th moments of MHPs introduced during Galerkin projection do not trivially decompose into products of one-dimensional expectations and have no closed-form expression for $N > 2$; consequently, these moments are typically estimated via brute-force sampling and quickly become prohibitively expensive to compute. In this paper, we introduce and prove several foundational results for MHPs. These results culminate in an equation that can be used to calculate the $N = 3$ moments (triple products) exactly, whose implementation dramatically reduces the computational bottleneck otherwise inherent to SGS with correlated Gaussian parameters.
We show that if \((A, τ)\) is a selfless C\(^\ast\)-probability space with \(τ\) being a faithful trace, then commutators are dense in \(\ker τ\).
Differentially Private Synthetic Data via Generalized Moment Matching
Rundong Ding; Yiyun He; Yizhe Zhu

We study $(\varepsilon,δ)$-differentially private synthetic data for arbitrary databases of $n$ records in $[-1,1]^d$ under a specified integral probability metric (IPM). We introduce generalized moment matching, which estimates moments privately, fits a probability measure, and samples synthetic records. A general error theorem applies when moment error controls the target IPM. This framework extends Chebyshev moment matching for $1$-Wasserstein distance and smooth queries. We apply the framework to maximum mean discrepancy with Matern and Laplace kernels and a two-layer ReLU neural tangent kernel. We also obtain guarantees for sliced Wasserstein-$1$ and the IPM induced by norm-bounded ReLU networks. With sufficiently many synthetic records,these rates are minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed dimension.
Alexander Torsion and Floer Comparisons in the BV-BFV Formalism

We compare relative Abelian BF torsion with the Alexander-graded Euler characteristic of knot Floer homology. A meridional annulus boundary condition identifies the normalized relative torsion with the Alexander polynomial. One exact prime-cyclotomic torsion value recovers all its coefficients under a sharp genus bound, compatibly with connected-sum gluing and branched-cover formulas. We compute interface contractions and obstructions to scalar comparisons, including the pairing defect of two-sector reduction for the degree-zero torus algebra. A six-generator dg resolution yields an equivalence of perfect-module categories preserving derived pairings and admits a classical one-dimensional BV-BFV realization. In the fixed nonresonant polynomial quantum BFV sector, over characteristic zero with $\hbar$ inverted, both states and Weyl observables reduce to a vacuum field; a Hochschild invariant obstructs a Morita equivalence with the degree-zero torus algebra. These results do not establish a full geometric BV-BFV/Floer equivalence.
Scaling H2 Factorization to Billion-Unknown Three-Dimensional Problems
Tianyu Liang; Chao Chen; James Demmel; Yang Liu

Strong recursive skeletonization provides approximate direct solvers for dense matrices from integral equations and kernel methods, but distributed implementations face substantial communication costs and limited parallelism, especially in three dimensions. We present a distributed-memory $\mathcal{H}^2$ factorization solver for symmetric matrices that combines spatial box coloring, delayed Schur complement updates, streamed sketching-based interpolative decomposition, and BLAS-3 and shared-memory kernels. Spatial coloring enables every process to participate in each boundary stage, while delayed updates and streamed sketching reduce dense storage and communication. To our knowledge, this is the first distributed-memory strong recursive skeletonization factorization demonstrated for three-dimensional volume integral equations at billion-unknown scale. Experiments on up to 512 compute nodes demonstrate factorization of a three-dimensional Laplace system with 3.62 billion unknowns, alongside three-dimensional Helmholtz tests and a two-dimensional Matérn system with 268 million unknowns. Combining streamed sketching and fully delayed updates reduces factorization time by $6.9\times$ for Laplace and $8.5\times$ for Helmholtz relative to the unsketched, eager configuration, while reducing maximum per-process resident memory by 57\% and 54\%, respectively.

We study the notion of generalized Kahler Bismut--Hermitian--Einstein (GKBHE) manifolds, namely generalized Kähler manifolds for which both Bismut Ricci forms vanish, and we develop a theory for such structures on compact threefolds. We organize the analysis according to the horizontal rank, an invariant taking values in $\{0,1,2\}$ that measures the relative position of the canonical foliations associated with the two Hermitian structures. We characterize the case of horizontal rank $0$ (which corresponds to Kähler Ricci flat geometry) and describe the case of horizontal rank $1$, revealing its close interplay with the steady $ν$-soliton equation in Kähler geometry. This description also provides a tool for constructing new compact GKBHE threefolds.
Temporal Exploration and Rendezvous via Weisfeiler-Leman Colorings
Frank Kammer; Sandra Kiefer; Johannes Meintrup

Temporal graphs are graphs whose edge relation changes in discrete time steps. The Temporal Exploration Problem (TEXP) asks for a temporal walk that visits all vertices. We show that every connected temporal graph with $n$ vertices can be explored in $O(qn\log^3(n))$ time steps, where $q$ is the number of vertex color classes induced by the 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman (2-WL) coloring. For small $q$, our bound substantially improves on the known worst-case bound of $Θ(n^2)$ in general connected temporal graphs. A corresponding walk can be constructed in deterministic polynomial time. The upper bound is complemented by lower bounds of $Ω(n\log(n))$ when $q$ is constant and $Ω(qn)$ when $1 \leq q \leq n$. We also apply our techniques to the Temporal Rendezvous Problem (TRP), in which two agents that do not communicate have to meet on a vertex of the temporal graph. Our exploration algorithm yields that, with only polynomial-time computational power, the agents can meet in $O(n\log^3(n))$ time steps, leaving a gap of only $\log^2(n)$ to the known lower bound. Dogeas, Erlebach, Kammer, Meintrup, and Moses Jr. [ICALP'24] have shown an $O(rn^{1+ε})$ bound for TEXP, for every fixed $ε> 0$, where $r$ is the number of orbits, and an $O(n^{1+ε})$ bound for TRP. Both results require superpolynomial computation time. Our contribution improves upon these results in several ways. First, the dependence on $n$ in the upper bounds on the number of time steps is decreased from $n^{1+ε}$ to $n\log^3(n)$ for both TEXP and TRP. Second, for TEXP, we bound the number of time steps linearly by the parameter q, which is efficiently computable and upper bounded by $r$. Third, we provide novel deterministic polynomial-time algorithms for both TEXP and TRP.

We give an algorithm for computing an $\eps$-approximate fixed point of any $d$-dimensional nonexpansion with respect to the $\ell_\infty$ norm in time $\log(1/\eps)^{O(\log^2 d)}$. At its core, our method uses a boosting argument to geometrically shrink a search region. Among other consequences, our algorithm implies that simple stochastic games can be solved in quasipolynomial time.
Self-normalized Bernstein Inequalities for Regenerative Processes and Applications to Learning Without Independence

We prove a self-normalized Bernstein inequality for bounded functions of a regenerative process with independent, identically distributed marked cycles of finite mean length. The bound uses observed cycle lengths and retains explicit terms for truncation and the cycle ending after the observation horizon. Selecting a tuning parameter from a finite deterministic collection gives a version of Bernstein inequality where all terms are empirical but one, related to the tails of the regeneration times. We then study this term in many regimes: it turns out that it is of second-order in many cases of interest. This is important for applications in machine learning: we prove generalization error bounds for classification with non-i.i.d., regenerative data.
