Particles carry a smooth core of compact support whose field outside four core radii is exactly the singular Biot-Savart field, so the multipole far field of the treecode carries no regularization error. The subfilter closure is a dynamic eddy viscosity on a fixed filter width, applied by core spreading with a Lagrangian exchange of its local excess under an explicit stability bound, and the strengths are relaxed by projection; global corrections make both the exchange and the relaxation conserve total vorticity and linear impulse. All rotor models shed connected bound circulation, the disks along the arcs swept in each step however long, so the wake receives the lift impulse. The solver agrees with direct summation to $5\times 10^{-7}$ and converges at third order in time. Without calibration, an actuator-line model that includes its own near sheet predicts the hover thrust of a DJI 9443 propeller within 2%. With calibrated section polars it reproduces a Crazyflie propeller's thrust and torque within 3.2% at three speeds and the near wake of a hovering quadrotor with relative $L^2$ differences of 0.08-0.21 against particle image velocimetry, while the wake keeps the delivered impulse. A closed-loop formation of 100 quadrotors, run at a coarser setting on one GPU, illustrates the coupled method at swarm scale.
Time-asymptotic stability of generic Riemann solutions for viscous-dispersive heat-conducting compressible fluids

We establish the time-asymptotic stability of generic Riemann solutions for the one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg (NSFK) system, which describes the dynamics of viscous, heat-conducting, compressible fluids with internal capillarity. We prove that, for the adiabatic exponent $γ\in(1,2]$, the solution to the NSFK system converges uniformly in space, as time tends to infinity, to a composite wave consisting of a rarefaction wave, a viscous contact wave, and a viscous-dispersive shock with a time-dependent shift, provided that the initial perturbation and the strengths of the contact wave and the shock are sufficiently small. In particular, we do not impose any smallness condition on the strength of the rarefaction wave. Because of the capillarity, the shock is viscous-dispersive and its profile equation is of third order. We treat the shock by the method of $a$-contraction with shifts introduced by Kang and Vasseur. This is the first result on the time-asymptotic stability of a viscous-dispersive shock, and of a generic Riemann solution, for the NSFK system.
Regularity and $v$-number of syzygies of graded maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules

Let $A=Q/(\mathbf f)$, where $Q$ is a polynomial ring over an infinite field $k$ and $\mathbf f=f_1,\ldots,f_c$ is a homogeneous $Q$-regular sequence. For $1\leq j\leq c$, set $w_j=\operatorname{deg}(f_j)>0.$ Let $M$ be a finitely generated graded $A$-module of infinite projective dimension. Set $M_i=\operatorname{Syz}_i^A(M)$. We prove that, for each $l\in\{0,1\}$, the sets $\operatorname{Ass}_A(M_{2i+l})$ eventually stabilize, and that $\operatorname{reg}(M_{2i+l})$ is eventually bounded above and below by linear polynomials. If $w_j=w$ for all $1\leq j\leq c$, then the functions $i\longmapsto \operatorname{reg}(M_{2i+l})$, $i\longmapsto v(M_{2i+l}),$ and $i\longmapsto v_{\mathfrak p}(M_{2i+l}),\, \mathfrak p\in\mathcal A_l,$ are eventually linear with leading coefficient $w$, where $\mathcal A_l$ denotes the stable set of associated primes.
Spatial preferential attachment models: robustness revisited

We investigate robustness under percolation in the degree-driven spatial preferential attachment model. Consider a profile that is regularly varying with exponent $-δ$, where $δ>1$, and an attachment rule with asymptotic slope $γ\in(0,1)$. Jacob and Mörters (Ann. Probab. 45 (2017)) proved robustness when $$ δ\left(\frac1γ-1\right)<1. $$ We prove the converse in the strict regime: if $$ δ\left(\frac1γ-1\right)>1, $$ then sufficiently strong Bernoulli vertex thinning destroys the giant component. In particular, the strict robustness boundary coincides with that of the age-dependent random connection model.
Finite-Shift Inverse-Concavity and Exterior Noncollapsing for Fully Nonlinear Curvature Flows of Nonconvex Hypersurfaces

We give a finite negative-shift criterion for preserving a prescribed exterior noncollapsing bound under fully nonlinear curvature flows whose hypersurfaces need not be convex. The criterion uses the optimized two-point expression of Andrews and Langford. We verify it by a uniform global two-matrix estimate for the explicit speed \[ F_{\varepsilon}(A)= tr A- \varepsilon\frac{\norm{A^{\circ}}^{2}}{ tr A} \] on the open cone \[ Γ=\{A\in\Sym(n): tr A>0, \norm{A^{\circ}}< tr A\}.\] Here $A^\circ$ denotes the trace-free part of $A$. This cone contains the positive cone and also matrices with a negative eigenvalue, while the displayed speed is concave and non-convex. For an explicit range of parameters depending on the initial exterior bound, the cone and that bound are preserved throughout the smooth embedded existence interval. Together with the known interior estimate for concave speeds, this gives two-sided tangent-ball bounds for this nonlinear family, including closed nonconvex initial hypersurfaces.
The Kemper--Malle conjecture and isolated linear quotient singularities

We prove the Kemper--Malle conjecture, which provides a modular analogue of the Chevalley--Shephard--Todd theorem. As a consequence, the classification of isolated linear quotient singularities over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic reduces to the classical Zassenhaus--Vincent--Wolf classification.
Permutations, Pattern Covers, Posets and Positivity: Part I: Patterns and Posets
Natasha Blitvić; Mohammed Slim Kammoun; Einar Steingrímsson

We study permutations covered by overlapping occurrences of a consecutive pattern. Special cases of this have been studied for consecutive patterns and via the cluster method. We study enumeration sequences obtained by repeating a fixed overlap. We elicit many structural properties of such pattern covers, mainly in terms of posets whose linear extensions are in bijection with the permutations in question. The enumeration of these permutations for different patterns gives rise to a great variety of sequences, many classical, but most of them not found in the OEIS. We conjecture that, essentially, all these sequences are moments of probability measures on the real line. We develop an enumerative and order-theoretic framework for this. For overlap 1 we give a generating function whose coefficients enumerate permutations covered by any fixed pattern with any fixed number of occurrences. For overlap at most half the pattern length we derive a polynomial-time enumeration formula. We associate to each pattern, overlap, and number of occurrences a poset whose linear extensions are the corresponding permutations. The regularity of this poset construction makes possible a structural analysis that in many cases leads to enumerative formulas for large classes of patterns. We prove uniform restrictions on the local structure of the Hasse diagrams, describe their branches (pendant chains) in terms of the corresponding patterns, and characterize when the poset is a tree or chain or subdivisions of a grid. Some of these constructions yield explicit families of formulas and explain unexpected equinumerations. In a forthcoming paper we investigate the sequences arising here from a probabilistic perspective, viewing them both as point processes and as moment sequences. We also obtain integral and matrix representations for important overlap 1 and 2 classes of pattern-covering sequences.
Explicit finite size corrections for Toeplitz determinants and rectangular domino tilings

Finite Toeplitz truncation does not, in general, preserve multiplication. For products of $m$ $N\times N$ tridiagonal Toeplitz matrices with symbols $z+z^{-1}+a_h$, we make the two boundary corrections in Widom's product formula for finite sections explicit. The method of images gives two Hankel corrections when $m\le N+2$, a sharp uniform degree bound. For $N\ge m-1$, the ratio of the determinant of the matrix product to the Toeplitz determinant with the product symbol reduces, whenever defined, to a determinant of order $2(m-1)$, which reversal symmetry splits into two determinants of order $m-1$. A rectangular Schur polynomial gives an exact formula for the Toeplitz determinant with the product symbol, including when roots coincide. For symbols nonzero on the unit circle, classical identities for rational symbols give an exact $m\times m$ determinant formula for the ratio, with an explicit confluent form for repeated roots. With $ρ_h$ the zero of $z+z^{-1}+a_h$ in $|z|<1$, the limit is $\prod_{i<j}(1-ρ_iρ_j)^2$ as $N\to\infty$ at fixed $m,a_h$. For rectangular domino tilings, these formulas compare the classical Kasteleyn--Temperley--Fisher product with the banded Toeplitz determinant formed from the product symbol. We obtain the first exponentially small correction at fixed width and relate this comparison to the Toeplitz determinant furnished by the dual Cauchy identity.
Rigidity theorems of complete self-shrinkers in the Euclidean space
Zhi Li; Guoxin Wei; Cheng Xing

We classify complete Lagrangian self-shrinking surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant squared norm of the mean curvature vector, without assuming an upper bound for the second fundamental form. Their images are a plane through the origin, the round cylinder $S^1(1)\times \mathbb{R}$, or the Clifford torus $S^1(1)\times S^1(1)$. More generally, a complete self-shrinking surface in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant $|\vec{H}|^2$ is either a plane, a round cylinder, or a complete minimal immersion into $S^3(\sqrt2)$. The proof uses the function $|x|^2-|\vec{H}|^2$, the Bochner formula, and completeness.
Rayleigh's conjecture for vibrating plates: simpler planar proof and nonlinear extensions

We give a simpler proof of Nadirashvili's theorem (Rayleigh's conjecture) that among vibrating clamped plates of prescribed area in the plane, the disk has the lowest fundamental tone. The proof uses a one-shot Talenti type comparison for sign-changing solutions of the Poisson equation with mean-zero data, established in a companion paper. The comparison considers just two rearranged sources, rather than optimizing over all admissible sources as in the traditional two-ball technique. This ``paired comparison'' simplification yields immediate nonlinear extensions: the disk minimizes the clamped quotient $\|Δu\|_q/\|u\|_p$ among bounded open sets of prescribed area, for every $1\le p,q\le\infty$. Equality is characterized for $q>1$, while exceptional behavior at $q=1$ is identified. In higher dimensions, we prove ball minimality for $p=\infty$ and conjecture minimality for all $p,q$ within the compact embedding range. We also establish the corresponding interval inequality in one dimension.
Linear Complementary Pairs of MDS Codes from Elliptic Curves

In this paper, we investigate the Linear Complementary Pairs (LCPs) of Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes that arise from elliptic curves. We establish geometric conditions for LCPs of elliptic codes and prove that they cannot consist entirely of MDS codes when evaluated over all rational points of the curve. To address this, we construct LCPs of MDS elliptic codes by restricting evaluation divisors to subgroup cosets. We apply this method to obtain explicit infinite families of LCPs of MDS codes over Mordell and supersingular elliptic curves, including large-length constructions over quadratic extensions.
The Diophantine Problem with constraints in some free-by-cyclic groups
Laura Ciobanu; Robert D. Gray; Alex Levine

In this paper we explore the Diophantine Problem, that is, the solvability of equations, in one-relator and free-by-cyclic groups, showing that this is decidable in some cases and undecidable otherwise, depending on their abelianisation and centre. In particular, we focus on a version of the Diophantine Problem which asks about the existence of solutions satisfying abelianisation constraints, and prove a number of results concerning the decidability of this problem for free-by-cyclic groups with centre, tree-GBS groups, cyclically pinched groups and the first hydra group.
Numerical Information of Hilbert Space Operators

For a Hilbert space operator $A\in B(H)$, the numerical range map of $A$, denoted $ϕ_A$ is the map sending unit vectors $x$ in $H$ to $\langle Ax,x\rangle$. From this map we define the Numerical Information of $A$, denoted $Σ_A$, which is the sigma algebra induced on the unit sphere by the numerical range map. One of the main results of the paper are that if $A,B\in B(H)$, and $ϕ_B=f\circ ϕ_A$, then $f$ is affine. Our other main result is showing that $Σ_B\subsetΣ_A$ if and only if $B=αRe(A)+βIm(A)+γI$ for some complex numbers $α,β,γ$.
A paintbox characterization of labeled partitions

We study pairs of labeled random partitions $(Π,τ)$ with a finite label set $E$, which can be thought of as a random mutation and coalescence mechanism of a countable number of blocks. Labeled exchangeable partition probability functions (LEPPFs) are defined via labeled analogues of Kingman's paintbox partitions. They satisfy normalization, symmetry and consistency in a multivariate sense. Under an equivariance condition, a representation for $(Π,τ)$ in terms of labeled paintbox partitions is derived, leading to a full characterization of LEPPFs by a unique probability measure $G$. This representation is extended to jointly exchangeable and consistent transition pairs using a product measure $F \otimes G$. These results yield a one-to-one correspondence between distributions of jointly exchangeable and consistent transition pairs and pairs of exchangeable distributions and LEPPFs.
A Super-Convergent Quasi-Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Advection-Diffusion Problems

The aim of the present study is to develop discontinuous Galerkin and nonconforming finite-element methods for solving the 2D advection-diffusion equation. The discrete formulations are stabilized by means of a family of numerical fluxes and the dispersion relations are constructed via a Fourier/stability analysis. The linear discontinuous P1DG and non conforming P1NC Galerkin discretizations are studied. A long time stability result is proven for the P1NC and P1DG schemes and fluxes examined here by inspecting the discrete frequencies, solutions of the dispersion relations. A super-convergent result is also demonstrated for the P1NC discrete frequency (O(h 4 ) accuracy) compared to the P1DG one (O(h 2 ) accuracy). These results are in line with those obtained in a previous paper for the shallow-water system.
Strong Positive Recurrence for Strongly Entropy Expanding Maps

We introduce expanding strong positive recurrence (expanding-SPR) for non-invertible systems with critical points. We then give a sufficient condition for maps to be SPR: strong entropy expansion (SEE). We prove that expanding-SPR implies good thermodynamical properties, including exponential decay of correlations of Hölder observables for the measures of maximal entropy. The class of maps that are SEE includes all C^{\infty}-interval maps with h_{top}(f )>0 and all Viana maps.
The three-colour bipartite Ramsey number of sufficiently long even cycles

For a bipartite graph $H$, let $\operatorname{br}_3(H)$ be the least integer $N$ such that every three-colouring of $K_{N,N}$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$. We prove that $\operatorname{br}_3(C_{2n})=3n$ for all sufficiently large $n$, and give the lower bound for every $n\ge2$. For the upper bound, we reduce a counterexample to a finite rational weighted profile. Cycle extension and vertex-cover arguments force the critical components to have six unique minimum covers which partition the profile. The remaining component supports give a contradiction.
On the maximum length of cyclic MDS codes
Gaojun Luo; Xiwang Cao; Shitao Li; Yang Li

We study the maximum length of nontrivial simple-root cyclic maximum distance separable (MDS) codes over ${\mathbb F}_q$. We prove $n\le q+1$ if $\gcd(n,q^2-1)>2$, or if the dimension is even and $\gcd(n,q^2-1)>1$. The bound also holds for all lengths whose prime factors lie in $\{2,3,5,7\}$. We obtain further cases involving primes $\ell\ge11$ with $(\ell-1)/2$ prime, under conditions on the exponents and the characteristic. The proofs combine Fourier supports, locality bounds and field descent with arithmetic restrictions on multiplicative orders and prime-adic valuations.
A bounded Borel set in the plane none of whose orthogonal projections is Borel
We construct a bounded Borel set in the plane whose orthogonal projection onto every line is non-Borel. This gives a negative answer to a question of Thierry De Pauw.

We study the topological degree on the positive orthant of a map $F:\mathbb{R}^n_{>0}\to\mathbb{R}^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support $\mathcal{A}$ of $N=n+k+1$ monomials. This degree is well defined under a half-space condition on the columns of the coefficient matrix indexed by the faces of the Newton polytope, which holds for generic exponents and coefficients. We give three formulas for it, all in terms of signs of maximal minors. The first one is a Viro formula: the degree is a signed count of the simplices of a regular triangulation of $\mathcal{A}$ which are positively decorated in the sense of Bihan, Santos and Spaenlehauer. The second one is a sum over the facets of the Newton polytope, and the third one a sum over the vertices of the polyhedron of the Gale dual system. As a consequence, the degree only depends on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices restricted to the vertices of the Newton polytope. We also obtain a Descartes rule of signs for the degree and, in the generic case, the upper bound $|°F|<\frac12\min(M(n,N),M(k,N))$, where $M(d,N)$ is the largest number of facets of a $d$-polytope with $N$ vertices. This bound is sharp when $n=2$ or $k=2$. Using the H-duality of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård, we show that the set of possible degrees is symmetric in $n$ and $k$. Since a nonzero degree forces a positive zero, our formulas give sign conditions for the existence of positive solutions, as well as parity statements for their number.
Some Results on the Weight Spectrum of Binary Reed-Muller Codes $RM(m-7,m)$
Zibo Wei; Bo Zhou; Xiao Zhang; Hao Chen

We study the set of weights occurring in the high-order binary Reed-Muller codes $RM(m-7,m)$. For every $m\geq 14$, we prove that the weight spectrum contains all even weights in $[336,2^m-336]$, together with an explicit finite set of low weights and their complements. The proof first establishes the corresponding base-code inclusion in $RM(7,14)$. This base step uses four-block concatenation, explicit degree-six monomial witnesses, and known spectrum inputs for $RM(5,10)$ and $RM(6,12)$. The base inclusion is then lifted to all $m\geq 14$ by a concatenation-based induction. We also analyze the remaining base-code target weights $322,326,330,334$ in several restricted families, including four-block branches, affine-flat and structured inner corrections in a fixed Carlet-type Maiorana-McFarland outer shell, and sparse sums of degree-7 coordinate monomials. The residual analysis delineates several construction routes that cannot yield the four unresolved base-code weights, thereby sharpening the remaining $c=7$ spectrum problem.
In vitro starch digestion kinetic, formal analysis and new kinetic model
Flavien Alonzo; Yuzi Wang; Luc Saulnier; Jean-Philippe Ral; Kamal Kansou

Describing mathematically the kinetics of the enzymatic hydrolysis of starch is a crucial part of nutrition and industrial applications studies. The majority of math models aim to fit the hydrolysis-extent curve ($X\_t$), so-called digestogram, whose simple shape which can be fitted equally well by various math models. A relevant model of starch digestion kinetics should be more specific of the phenomenon. This study proposes a novel analytical framework that jointly fits the hydrolysis-extent curve ($X\_t$) and the instantaneous reaction-rate coefficient ($k\_a(t)$). A large dataset comprising 672 wheat-starch time-course measurements (including normal, waxy, and high-amylose genotypes), and additional experiments on other botanical starches was analysed. Standard First-Order and Weibull models were compared with two newly derived kinetic formulations \eqref{Eq.11} and \eqref{Eq.12} based on expected starch hydrolysis' phenomenon by which $k\_a(t)$ tends with time towards an asymptotic-rate constant value, $k\_e$, following a characteristic relaxation time ($τ$). A mathematical proof of the existence of $k\_e$, specific of the type of starch, is provided, based on an analysis of the Weibull's parameters. Model ability to fit both $X\_t$ and $k\_a(t)$ was assessed by examining coefficients of determination ($R^2$) for both data types, and its adjusted version ($R^2\_{adj}$) was used to compare performances between models. All models fit very well $X\_t$ data, while $k\_a(t)$ is much more discriminant of the model formulation. Wheat starch types are well distinguished, regarding ke, by the new models, with higher susceptibility to amylase for waxy samples ($\approx 5.7\times 10^{-3} min^{-1}$), than normal ($\approx 2.2\times 10^{-3} min^{-1}$) and high-amylose ($\approx 1.7\times 10^{-3} min^{-1}$) ones. The new models outperformed the other models for monotonic evolution of $k\_a(t)$, particularly digestion of high-amylose, and allow a more accurate estimation of $k\_e$. However, the analysis also highlighted limitations for modelling non-monotonic kinetics observed for waxy wheat starch digestion, suggesting a need for more sophisticated differential-equation descriptions for $k\_a(t)$. Overall, the combined fitting strategy provides a robust method for extracting physically meaningful kinetic parameters, facilitating deeper insight into the factors controlling starch digestion and supporting the development of more accurate predictive models for glycaemic response and food processing.
Duality in Harmonic Analysis and beyond
Bartosz Langowski; Mariusz Mirek; James Wright; Błażej Wróbel

In this short note, we develop a duality-based, purely operator-theoretic method for proving several classical maximal inequalities on $L^p$ spaces for $p\in(1,\infty)$. The method applies to maximal ergodic operators, Hardy--Littlewood maximal functions, and maximal Radon averaging operators, and derives their boundedness directly from structural properties of the underlying operators. Further, we show that the same duality principle extends beyond maximal functions. We develop a theory of $r$-variational and jump inequalities for sequences of bounded positive monotone operators on Hilbert spaces, using soft arguments that apply to various classical operators in analysis. In particular, answering a question that had been open for some time, we give direct proofs of $r$-variational and jump inequalities for convolution operators associated with lacunary dilations of smooth bumps on $\mathbb R^d$, completely avoiding any appeal to martingale inequalities.
Gunjan Kumar; Yash Pote; Jonathan Scarlett

In likelihood-free hypothesis testing (LFHT), given samples from two unknown distributions $P,Q$ on $[n]$ with $\mathrm{d_{TV}}(P,Q)\geq\varepsilon$, and from a third distribution $D\in\{P,Q\}$, the goal is to identify whether $D=P$ or $D=Q$. We study asymmetric likelihood-free hypothesis testing, where the sample budgets $s_P$ and $s_Q$ for $P$ and $Q$ may differ, and characterize the feasible triples $(s_P,s_Q,s_D)$ up to logarithmic factors. We establish that unequal reference budgets can give a polynomial saving. For instance, for constant separation, $n$ samples from $P$ and $n^{3/4}$ from $Q$ allow testing with $\widetilde O(n^{1/4})$ samples from $D$, whereas both existing baselines---symmetric LFHT and unequal-sample closeness testing---require $Ω(\sqrt n)$ samples from $D$. We further apply our results to non-adaptive distribution 2-clustering, where the sample allocation among $k$ distributions must be fixed before observing any data. We obtain matching upper and lower bounds for this problem up to logarithmic factors in terms of the domain size, number of distributions, smaller cluster size, and separation, both with one cluster distribution known and with both unknown. Comparing with known bounds for adaptive sample allocation gives a worst-case adaptivity gap of $\widetildeΘ(k^{1/4})$.

Let an isometric involution act on a smooth Riemannian $3$-sphere with sectional curvature at least one. We prove that every one-dimensional connected component of its fixed-point set has length at most $2π$, and that the bound is sharp. The proof realizes the fixed circle as the link of a complete totally geodesic surface in a positively curved expanding Ricci soliton and applies Bishop--Gromov comparison to its area growth. The analytic input is an equivariant version of Deruelle's smoothing of positively curved cones. We use Gianniotis--Schulze's equivariant local deformation and explain a marked compactness argument for arbitrary finite isotropy. In particular, the end chart retains the specified group action, rather than only an unspecified conjugate.
Stability analysis of boundary element methods for the wave equation: The weakly singular operator in $1d$
Daniel Hoonhout; Richard Löscher; Carolina Urzúa-Torres

We discuss the construction of stable discrete pairs of trial and test spaces for the wave equation. Building on a general abstract operator-theoretic framework, we show how optimal pairings can be derived for a one-dimensional boundary element formulation of the wave equation with prescribed Dirichlet data, based on an indirect single layer potential ansatz. In this setting, the optimal test space can be computed analytically and has a physical interpretation, reflecting the non-local nature of the underlying operator.
Integer symplectic matrices in expanding boxes
We prove an essentially optimal uniform upper bound for the number of integer symplectic matrices inside a box of expanding side length and arbitrary centre.
Kan Jiang; Nero Ziyu Li; Lifeng Xi

In this paper, we study the structure of the solutions of $x^α+y^α=1$ with both coordinates in a $λ$-Cantor set. We prove that, for any $α>1$, the intersection with the middle-third Cantor set has positive Hausdorff dimension, strengthening the infinitude question posed by Jiang et al. [J. London Math. Soc. 113 (2026), e70408]. To explore the structure of the solutions, for arbitrary $α$, we find that their Hausdorff dimension undergoes phase transitions as $λ$ varies: we establish the occurrence of Hausdorff phase transitions by proving the existence of zero-dimensional and positive-dimensional regions.
Quantum Charge as a Particle/Antiparticle Label

We show that the concept of particles and antiparticles is related to the Weyl-Heisenberg group $W\!H_3$. Its generators are the position operators $\hat x^a$, the momentum operators $\hat p_a$, and the central element $Q_{\sf{v}}$, which defines a subgroup U(1)$_{\sf v}$ of $W\!H_3$. We show that the wave functions have a charge relative to the group U(1)$_{\sf{v}}$ equal to either $q_+=1/\hbar$ (particle $ψ_+$) or $q_-=-1/\hbar$ (antiparticle $ψ_-$). We call these eigenvalues of the operator $Q_{\sf{v}}$ quantum charges: $Q_{\sf{v}}ψ_\pm^{}=q_\pm^{}ψ_\pm^{}$. The wave functions $ψ_+$ and $ψ_-$ belong to the Hilbert spaces $\mathcal{H}_+$ and $\mathcal{H}_-$, on which unitarily inequivalent representations $π_\hbar$ and $π_{-\hbar}$ of the Weyl-Heisenberg group $W\!H_3$ are defined. These representations are related to each other by the antilinear charge conjugation operator $\hat C$, which maps $\mathcal{H}_+, q_+$ to $\mathcal{H}_-, q_-$. Charges $q_\pm^{}$ are intrinsic characteristics of the wave functions $ψ_\pm^{}$, similar to spin and electric charge. The wave function possesses one of these charges, $q_+$ or $q_-$, prior to the specification of any equations. We show that negative probabilities/energies and the Klein paradox in Klein-Gordon and Dirac theories are consequences of the violation of U(1)$_{\sf v}$-invariance in these theories. Restoring this invariance separates particle and antiparticles and eliminates all paradoxes at the level of first-quantized relativistic theories.
Principle of generating critical points of rational functions and Gauss-Fourier conjecture for second-kind zeros

The precise origin of critical points in rational functions remains a longstanding open problem. This paper elucidates the mechanism underlying critical point generation in rational functions. For over two centuries, a conjecture attributed to Gauss and Fourier has remained unresolved: every real zero of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ is associated with a pair of non-real zeros of the real polynomial $p(s)$. The real zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ that are multiple real zeros of $p^{'}(s)$ are termed second-kind zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$. By developing the root locus method, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the emergence of second-kind zeros: a second-kind zero $M$ arises if and only if at least two root loci of $2qπ$ or $2qπ+π$ degree, emitted from at least one pair of non-real conjugate zeros of $p(s)$ (in the extended complex plane, excluding the real axis), directly intersect another root locus at $M$ on the real axis. Our results resolve one conjecture of the Gauss-Fourier conjectures and reveal the fundamental mechanism by which critical points of rational functions are generated.
Macroscopic Poincaré Inequalities and Weak-Type Characterizations of $p$-Energy Forms
Fabrice Baudoin; Andrea Pinamonti; Meng Yang

For a class of regular strongly local $p$-energy forms on complete doubling metric measure spaces, $1<p<\infty$, we derive a macroscopic Poincaré inequality from a Poincaré inequality and a capacity upper bound at a doubling scale $Ψ$. The macroscopic inequality compares $L^p$-oscillations at any two scales and yields a uniform two-scale comparison $J_s\lesssim J_r$, $0<r<s$, for the Korevaar-Schoen functionals, strengthening their usual weak monotonicity property. Conversely, under a density assumption on compactly supported functions, the macroscopic inequality yields a regular strongly local Korevaar-Schoen $p$-energy satisfying a $Ψ$-Poincaré inequality. We also show that the macroscopic inequality forces lower $p$-scaling of $Ψ$ on scales not exceeding $\mathrm{diam} X$; together with doubling, this gives two-sided power bounds. Finally, we establish a weak-type characterization of the energy domain of Brezis-Van Schaftingen-Yung type.
Weighted composition operators on the Fock space

In this paper, we discuss the compactness, invertibility and isometry of the operators on the Fock space formed by multiplying a weighted composition operator with the adjoint of another weighted composition operator to form either $W_{g, ψ}W_{f, φ}^*$ or $W_{g, ψ}^*W_{f, φ}$.
Elliptic rearrangement for Poisson equations with mean-zero data

The $L^p$ norm of a sign-changing Dirichlet solution of Poisson's equation is shown to be bounded by the maximum of the $L^p$ norms of the ball solutions obtained by signed rearrangement of the source and its negative, assuming the source term has mean value zero. This paired comparison on bounded open sets extends Talenti's elliptic rearrangement principle to solutions that change sign. In dimensions one and two, the paired comparison holds for all $1\le p\le\infty$, and it holds in every dimension for $p=\infty$. The inequalities are sharp and equality cases are characterized. In dimensions $n \geq 3$, paired comparison can fail for every finite $p$ although it remains valid for $p\ge(3n-1)/4$ in the special case of bang-bang sources with mean zero. The mean-zero source assumption is crucial when $p<\infty$. Without it, paired comparison can fail even for bang-bang sources. For sources of arbitrary mean in one dimension, however, the $L^\infty$ paired comparison still holds and so does a comparison for $L^p$ norms of the derivative when $1\le p\le3$.
Modulating flow polynomials and parity bias in homological walk counting

Long weighted walks seem to sample mod-$t$ flows uniformly, but at even moduli a persistent parity bias survives. Writing $C_G(t)$ for the flow polynomial of a connected graph $G$ of genus $g$, the proportion of nowhere-zero flows under uniform sampling is $C_G(t)/t^g$. For arbitrary positive directed weights and all moduli, we determine the exact leading corrections for both closed walks and nonbacktracking closed walks, which we call circuits. Only the circuit result requires $g\ge2$. For closed walks, the canonical character governs the leading correction through the canonical modulating flow polynomial $D_G$; for circuits, the period character, when it exists, governs the leading correction through the period modulating flow polynomial $D_{G,η}$. At even moduli these give parity-dependent corrections: the two mechanisms coincide on nonbipartite graphs and separate only in the bipartite circuit problem. More generally, each integral-homology character $ζ$ determines a balanced-dichromatic specialization $D_{G,ζ}$. These polynomials form a character-indexed family whose finite-order members give Fourier coefficients of the nowhere-zero flow set and whose retained edge sets are the central sets of a gain semimatroid. We further show that $D_G$ is a cycle-matroid invariant and a signed-Tutte specialization satisfying signed deletion-contraction. Finally, an integral nowhere-zero approximation theorem implies that asymptotically almost every weighted circuit traverses every edge.
Logics vs doctrines, a mirror symmetry
Ivan Di Liberti; Umberto Tarantino; Lingyuan Ye

We study the relationship between doctrines, encoding 2-categories of theories in predicate logic, and fragments of geometric logic, defined through Kan injectivity in the 2-category of topoi. After a brief historical account of the notion of doctrine, we propose our working definition. Our main result then establishes a Galois connection between doctrines and subgeometric logics. This connection suggests a mirror symmetry between the world of doctrines and the world of logics, in which constructions and results on either side admit counterparts on the other. We develop this symmetry through constructions of syntactic categories and classifying topoi in both settings, recovering the familiar examples from categorical logic. We prove paired Diaconescu-type theorems and give symmetric universal characterisations of the two closure operators induced by the Galois connection. Finally, we show that passing from a doctrine to its closure induces a reflection between the corresponding 2-categories of algebras, and we relate this reflection to conceptual completeness.
The sharp Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality and its variants

We introduce and prove a new conformally invariant Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality, and classify all optimizers, which are the Hopf map $π:\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}\to\mathbb{CP}^n$ composed with a symplectic diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and an orientation-preserving conformal transformation of $\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$. The proof uses the sharp curl-Sobolev inequality and a rigidity argument for its equality case. Motivated by the main result, we also introduce the spherical Radu--Tchrakian--Yang functional, and prove the global minimality of the Hopf map for radii in a neighborhood of $((n!)^2/n)^{1/(4n-4)}$, and characterize all minimizers. We also prove local instability for sufficiently small and sufficiently large radii, with explicit lower bounds for the Morse index.
Recovering the reaction coefficient in a time-fractional diffusion equation with variable coefficients in any spatial dimension

We explore the inverse problem of determining the reaction coefficient $q(x',t)$ in the time-fractional diffusion equation ${}^CD_t u-Lu+q(x',t)u=f$ in $\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,T]$, $x=(x',x_n)$, $0<α<1$, from the trace of the solution on the hyperplane $\{x_n=0\}$. Here ${}^CD_t$ is the Gerasimov--Caputo derivative and $L$ is a uniformly elliptic second-order operator with variable, $x_n$-independent coefficients and without zero-order term. For $L=Δ$ this problem was studied in dimensions $n=1,2,3$ by methods based on pointwise bounds of the kernels, which are not available for $n\ge4$. Our approach relies on the Eidelman--Kochubei fundamental solution: although its singularity on the diagonal depends on the dimension, we show that it satisfies integral bounds of the same form for all $n\ge1$. Using these bounds, we prove existence, uniqueness and stability of regular solutions of the direct problem with a Hölder continuous reaction coefficient. Without assuming additional smoothness of the solution, we show that the inverse problem is equivalent to a closed system of integral equations for $q$ and the derivatives $\partial_{x_n}u$, $\partial^2_{x_n}u$. For the inverse problem we establish a conditional Lipschitz stability estimate on the whole time interval and global uniqueness in every dimension, and prove local existence of a solution. In the case $a_{in}\equiv0$, $b_n\equiv0$ we obtain a stability estimate with explicit constants, which reduces to the known estimates for the Laplacian. An explicit two-dimensional example with a mixed coefficient and a normal drift shows that the hypotheses of the main theorems are compatible and that the corresponding terms in the trace condition cannot be omitted.
A branching model for selective sweeps
Luiz Renato Fontes; Rinaldo B. Schinazi

At every discrete time i we introduce exactly one individual whose genotype is given by a p_i sampled uniformly in (0,1). This individual will be the founder of a branching process with a geometric offspring distribution with parameter p_i. All the branching processes are independent. We show that as time goes to infinity successive selective sweeps occur. That is, ever more fit single genotypes dominate the population. Moreover, at any fixed time we prove that the dominating genotype is not the most fit genotype. Finally, we show that the rescaled point process associated to selective sweeps converges to an inhomogeneous Poisson process.
Choice principles in countable partition models

We study the countable partition model over a set of atoms of arbitrary uncountable cardinality $κ$. Its supports are partitions of the atoms into countably many blocks, and a permutation fixes a support when it preserves each block setwise. This model was proposed by Bruce and studied by Banerjee. We prove that dependent choice holds for every $κ$, although the filter of subgroups is not closed under countable intersections. Choice for well-orderable families holds exactly when $κ<\aleph_{ω_1}$; when $κ\ge\aleph_{ω_1}$, an $ω_1$-indexed family witnesses its failure. The Hartogs and Lindenbaum numbers of the set of atoms are both $ω_1$. The proofs use permutations matching blocks of equal cardinality and establish shift completeness of the filter. Together with Banerjee's failure of $\mathsf{DC}_{ω_1}$, these results determine which dependent choice principles hold in the model.
On Lusztig Sheaves for Tame Quivers

Let $Q$ be a connected quiver of tame type, and let $U_v^-$ be the positive part of the corresponding quantized affine algebra. In Lusztig's construction of the canonical basis of $U_v^-$, the simple perverse sheaves occurring, up to shift, as direct summands of the flag sheaf complexes are given by intersection cohomology complexes $\operatorname{IC}(X(c,m),\mathcal{L}_χ)$. We study the restrictions of these intersection cohomology complexes to the locally closed subsets $Y(c,m)$ obtained by fixing the preprojective, non-homogeneous regular, and preinjective summands in the category $\operatorname{rep} Q$. We prove pointwise purity on the loci where the homogeneous regular part is a direct sum of pairwise non-isomorphic quasi-simple modules, and establish a semisimple decomposition of the restrictions to the corresponding larger strata. The graded multiplicities of the local systems associated with irreducible characters of symmetric groups determine the transition coefficients from the canonical basis to the PBW basis constructed via quiver representations. This gives a geometric explanation of the positivity of these coefficients and the unitriangularity of the transition matrix.
No braiding for quantum sl2 reps - A short proof
We give a short and self-contained proof that the category of all finite dimensional representations of quantum sl2 is not braided.
On Almost MDS codes holding $(n-k-1)$-designs and an open problem on Witt design
Huakai Wei; Shiyuan Qiang; Shaofang Hong

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an almost maximum distance separable (AMDS) code over the finite fields with parameters $[n,k,n-k]$ whose minimum-weight codewords support an $(n-k-1)$-$(n,n-k,λ)$ design. We first determine the parameters of the dual code $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$. We also characterize the design and its complementary design supported by the minimum weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$. In particular, we present explicit formulas for the weight enumerators of all subset codes of $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$ with length at least $k+1$. These formulas are completely determined by the cardinality of the subset, the dimension, together with the parameter $λ$, and are independent of the specific choice of subsets. As an application, we answer an open problem posed by Wang, Tang and Ding in 2023 by proving that the $3$-design supported by the minimum-weight codewords in their proposed cyclic dual code is isomorphic to the complementary design of the Witt spherical geometry design.
Weighted Risk Aggregation under Long-Memory Dependence: Pathwise Fluctuations of Exposure-Weighted Losses

We model insurance loss in each period as deterministic exposure multiplied by a nonnegative function of a long-memory Gaussian sequence. A weighted law of the iterated logarithm yields the exact almost-sure scale and sharp constant of centered cumulative loss. Loss per unit of cumulative exposure converges almost surely to its mean, with an exact error scale common to all admissible exposure profiles; the sharp constant depends on the exposure exponent. Lognormal and quadratic examples, of Hermite ranks one and two, and a simulation illustrate the results. A known spectral formula expresses the quadratic coefficient through a leading eigenvalue.
Spanning bipartite quadrangulations in even triangulations of real projective spaces

We study spanning quadrangulations of even triangulations of real projective spaces, using the higher-dimensional notion of quadrangulation introduced by Kaiser and Stehl\'ık. We prove that every even triangulation of $\RP^d$, where $d\ge 2$, admits a spanning bipartite quadrangulation. Moreover, such a triangulation admits a spanning non-bipartite quadrangulation if and only if it is not balanced; if it is balanced, every spanning quadrangulation is bipartite. Our proofs use coloring monodromy: its orbits yield bipartite quadrangulations, while a covering-space construction gives non-bipartite ones. %In dimension three, a bipartite quadrangulation can always be chosen to induce $K_{2,2}$ on each tetrahedron. More generally, we establish a sufficient condition for the existence of spanning bipartite quadrangulations on closed manifolds in terms of the monodromy action, and derive a consequence involving the fundamental group.
BCC optimality for the three-dimensional Coulomb lattice energy

We prove that the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the renormalized Coulomb energy among three-dimensional Bravais lattices of fixed covolume, up to orthogonal transformations. Using Ewald summation, we write the energy, to within an additive constant, as a sum of two positive, rapidly convergent series in real and reciprocal space. Their positivity provides finite lower bounds for all competitors. A passage to the dual lattice reduces the problem to a face-centered cubic comparison. A short basis vector estimate, a certified local Hessian, and interval bounds on a compact five-dimensional domain complete the computer-assisted proof.
Model Predictive Control: Systematic Design Tailored to Nonholonomic Systems
Emilia F. P. Krendelsberger; Jasmin Krauspenhaar; Lea Bold; Mario Rosenfelder; Peter Eberhard; Henrik Ebel; Karl Worthmann

Nonholonomic systems are ubiquitous in applications such as transportation and robotics, yet their control remains challenging. In order to achieve asymptotic stability of a desired equilibrium, model predictive control (MPC) schemes without stabilizing terminal conditions have recently been proposed for nonholonomic kinematic systems. However, this approach still required lengthy system-specific calculations. This paper eliminates the need for these auxiliary calculations, as we propose a streamlined systematic design for MPC stage costs tailored to nonholonomic systems, utilizing the concepts of privileged coordinates and nonholonomic weights. Furthermore, the proposed design methodology is extended beyond purely kinematic models to a wider class of systems with non-negligible dynamics, and we highlight the geometric meaning of the resulting MPC stage costs. The systematic procedure is demonstrated using an articulated vehicle as an example.
Accelerated primal-dual dynamics and algorithms for strongly convex-concave bilinear saddle point problems
Yun-xi Zhang; Yi-bin Xiao; Xin He

In this paper, we develop accelerated primal-dual dynamics and algorithms for strongly convex-concave saddle point problems with bilinear coupling. Combining strongly convex Nesterov dynamics with scaled heavy-ball dynamics, we propose a second-order primal-dual dynamical system with constant damping and derive an associated algorithm by time discretization and coefficient adjustment. Under suitable conditions on the continuous scaling function $β(t)$ and the discrete scaling sequence $β_k$, we establish primal-dual gap estimates of $\mathcal O(1/β(t))$ in continuous time and $\mathcal O(1/β_k)$ in discrete time. The maximal admissible growth rates of these scales recover the exponential and linear convergence rates of strongly convex Nesterov methods in continuous and discrete time, respectively. We also prove convergence of the primal-dual trajectory and sequence, even when the dual solution is nonunique. Saddle residual estimates of $\mathcal O(1/\sqrt{β(t)})$ and $\mathcal O(1/\sqrt{β_k})$ hold under globally Lipschitz gradients in continuous time and with a possibly nonsmooth dual potential in discrete time. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and the performance of the proposed methods.
Higher rank spectral projector estimates and a Stein--Tomas restriction theorem
Phillip Harris; Jiaqi Hou; Xiaoqi Huang

Let $X$ be a compact locally symmetric space of noncompact type. We prove sharp upper bounds for the $L^2\to L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for joint eigenfunctions of the full ring of invariant differential operators on $X$. This improves the corresponding result of Marshall, by removing a logarithmic power loss at the critical exponent. Using the same method, we also prove the endpoint case of Mockenhaupt's $(L^2,L^p)$ Fourier restriction theorem.
Will AI kill us all---or just make mathematicians obsolete?

AI's recent advances have fueled predictions of human intellectual obsolescence and fears for the future of mathematics. I argue that, impressive as these achievements are, they do not establish AI's capacity to invent new concepts and theories or sustain autonomous recursive self-improvement. Human intelligence also involves judgment, imagination, and embodied experience that standard measures fail to capture. Mathematics extends beyond proving theorems: its creative core lies in conceptual discovery and understanding. AI can strengthen this enterprise, but realizing its promise requires protecting attribution, open exchange, confidentiality, and mathematical training. I propose an academic AI consortium to provide powerful research tools with enforceable guarantees safeguarding unpublished ideas.
On unit groups of purely infinite rings

We prove that the unit group of any purely infinite, regular, right self-injective ring admits a universal sequence of words (thus has strong distortion), is minimally almost periodic, has finite involution width, is verbally simple and verbally elliptic, and has uncountable uniform strong cofinality. These findings are consequences of more refined structural results, some of which provide concrete cardinal estimates involving the Goodearl--Boyle dimension of the ring. A central ingredient in our results is a comprehensive study of bounded normal generation, in particular with respect to certain classes of involutions. Along the way, we develop some abstract methods and concepts pertaining to geometric group theory.
Property (R) with its stability for analytic functional system and under compact perturbations
Sinan Qiu; Lining Jiang; Xiaomin Wei

Let $\mathcal{F}_T$ be the analytic functional system generated by a linear bounded operator $T$ on an infinite dimensional complex Hilbert space. This paper characterizes the stability of property (R), a variant of Weyl's theorem, for $\mathcal{F}_T$ and under compact perturbations in terms of the spectrum on consistency in Weyl. In particular, the stability of property (R) under compact perturbations is shown to imply the (R)-stability of $\mathcal{F}_T$.
Monotonicity and evolution of total isoperimetric profiles under Minkowski regularization
Zakaria Fattah; Ilias Ftouhi; Giorgio Saracco

We study the evolution of the total isoperimetric profile of a planar convex body under volume-preserving Minkowski regularization. Several scalar geometric quantities are known to be monotone along this flow; we prove that the total isoperimetric profile is monotone as well, and characterize the equality cases. We also establish an explicit reparametrization law, by which, for nonnegative times, the profile of the regularized body is determined by that of the initial one, and the order of profiles of bodies of equal area is preserved. As consequences, we obtain the uniform convergence of the profile to the one of the ball of equal area; its joint \(\mathrm C^1\) regularity in the volume and the regularization parameter; the fact that it solves a nonlocal quasilinear Hamilton--Jacobi equation; and sharp inequalities for the profile.
S-PASS: Star-Topology Pinching-Antenna Systems with Pipelined Antenna Pre-Positioning

Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) flexibly reconfigure the wireless channel by positioning dielectric antennas along a waveguide near each user. Releasing and re-attaching an antenna, however, is a mechanical operation orders of magnitude slower than electronic switching, wasting much transmission time. Existing designs generally assume instant reconfiguration, neglect the mechanical latency, or keep the antenna fixed. This paper proposes S-PASS, a star architecture of waveguides sharing one radio-frequency chain through a switch, and pipelined antenna pre-positioning (PAP), a time-division protocol in which idle waveguides pre-position their antennas for their next users while one transmits. It derives in closed form the scheduling efficiency, the number of waveguides beyond which the latency costs no transmission time, and the latency up to which PAP outperforms fixed placement. Analytical and numerical results show that this latency grows with each added waveguide, and users at the outer ends of the waveguides gain most.
Moduli spaces of logarithmic connections associated with difference Painlevé equations of type $E^{(1)}_n$

In this paper, we provide an explicit correspondence between moduli spaces of parabolic logarithmic connections on the projective line with spectral type $(2^2,1^4,1^4)$ and $(3^2, 2^3, 1^6)$, and the spaces of initial conditions for difference Painlevé equations with symmetry of type $E^{(1)}_7$ and $E^{(1)}_8$, respectively. Furthermore, we realize the extended affine Weyl group symmetries of the space of initial conditions in terms of connections.
Quantum f-divergences from retrodictive tests: a unifying classical variational principle

The same classical f-divergence admits inequivalent extensions to quantum states. The question is whether these extensions can be obtained from a common classical variational principle with an operational interpretation. Here we generalize Matsumoto's reverse-test optimization by introducing retrodictive tests relative to a reference state. A retrodictive test compares a forward and a reverse stochastic process, realized by quantum preparation and measurement, related by Petz transposition relative to the chosen reference, and subject to prescribed quantum averages. Equivalently, it compares two reverse tests sharing a reference output, whose labels are coupled by retrodiction. For faithful states in finite dimension, we prove that the same spectral implementation attains the minimum classical f-divergence over all admissible implementations simultaneously for every operator-convex f. A flat reference yields the standard quantum f-divergences, thereby giving the Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions a variational characterization. Choosing either prescribed state as reference recovers maximal quantum f-divergences and Matsumoto's reverse-test optimization, while power references interpolate between the standard and maximal divergences along the geodesic family. In the relative-entropy case, this gives the passage from Umegaki to Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy by changing the reference state. The same optimization extends to arbitrary quantum channels and, for channels with faithful Choi operator, gives a variational characterization of quantum entropy production.
Discrete homotopy of graphs and $k$-parabolic subspace arrangements

Discrete homotopy theory is a combinatorial homotopy theory defined for discrete objects. Barcelo--Severs--White conjectured that the homotopy groups of complements of $k$-parabolic subspace arrangements are isomorphic to the discrete homotopy groups of graphs associated with the Coxeter complexes. We show that this correspondence fails in general by giving a counterexample in degree two for the $4$-parabolic subspace arrangement of type $A_5$.
Wave Processing Unit: Closed-Form Matrix Synthesis for Wave Computing in Multiuser MIMO Communications
Xiaokun Teng; Yanqing Ren; Weicong Chen; Wankai Tang; Xiao Li; Shi Jin

Wave computing offers a compelling route to bypass the latency and energy bottlenecks of digital baseband processing. However, existing wave-domain processors rely on task-specific, non-convex iterative optimization, which incurs substantial configuration overhead and limits real-time applications. In this paper, we propose the wave processing unit (WPU), a programmable planar Mach--Zehnder interferometer (MZI) network that accelerates matrix--vector multiplications in MIMO communications. First, we model the tunable MZI element as a parameterized $2\times2$ unitary transformation, and establish a closed-form synthesis framework for the WPU that decomposes an arbitrary unitary matrix into a cascade of MZI elements arranged in a compact rectangular topology. To handle arbitrary complex-valued operators, we further extend the method through singular value decomposition (SVD) and a hardware-efficient semi-unitary synthesis, avoiding redundant hardware and reducing the compilation complexity. We then apply the WPU to multiuser downlink precoding by an efficient WPU synthesis method, and compare the proposed architecture with hybrid and wave-domain ones. Numerical results demonstrate machine-precision synthesis with negligible residuals for up to $64\times64$ operators, with approximately $380\times$ faster configuration than iterative wave computing baselines. For 64-antenna, 8-user downlink precoding, WPU requires 87.5% fewer RF chains than the fully digital architecture while achieving the same sum rate under ideal hardware. These results highlight the potential of the WPU for precise, hardware-efficient wave-domain processing with rapid configuration.
Optimally Emulating Smooth Functions for Bayesian Analyses
Scott Pratt; Oleh Savchuk; Eren Erdogan; Ekaksh Kataria; Christal Martin; Syed Afrid Jahan; Frederi Viens

For Bayesian analyses aimed at constraining the parameter space of computationally expensive models by comparison with heterogeneous data sets, model emulators play a pivotal role. Model emulators enable searches through high-dimensional parameter spaces, searches which might otherwise require millions of full model runs. Here, an emulation strategy is presented based on the assumption that the model output can be well described by a polynomial expansion with all terms being independent of one another and with higher order terms being given decreasing weights according to a convergence parameter. It is found that if the expansion's form is constrained to being invariant to rotation and translation of the parameter space that the polynomial form becomes equivalent to that of a Gaussian process emulator using a correlation kernel with a Gaussian form. In the limit that the function is smooth, quantified by a convergence parameter, $Λ$, it is found that rather few training points are required to reproduce the full model and provide a good estimate of its uncertainty. An accuracy metric is defined based on an average of the expected uncertainty over the prior before training data are actually gathered. Analytic expressions for the expected accuracy are provided based solely on an expected value of $Λ$ and the location of the training points. This enables a tenable optimized placement of training points, which is shown to be significantly superior to random placement or that from Latin hyper-cube sampling. Examples of optimized placement are provided, and the accuracy is studied as a function of various variables, such as the number of model parameters, the number of training points, and the convergence parameter.

The numerical shadow of a complex matrix is the measure obtained by pushing forward that Haar measure on the unit sphere in $\mathbb{C}^n$ by the numerical range map. By the choice of measure, unitary equivalence implies same measure, but the reverse is not true for $n\geq 3$. We name a matrix $\textbf{shadow rigid}$ it its unitary equivalence class and shadow equivalence class coincide. It is known that normal matrices are rigid, but the topic has not been explored beyond this in the literature. The main result of the paper is showing that in the $n=3$ case, a matrix is rigid if and only if it is non-generic. We also show that rigidity is preserved under an affine group action and present three normal-like properties of $3\times 3$ non-generic matrices.
Restriction of $p'$-degree characters, fields of values, and relative normal complements

Let $G$ be a finite $p$-solvable group for a prime $p$, and let $P$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$. Centella and Navarro proved that there is a canonical bijection ${\rm Irr}_{p'}(Φ_{1_G})\to{\rm Irr}_{p'}(Φ_{1_{\textbf N_G(P)}})$ preserving fields of values, where $Φ_{1_G}$ denotes the principal projective indecomposable character of $G$. In the spirit of a result of Berkovich on the McKay bijection, we characterize when this projective correspondence can be realized by restriction, proving that it holds if and only if $\mathbf{N}_G(P)$ admits a certain relative normal complement in $G$. More generally, we establish a refined criterion incorporating fields of values, and we extend this characterization to $π$-separable groups with nilpotent Hall $π$-subgroups.
Parameters Robust Parallelizable Iterative Decoupled Algorithms for Thermo-Poroelasticity with Nonlinear Convective Transport

This paper presents several parallel iterative algorithms for the nonlinear thermo-poroelasticity. We introduce an auxiliary variable to transform the original model into a four-field formulation to overcome Poisson locking. The iterative idea is extended to linearize and decouple the four-field model. Different coupling strategies are employed among these three subproblems, combined with appropriately designed iteration settings, yielding distinct iterative parallel algorithms. Stabilization terms are incorporated into these algorithms to ensure parameter robustness in extreme situations. We derive error estimates and prove the convergence of these parallel iterative decoupled algorithms. Finally, numerical experiments are presented to compare the performance of the different parallel algorithms in extreme parameter settings, thereby validating their efficiency and robustness.
Sharp spherical $L^p\to L^4$ extension estimates over finite fields in odd dimensions

Let $q$ be an odd prime power, let $d\ge3$ be odd, and let $S_j=\{ξ\in \mathbb F_q^d:ξ_1^2+\cdots+ξ_d^2=j\}$, where $j\ne 0$. We prove the sharp extension estimate ${L^{4(d+1)/(3d+1)}(S_j, dσ)\to L^4(\mathbb F_q^d,dc)}$ whenever $η_q((-1)^{(d-1)/2}j)=-1$, where $η_q$ is the quadratic character. This confirms the odd-dimensional spherical extension conjecture of Koh, Pham, and Vinh over every finite field of odd characteristic. Together with the known estimate in the complementary sign class, this determines the sharp ${L^p\to{L^4}}$ extension range for all nonzero-radius spheres in odd dimensions. We also apply the endpoint estimate to obtain sufficient conditions for the unique recovery of sparse signals from incomplete Fourier data.
On the planar Neumann--Poincaré inverse spectral problem

Does the Neumann--Poincaré spectrum determine a planar domain up to an extended Möbius transformation? We construct a pair showing that the answer is no, even for analytic, strictly convex, algebraic boundaries. Their operators are similar. We then prove a positive result for prescribed finite-dimensional families of normalised exterior conformal maps. For every $m\ge1$, the first $m$ positive eigenvalues determine $m$ real Laurent coefficients on a small truncated convex cone, provided the higher coefficients are a prescribed analytic remainder of quadratic order. Recovery is Lipschitz stable, uniformly down to the disk. The proof combines the Grunsky representation with a nondegeneracy argument for weighted Hankel matrices and differentiated perturbation estimates. Explicit two- and three-parameter examples, single-mode families with repeated leading eigenvalues, and Möbius equivalence classes illustrate the result. Direct proofs for complete polarization data show what spectral weights add to the eigenvalues.
Small and Large Quasi-Kernels in General Digraphs

In a digraph $D$, a set $Q$ of vertices is a quasi-kernel if $Q$ is an independent set and every vertex in $D$ can be reached from $Q$ via at most two edges. The small quasi-kernel conjecture by Erdős and Székely predicts that every source-free $n$-vertex digraph contains a quasi-kernel of size at most $n - n/2$. Chvátal and Lovász' 1974 work implies a bound of $n - \sqrt{n}+1$. In 2024, Sprio shows the bound $n - \frac{1}{4} \sqrt{n \log_2 n}$. We show that there always is a quasi-kernel of size at most $n - \frac{1}{51}n^{2/3} / \ln^{2/3}(n)$. For the related large quasi-kernel conjecture by Spiro, we show that there always is a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|N^+[Q]| \ge 0.2917 \cdot n^{2/3} / \ln^{2/3}(n)$.
Connected Coloring Games on Corona Products of Graphs

We study the connected coloring game on corona products of graphs. For connected graphs $G$ and $H$, we prove the sharp upper bound $χ_{cg}(G\circ H)\leq\max\{Δ(G),Δ(H)+1\}+1$ and establish a further bound using the Bob-start ordinary coloring game on the second factor. We show that the difference between the Alice-start and Bob-start connected game chromatic numbers can be arbitrarily large in either direction. We further prove that a connected subgraph may have arbitrarily larger connected game chromatic number than its ambient connected graph, and that $χ_{cg}(G\circ H)$ cannot be bounded in terms of $χ_{cg}(G)$ and $χ_{cg}(H)$ alone, even when both factors have connected game chromatic number $2$. We also obtain corona products for which the difference $χ_g-χ_{cg}$ is arbitrarily large and construct infinitely many connected graphs with $χ_g<χ_{cg}$. Finally, for corona products of trees, we prove the universal upper bound $5$, characterize those attaining the value $3$, give structural sufficient conditions for the value $4$, and exhibit a broad family attaining the value $5$.
Wave equation with unbounded terms driven by a stochastic measure

The one-dimensional wave equation with additive noise driven by a stochastic measure is considered. For the stochastic integrator, we assume only the sigma-additivity in probability and that $|y|^τ$ is integrable on $\mathbb{R}$ for some $τ>1/2$. The class of stochastic measures includes many important cases of random processes. In the equation, the stochastic measure depends only on the spatial variable. The existence, uniqueness, and Hölder regularity of the mild solution are proved. In the previous publications, similar results were obtained for the case of bounded terms of the wave equation driven by a stochastic measure. In our paper, one term may be unbounded, satisfying the linear growth condition. Nevertheless, we prove that the solution is bounded in this case.
Geometrization of continuum mechanics and nonequilibrium thermodynamics: Heat conduction

We propose a geometric formulation of non-equilibrium heat conduction. It combines the variational (Hamiltonian) structure of symmetric hyperbolic thermodynamically compatible (SHTC) equations with the exterior calculus of differential forms. The central object is the thermal impulse one-form on the four-dimensional matter-time manifold. Its time component is the temperature, and for reversible (ballistic) heat transport it is the exact differential of a scalar potential (i.e. it is holonomic). Non-equilibrium effects are described by a second one-form, the small-scale thermal impulse, which is not required to be exact. Its time component is a fluctuating temperature, and its exterior derivative, the four-thermal vorticity, satisfies a Bianchi-type kinematic identity. The variational principle together with this identity yields a non-equilibrium two-temperature model. Its field equations have the same structure as Maxwell's equations in a medium, with the thermal impulse field, the thermal vorticity field and a thermal Poynting vector contributing to the heat flux. Dissipation is introduced through relaxation terms that conserve the total energy and produce entropy. A formal asymptotic analysis shows that, in the relaxation limit, the model reduces to a Guyer-Krumhansl-type heat conduction with independent transverse and longitudinal length scales. The transverse nonlocal term comes from the spatial non-holonomy of the small-scale thermal impulse, while the longitudinal term comes from its non-holonomy in time, i.e. from the relaxation of the fluctuating temperature. We also discuss the gauge-theoretic interpretation of the model. Its kinematics is that of an abelian gauge theory, while the local gauge symmetry is explicitly broken by the existence of two temperatures. Finally, we discuss the consequences of the geometric structure for structure-preserving numerical methods.
Recursive Code Evolution for Task-Oriented Semantic Communications
Yan Gong; Zheng Chu; Wei Koong Chai; Hari Mohan Pandey; Jingrui Hou; Miao Zhang; Yuanjian Li; Pei Xiao

Semantic communication jointly optimizes inference accuracy, channel use, and computation, yet the underlying communication program is typically specified before training. This paper presents ComRSI (Communications-Oriented Recursive Self-Improvement), a framework for recursively evolving that program through large-language-model-assisted code edits. A fixed agent modifies the encoder, channel adapters, decoder, loss, and training policy; a protected evaluator screens candidates under prescribed budgets and resource constraints. Accepted code and textual feedback inform subsequent proposals, while candidate weights are trained from scratch. In the original ten-generation CIFAR-100 lineage, eight accepted revisions produce an attention-pooled code achieving 74.3% test accuracy over an Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) channel at 32 complex symbols per image, compared with 67.2% at 256 symbols for the initial design. The program also improves fading-channel accuracy and transfers to Tiny-ImageNet after retraining. A repeat study with ten searches per method compares ComRSI against non-recursive agents with and without textual history. Mean final search scores balancing accuracy, transmission rate, and computational cost are 0.7587, 0.7376, and 0.7089, respectively; the mean numbers of accepted revisions per search are 6.0, 5.0, and 2.1. The advantage over the memoryless agent is supported by a two-sided rank test, whereas the difference from the history-equipped agent remains statistically inconclusive at this sample size. Archived proposals show that pooling can yield a large improvement, while retained history supports subsequent refinement. These results support recursive program optimization within the evaluated setting and expose its remaining rate-robustness and compute-placement trade-offs.

In this article we improve Heath-Brown's estimate for the error term in the three-dimensional sphere problem, proving \[ \#\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^3:\|\mathbf x\|\le R\}=\frac{4π}{3}R^3+O_\varepsilon(R^{55/42+\varepsilon}). \] Incoporating the recent OpenAI quasi-GRH into our argument further improves this to \[ \#\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^3:\|\mathbf x\|\le R\}= \frac{4π}{3}R^3+O_\varepsilon(R^{\frac{2274811}{1743872}+\varepsilon}). \]
Fermion-Number Variation for Several Coupling Schemes in an $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Chiral Soliton Background

When topological solitons are coupled to fermions, they often induce a nontrivial fermion number. In the chiral quark soliton model (CQSM), this phenomenon underlies the identification of soliton topology with baryon number. However, whether this topology--fermion-number correspondence is determined solely by soliton topology or also depends on the fermion--soliton coupling scheme remains unclear. In this paper, we investigate this question by comparing several coupling schemes to the same $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ chiral soliton background. To treat the corresponding Dirac Hamiltonians within a common framework, we evaluate the variation of the regularized fermion-number along a model-parameter space. For the standard chiral Yukawa coupling of the CQSM, this variation reproduces the topological charge $Q$ associated with $π_3(\mathrm{SU}(N))$. The same result is obtained for an axial-vector coupling, whereas the fermion number variation vanishes for a vector coupling, despite the nontrivial topology of the chiral soliton background. These results provide an explicit example in which soliton topology alone does not determine the fermionic response; the topology--fermion-number correspondence also depends on how the background field is coupled to fermions.

We study the alternating perturbation of Conway's nested recurrence, $C(n)=C(C(n-1))+C(n-C(n-1))+(-1)^n$ for $n\geq 3$, with $C(1)=C(2)=1$. We prove that the sequence is well defined and satisfies $C(n)=ψ^{-3}n+O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$, where $ψ>1$ is the real root of $ψ^3=ψ^2+1$.
Homological branching laws for $p$-adic and mod $p$ representations of ${\rm GL}_2$ over a $p$-adic field

Let $F$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ and $p\geq 5$. In this paper, we establish homological branching laws for mod $p$ representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ restricted to split and nonsplit maximal tori, treating principal and special series and, when $F=\mathbb Q_p$, supersingular representations. We determine the derived Hom-complexes in both orders for nonexceptional characters. At exceptional characters, we calculate their Euler--Poincaré characteristics under a $p$-torsion-freeness hypothesis. We also establish corresponding results for a class of unitary Banach space representations.
Sharp Brezis--Merle Inequalities for Polyharmonic Dirichlet Problems: Extremal Measures and Critical Asymptotics
João Marcos do Ó; Federica Sani; Victor Rafael Silva

We establish the Brezis--Merle inequality for very weak solutions of polyharmonic Dirichlet problems with integrable data on smooth bounded domains in conformal dimensions. The inequality is sharp both with respect to the admissible range of the exponent and to the quantity appearing on the right-hand side, which is characterized as the maximum of an associated one-pole Green functional. The supremum defining this quantity is not attained by any integrable datum, but remains unchanged when the admissible class is extended to Radon probability measures; in this enlarged class, the extremals are Dirac masses, and their concentration points are characterized in terms of the associated Green function. On the unit ball, we prove uniqueness of the extremal measure and obtain an explicit optimal bound extending the sharp result for the Laplacian. Finally, we determine the critical asymptotics of the sharp constant on the right-hand side and show that the possible limiting concentration points are selected by the maximum points of the polyharmonic Robin function.
Global existence for the semilinear regular Euler-Poisson-Darboux-Tricomi equation, II

In our previous work [25], we established the global existence of solutions to the semilinear Euler-Poisson-Darboux-Tricomi equation with power nonlinearity \(|u|^p\) in the case where the damping term dominates the mass term. In contrast, this paper studies the reverse case, namely, the existence of global solutions to the equation when the mass term dominates the damping term. We prove that small-data solutions exist globally if \[ p>\max\{p_0((m+1)n,μ), \widetilde{p}_1(n,m,μ)\} \] for \(δ\doteq(μ-1)^2-4ν^2\leq0\), where \(δ\) measures the relative dominance between the damping and mass terms, \(p_0(n,μ)\) is the \textit{Strauss-related} exponent defined by (1.12), and \(\widetilde{p}_1(n,m,μ)\) is defined by (2.5).
Linear Stability of Double-Double Orbits in the Equal-Mass Four-Body Problem via Index Theory

In this paper, using the Maslov-type index theory in symplectic geometry, we study the linear stability of the double-double orbits in the planar equal-mass four body problem. By analyzing its symmetry properties and variational characterization, we clarify the relationship between linear stability and its variational nature on various loop spaces and show that for any rotation angle $θ=\fracπ{n}$, the retrograde double-double orbits are linearly stable with integer $n\in[3,30]$ and the prograde double-double orbits are linearly stable with integer $n\in[4,30]$. We also give the distributions of the eigenvalues on the unit circle of the monodromy matrices associated with the orbits. The basic idea is as follows: the variational characterization of the orbits provides information about its Morse index; based on its relation to the Maslov-type index, our stability criteria come into play.
Extending Doi--Takeuchi correspondence to bimodules and noncommutative covers

Doi and Takeuchi, and independently Blattner, Cohen and Montgomery, have exhibited a correspondence between cleft extensions of an algebra $U$ by a Hopf algebra $H$ and $H$-measurings on $U$ equipped with a compatible normalized 2-cocycle. Each cleft extension is isomorphic as an algebra, a left $U$-module and a right $H$-comodule to the crossed product algebra constructed from the measuring and the cocycle. Cleft $H$-extensions are a special case of $H$-Hopf-Galois extensions, describing noncommutative principal $H$-bundles with affine total and affine base space. Corings are used to describe noncommutative space covers, allowing a description of possibly nonaffine noncommutative spaces. We propose to describe the total space of a noncommutative $H$-principal bundle by an internal $E$-coring in $H$-comodules where $E$ is an $H$-comodule algebra which is itself $H$-Hopf-Galois. This article focuses on the cleft case. As corings involve bimodules and morphisms of bimodules we extend the Doi--Takeuchi correspondence to bimodule $H$-comodules between cleft extensions on one side and bimodules of $H$-coinvariants equipped with bimodule $H$-measurings compatible with 2-cocycles on the other side. In fact, the correspondences for algebras and for bimodules are parts of a biequivalence of suitable bicategories defined in this article. As a corollary one obtains a correspondence between cleft $H$-extensions of corings and corings equipped with a nonabelian Čech 1-cocycle covalued in $H$.
Residue Sums Modulo Products of Two Distinct Odd Primes
Haobo Ma; Mircea Merca; Wenlin Zhang

Let $S_m(a)$ denote the sum of the least positive residues in one multiplicative period of $a$ modulo $m$, of length $k$. We study the equality $S_m(a)=mk/2$ for $m=pq$, where $p,q$ are distinct odd primes and $k$ is even. Complementary pairing settles subgroups containing $-1$; the remaining cases depend on their embedding in the two local unit groups. At index four, we exclude mixed cyclic subgroups with biquadratic annihilator and classify every eligible imprimitive quartic kernel using two odd integer moments at its prime conductor. For each fixed conductor, the proportion of admissible second primes giving equality is $1/4$ or $1/2$; full coset balance has proportion $1/4$. For primitive quartic characters, classical triangular character-sum identities yield explicit short-sum criteria, and the relative class-number formula gives an obstruction to a centered coset. At index six, we give structural counts and construct an infinite family modulo $19q$ in which nonzero sextic and quadratic moments cancel. These applications use a standard odd-character expansion, which also recovers the known index-two balance classification and determines the sign of its deviation. A reproducible census for $pq\le10000$ counts $75\,090$ eligible cyclic subgroups and identifies $101$ mixed index-four subgroups whose own sum is centered although some coset sums are not.
Improved Training of Strong Stochastic Flow Maps
Zander W. Blasingame; Antonio Franca; Raul Minan; Christian Koke; Niklas Rindtorff; Alexander Tong

Stochastic flow maps promise few-step sampling of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) by learning to directly jump between times along the solution path, yet training these models to learn this solution map remains difficult. The primary obstacle is the Brownian path itself: it is an infinite-dimensional object which needs to be passed to the neural network and is nowhere differentiable, which makes the implementation of derivative-based losses that power the state-of-the-art deterministic flow maps just out of reach. We identify two core design principles which address these issues: a) represent the Brownian path with a basis which carries higher-order local information, and b) train with an objective that forces the network to use the full representation of the path, not just the first order. To address this, we leverage the shifted Legendre polynomial expansion with a Wong-Zakai styled objective, unlocking derivative-based losses.
