For an artinian complete intersection of forms of degree $d$, we prove that the multiplication by a general linear form is injective up to degree $\frac{3d-1}2$, independently of the number of variables. This is accomplished using algebraic and geometric properties of the union of two complete intersection curves and their general hyperplane sections. As a consequence, we solve, for any $d\ge 4$, the problem about the maximal variation of the hyperplane sections of a smooth hypersurface of degree $d$ posed by A. Beauville.
The Bourgain, Brezis, Mironescu localization for deterministic obstacle problems

We study the asymptotic behaviour of families of fractional energies normalized according to the Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu formula and defined on functions satisfying a pinning condition on possibly aperiodic families of small obstacles. The result of the simultaneous limit depends crucially on the critical rescaling chosen for the obstacles.
Partially Adaptive Robust Optimization for Uncertain Fluid Processing Networks
Roi Ben-Gigi; Evgeny Shindin; and Shimrit Shtern

This paper studies the problem of controlling fluid approximations of processing networks under uncertainty. Classical robust formulations for such models rely on static (here-and-now) control decisions that must remain feasible for all realizations of uncertainty, often leading to highly conservative solutions. We propose a partially adaptive robust optimization framework that incorporates observed system information into the control policy at the planning point, enabling less conservative and more responsive decisions while retaining worst-case guarantees. Our approach begins by modeling the fluid network dynamics as a Separated Continuous Linear Program (SCLP) in the server-effort formulation. We introduce continuous-time extensions of the budgeted uncertainty set and develop three families of uncertainty structures appropriate for fluid-flow systems. For each family, we derive the corresponding robust counterpart. Since these robust counterparts include uncertainty in the objective, they cannot be solved directly by the classical SCLP--Simplex method. To address this challenge, we develop a hybrid algorithm that integrates an extended SCLP framework with the Saddle-Point Frank--Wolfe (SP--FW) method. This hybrid approach combines tractable continuous-time optimization with efficient saddle-point updates, yielding feasible and near-optimal partially adaptive robust solutions. The resulting methodology advances robust fluid control by enabling uncertainty-aware, dynamically informed decision policies while preserving computational tractability.
Equidistribution, multipliers, and moving targets in polynomial families

We study equidistribution of parameters for each of which a polynomial has a cycle with a prescribed moving multiplier in the full critically marked or unicritical polynomial families of a given degree $d>1$. For the full critically marked monic polynomial family $f=(f_λ)$, $λ\in\mathbb{C}^{d-1}$, of degree $d$, letting $p_{f,n}^*(λ,w)$ be the multiplier polynomial for cycles of formal exact period $n$ having multiplier $w$, we show that for any target sequence $w_n=d^na_n$ satisfying $n^{-1}\log|a_n|\to\ell\in[-\infty,+\infty)$, the averaged current of integration $ν(n)^{-1}[p_{f,n}^*(\cdot,w_n)=0]$ along the zero divisor of $p_{f,n}^*(\cdot,w_n)$ tends to the $(1,1)$-current $\mathrm{d}\mathrm{d}^c\max\{L_d,\log d+\ell\}$ in the sense of currents on $\mathbb{C}^{d-1}$ as $n\to\infty$, where $L_d$ is the Lyapunov exponent function and $ν(n)$ is the degree of the $n$th formal exact dynatomic polynomial associated to $f$. We also obtain the corresponding equidistribution theorem for the unicritical family $f_λ(z)=z^d+λ$, $λ\in\mathbb{C}$, of degree $d$. The proof combines thermodynamic formalism, the Eremenko--Levin multiplier bound, and a comparison principle for plurisubharmonic functions, in a partly quantitative manner. A key ingredient is the vanishing of the bifurcation measure on the boundary of every component of the interior of the connectedness locus for the full critically marked family, which we show using Kiwi's study of critical portraits and rational laminations.
Degree Stability of Parallel Greedy Matching in Random Graphs

We study a natural synchronous greedy matching process in Erdős-Rényi random graphs $\mathbb{G}(n,p)$ and give a rigorous analysis of this parallel stochastic dynamics. The process evolves as follows: in each round, every unmatched vertex proposes to a uniformly random neighbour, and mutually proposing pairs are matched and removed from the graph, after which the process repeats on the residual graph. We consider the density regime $p=Θ(\log^{1+ε} n/n)$ for any constant $ε>0$, which lies just above the threshold for the existence of a perfect matching. We show that, with high probability, for $Θ(\log^{1+ε} n)$ rounds, every unmatched vertex keeps a constant fraction of its initial degree in the residual graph, simultaneously for all vertices and all rounds. By then, the process has matched a constant fraction of the vertices. Our analysis tracks fine-grained invariants that control the evolution of individual vertex degrees, rather than directly tracking the global degree distribution. At the local level, we analyze the per-round degree loss of a vertex via a neighbourhood-exposure martingale. We show that structural sparsity of $\mathbb{G}(n,p)$ yields $O(1)$ variance and thus the per-round degree loss is strongly concentrated around its conditional expectation. At the global level, these local concentration bounds control the increments of a martingale tracking cumulative degree loss over many rounds, allowing us to show that vertex degrees remain stable for $Ω(\log^{1+ε} n)$ rounds.
A Method for Linearization of Systems of Quadratic Equations
A. A. Pak; A. S. Pak

Integrating physical conservation laws into deep neural architectures remains a central SciML challenge. Soft-penalty approaches, including many PINNs, may be sensitive to loss weighting and optimization; generic DEQ and implicit-layer solvers may require instance-dependent iteration counts. We study a norm-linearization scheme for networked systems with linear continuity constraints and nonlinear quadratic or power-law energy balances. We derive sharp universal and finite-$n$ bounds on relative variance and, via the weighted Kantorovich inequality, relate them to worst-case single-step squared-norm distortion when target and operating states have a bounded multiplicative ratio. Euler's theorem shows that the scheme is Newton's method for degree-one norm differences $u_i(\mathbf{x})-v_i(\mathbf{x})=0$. Recasting raw degree-$α$ balances as norm differences removes radial curvature, yields a degree-zero homogeneous Jacobian, eliminates the affine Newton term, and row-equilibrates the loop Jacobian at equilibrium. Under regularity and nonsingularity assumptions, this gives local quadratic convergence for Darcy-Weisbach ($α=2$) and Hazen-Williams ($α=1.852$) models. We implement dynamic sign partitioning in a FlowDEQ layer using a reduced incidence matrix and implicit-function adjoint differentiation.
TIGER: Tunable-Geometry Accelerated Gradient Sliding with Adaptive Safeguards under Similarity
Darina M. Dvinskikh; Anton G. Novitskii; Ewsey R. Obzherin; Alexander V. Gasnikov

We study distributed composite optimization under function similarity when synchronized gradient queries dominate local computation. We propose TIGER, an accelerated gradient-sliding method in problem-adapted Bregman geometry. The method applies to constrained non-Euclidean domains, allows the communicated correction term to be nonconvex, and terminates each local subproblem using a computable stationarity residual. Each iteration reuses one synchronized correction gradient during the local solve and makes a second query to construct the composite subgradient for the mirror step. Under relative strong convexity and cocoercivity of the stabilized model error, the communication complexity is $O((1+\sqrt{δ_ω/μ})\log(1/\varepsilon))$, where $μ$ is the relative strong-convexity parameter and $δ_ω$ is a geometry-adjusted similarity parameter. The analysis recovers the Hessian-similarity rate in Hilbert geometry and provides an explicit finite bound on $δ_ω$ in entropy geometry on a truncated simplex. We also introduce Adaptive TIGER, which selects the stabilization coefficient and the similarity estimate during the run. Under uniform backtracking bounds, the adaptive method has the same asymptotic communication order as fixed-parameter TIGER, including the queries spent on backtracking. Numerical experiments compare Adaptive TIGER with several applicable first-order methods on entropic Wasserstein barycenter problems using the Fashion-MNIST dataset.
Torelli theorem for the moduli spaces of twisted vector bundles on smooth projective curves
Soham Ghosh; Ting Gong; Max Lieblich

We prove Torelli theorems for moduli space of twisted vector bundles on smooth projective curves over an arbitrary field of characteristic $\neq 2$. A twisted Hitchin construction recovers the curve in higher rank and degree, with partial recovery of the twisting class. For rank two with trivial determinant, we recover the curve and the Brauer class from the moduli stack through an ordered Kummer cover and its polarized Jacobian torsor. For odd determinant on hyperelliptic curves, residual gerbes give a relative Desale--Ramanan construction without an actual determinant line bundle over the ground field. An intrinsic polarized Fano torsor recovers the curve and the class, and a corrected polarization obstruction recovers the determinant gerbe. We also give a twisted Newstead construction in genus two, with an explicit descent condition for its converse, and period--index applications. This is the second part in a series of two papers.

We extend the recent work of Caster--Guyer--Samper (2026+) to establish a combinatorial interpretation of the $\textbf{cd}$-index for all $S$-partitionable posets, which includes all polytopes and $S$-shellable spheres. This interpretation is inductive on rank, but does not require passing to the order complex of the poset. We also provide topological interpretations of each $\textbf{cd}$-monomial. Furthermore, we establish a recurrence on the $\textbf{cd}$-indices of shelling components of the $d$-simplex that does not require the use of André permutations, a unimodality result for $\textbf{cd}$-words ending in $\textbf{d}$ for shelling components of the $d$-simplex and the $d$-cube, and provide two families of subdivisions of the boundary of the $d$-simplex whose sequence of $\textbf{cd}$-indices is unbounded on all but the monomial $\textbf{c}^{d+1}$ and all but the two monomials $\textbf{c}^{d+1}$ and $\textbf{d}\textbf{c}^{d-1}$.
From Formulation to Articulation: Considerations for AI-Assisted Research in Information Theory

Recent advances in artificial intelligence have contributed to several information-theoretic results through genuinely different modes: a language model may suggest a proof, participate in an extended mathematical dialogue, coordinate computation, or operate as one component of a search harness. Treating all of these as "AI-discovered mathematics" obscures distinctions that matter for scientific reliability, attribution, and reproducibility. This article examines a set of recent cases through a four-stage pipeline: how the problem was formulated; how AI participated in finding a solution; how the resulting analytical and computational claims were verified; and how machine-generated outputs were translated into mathematical exposition for human understanding. Based on these cases, we recommend that research publications (1) disclose the nature and extent of AI assistance at each stage, (2) report verification of analytical reasoning separately from certification of numerical computations, and (3) place more emphasis on articulating the underlying ideas, techniques, and interpretations.
An explicit Dennis trace and its compatibility with Koszul duality

In this paper, we construct explicit Dennis trace maps from algebraic $K$-theory to Hochschild homology for dg module and curved dg comodule categories, and prove their compatibility with derived Koszul duality. For this, we construct a natural chain map $τ$ from the chains on the newly defined thickened nerve to the total complex of the dg cyclic nerve, with explicit formulas incorporating morphisms and coherent higher homotopies, which generalizes McCarthy's approach. This $τ$ construction works both for modules over dg algebras and for cdg comodules over counital conilpotent curved dg coalgebras. Combining the $τ$ with the dg-enriched Waldhausen $S_\bullet$-construction and a Hochschild delooping theorem yields the Dennis trace maps. For thick subcategories corresponding under derived Koszul duality, we prove that the induced $K$-theory equivalences and Hochschild homology isomorphisms fit into natural commutative diagrams with these trace maps.
KernelPack-JAX: a meshless differentiable GPU framework for node generation and forward and inverse PDE problems
Alberto Cattaneo; M. Keith Ballard; Robert M. Kirby; Grady B. Wright; Varun Shankar

We present KernelPack-JAX, a meshless, differentiable, GPU framework in JAX for solving forward and inverse PDE problems in domains whose boundaries, including internal obstacles, are given only by samples of their smooth pieces. Our node generator is based on a new stacked representation of piecewise-smooth boundaries, in which a parametric partition of unity of each smooth piece induces the supports of a curl-free implicit partition of unity of the whole boundary. This representation keeps the edges and corners of the boundary and classifies every point of space without a global fit. Boundary and interior nodes are then selected by a parallel greedy independent-set algorithm that reproduces sequential Poisson-disk sampling exactly. We discretize elliptic and parabolic problems with radial basis function-generated finite differences (RBF-FD) on stencils selected by a new visibility heuristic to avoid crossing the boundary, with ghost nodes for the boundary conditions. In addition, our framework exposes a GPU sparse direct solver to JAX as a differentiable linear solve, so that Jacobians of time-dependent problems cost a small multiple of a forward solve. We derive error estimates that separate consistency from stability and bound the parameter error by the forward error. We demonstrate high-order convergence for Darcy flow, reaction-diffusion, and advection-diffusion in 2D and 3D domains, including one with an internal obstacle, and show that the recovered parameters largely follow the forward errors. We also present timings for every stage.
On elements of degree $g$ in the separating semigroup of a real curve of genus $g$
G. B. Mikhalkin; S. Yu. Orevkov

Let $C$ be a separating real algebraic curve of genus $g$ whose real locus consists of $r$ components and let $S=\mathrm{Sep}(C)$ be its separating semigroup. An element $δ\in S$ is called extendable if $δ+\mathbb N_0^r\subset S$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{n\in\mathbb Z\mid n\ge 0\}$. We prove that an element of $S$ is extendable if it is realizable by a separating mobile divisor of degree $g$ and projective rank 1.
Acceleration of Generalized Conditional Gradient Methods

We develop an adaptive acceleration of generalized conditional gradient methods for convex objectives with a strongly convex regularizer. A computable primal--dual residual certifies Lyapunov decrease without evaluating the regularizer or any Hessian. Each iteration accepts a balanced accelerated trial when the residual is nonpositive; otherwise it takes a mirror-descent step with doubling backtracking and sets the auxiliary parameter explicitly from the dual decrease and the stopping gap. Under uniform strong-convexity and smoothness bounds on the relevant sublevel set, the method converges globally at a linear rate. Near a nondegenerate minimizer, balanced trials pass above a fixed curvature threshold. The adaptive curvature updates then guarantee a positive fraction of accelerated steps and a local accelerated rate. The method applies directly to entropically regularized Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) steps whose energies contain nonlocal interaction terms with nondiagonal Hessians. Experiments on JKO steps for granular media and for Poisson--Nernst--Planck systems, in one and three dimensions, show that the method reduces both oracle calls and computing time by a large fraction compared with generalized conditional gradient methods with fixed or adaptive step sizes.
Topological Quantum Gates on FCIs with Bounded Quantum Geometry

Two-band 2D fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) have recently been shown, in principle, to admit unusual anyonic order, associated with Bloch Hopfions localized in momentum space. Here we show that bounding the integrated quantum metric along one primitive Brillouin-zone cycle may refine this topological order to $|C|$ distinct braiding observables, cyclically permuted by lattice translations, for Chern numbers $|C| > 1$. The cyclic structure entails mildly non-abelian braiding phases and otherwise matches the spectral flow exhibited by the FCI's hybrid Wannier states, with the metric bound equivalently a bound on the states' real-space spread. We give a classification of quantum gates in principle implementable on this topological order; among them we find the non-Clifford T-gate and the non-Clifford entangling CCZ-gate. This points to novel pathways to fault-tolerant quantum processes within the known orbital structure of FCIs, potentially informing experimental searches towards hardware for future topological quantum computers.
\textit{In situ} certification of multiparticle indistinguishability in a generic interferometer

We propose a scalable and efficient \textit{in situ} method for assessing the multiparticle indistinguishability of identical bosons or fermions in quantum interference experiments on linear interferometers by harnessing quantum parallelism and the bunching/anti-bunching tendencies of these particles. The proposed certification method can be applied to any generic linear interferometer. For particles occupying distinct input ports of a Haar-random unitary interferometer, the number of experimental runs required to attain a prescribed statistical precision is polynomial in the number of particles, the interferometer size, and the inverse precision, with high probability. Our method is robust under losses: for uniform particle losses, the polynomial scaling is preserved when the inverse single-particle survival probability is polynomially bounded. Our scheme is especially suitable for certifying the indistinguishability of single photons in large-scale interference experiments, such as Boson Sampling in the regime of quantum advantage over classical computation.
Improvement of the Crossing Lemma for the odd-crossing number

A graph is called $1$-planar if it can be drawn in the plane so that every edge is crossed by at most one other edge. It is known that the maximum number of edges of $1$-planar graphs is $4n-8$. We prove the following generalization. A graph is $1$-odd-planar if it can be drawn in the plane so that every edge is crossed {\em an odd number of times} by at most one other edge. We show that the maximum number of edges of $1$-odd-planar graphs is also $4n-8$. As a consequence, we improve the constant coefficient in the Crossing Lemma for the odd-crossing number.
Advancing the Theory of Sheffer Sequences via Dual Padé Rational Approximants

Sheffer sequences offer an operational framework that unifies a wide range of classical polynomial families. In this article, a rational approximation is developed for both the amplitude and the delta-operator symbol in the exponential generating function. The resulting Padé Sheffer polynomials are shown, within the umbral calculus framework, to retain the Sheffer structure. Explicit operational representations are obtained, together with finite-order differential recurrences and closed-form connection constants characterizing the deviation from the underlying polynomial family. An important consequence of the construction is that rational generating indicators reduce the usual transcendental Lagrange inversion problem to a finite multinomial computation. The framework also suggests an interpretation in terms of weighted finite automata, linking polynomial constructions with state-space dynamics for unbounded combinatorial partitions.
An A-B-C Coordinate Encoding for Exact Boundary-Cycle Extraction on Hexagonal Lattices

We study an integer-coordinate encoding of boundary incidences for finite subsets of the regular hexagonal tiling. Each selected cell contributes six ordered records with endpoints in two role-distinguished classes, point and tail. Identical records from neighboring cells cancel, and the surviving records form a disjoint union of cycles, including the exterior boundaries of disconnected components and the boundaries of holes. We derive the actual even- and odd-row record formulas from the A--B--C transforms used in Hexagones 2.0, prove exact shared-edge identities and the global role-qualified incidence structure, and thereby obtain an unconditional correctness theorem for the abstract coordinate construction. We compare the encoding with an independent exact cube-coordinate half-edge hashing implementation, proving an incidence isomorphism and checking 504 finite regions. We give an expected-linear-time indexed algorithm and distinguish it from the historical fixed-capacity C traversal, whose sentinel and closure conventions do not inherit the theorem automatically. The claim is a compact coordinate realization of a known planar boundary principle, not historical priority or a new three-axis lattice.
Semi-supervised learning on singular data sets

We propose to model singular data clouds by subanalytic sets, and develop an approach to semi-supervised learning in this setting. It relies on a Morrey-type embedding for Sobolev spaces relative to globally subanalytic measures with possibly singular support. As an illustration, we present a greedy method based on a Monte Carlo approximation of the Sobolev norm of the candidate solutions. We report numerical experiments on point clouds sampled from real algebraic varieties, as well as a test on a classification problem based on MNIST images downsampled into $7\times7$.
Mixing time of the tranvection walk on $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z}_p)$

We consider a Markov chain on $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z}_p)$, the space of $n \times n$ matrices with determinant $1$ and entries in $\mathbb{Z}_p$, for $p$ a prime number. At every time step, the chain updates by adding one row (or its negation) to another. By way of a log-Sobolev inequality, we show the mixing time of this chain is at most of order $O(n^2p^2(\log n +\log \log p))$.
Endpoint capacity at strictly stable minimal boundaries:Gaussian layers and Schwarzschild deficits

Let $(M^n,\mathfrak g)$, $3\le n\le7$, be a one-ended asymptotically flat manifold whose boundary $Σ$ is a connected, strictly stable, outermost minimal hypersurface. As $p\downarrow1$, the $p$-capacity of $Σ$ converges to its area, by a theorem of Fogagnolo and Mazzieri. We establish a higher-order asymptotic expansion governed by a single function on $Σ$: the positive solution $g$ of the reciprocal Jacobi equation $Jg=g^{-1}$. After a universal term, the first correction is determined by the average of $\log g$, and the capacitary potential drops from one to zero across a Gaussian boundary layer of width $g\sqrt{p-1}$; under the normalized energy measure, the logarithm of the gradient has limiting variance $\frac12$ plus the variance of $\log g$. In dimension three, assuming in addition that $R_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{II}|^2\ge0$ along $Σ$, we identify the capacity deficit of $Σ$ relative to the Schwarzschild horizon of the same area at order $p-1$: it is nonnegative, vanishes exactly when the induced metric of $Σ$ is round and $R_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{II}|^2\equiv0$, and controls the deviation of $g$ from a constant through a relative-entropy identity.
Distinctness and Algebraic Degrees of Inverted Kloosterman Sums

We study the distinctness and algebraic degrees of inverted Kloosterman sums over finite extensions of $\mathbb{F}_p$. For each $d\geq 2$, we prove that the $(d-1)$-dimensional sums over $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$ are equal precisely when their parameters are Frobenius conjugate, provided that $p\equiv 1\pmod d$, $p>2d+1$, and $p$ does not divide the nonzero integer $2(d+1)^d-\binom{2d}{d}^2$. For two-dimensional sums over $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$, the same conclusion holds for $2\leq r\leq 5$, $p\equiv 1\pmod 3$, and $p>3r+1$. In both cases we determine the algebraic degree of every sum in terms of the minimal polynomial of its parameter. The proof combines a cyclic-carry analysis of a Gauss-sum expansion with the recovery of power traces from a formal logarithm.
Jonah Berean-Dutcher; Clay Cordova; Julio Parra-Martinez; Richard Tuddenham

We classify possible topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions with up to 22 anyons in the bosonic case and up to 26 in the fermionic case, through the modular data of modular and supermodular tensor categories. We construct such data via congruence representations of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ using a numerical optimization algorithm that scales to high rank. We chart the relations between the resulting theories, including anyon condensations and Chern-Simons realizations. We find examples of modular data that do not appear to arise from any Chern-Simons theory by any sequence of condensations of anyons or gaugings of ordinary global symmetries. These examples give qualitatively new topological quantum field theories, which go beyond any notion of gauge theory. For examples in this class with 11 and 12 anyon types, we solve the pentagon and hexagon equations explicitly, showing that these modular data are realized by full unitary topological quantum field theories. We also introduce https://www.AnyonAtlas.org, an online resource for exploring the data.
Yielding-dependent Taylor dispersion in electrokinetic-magnetohydrodynamic Casson microflows
Nanda Poddar; Debabrata Das; Suman Chakraborty

Longitudinal dispersion in a yielding fluid depends on the velocity distribution and on how the flow is maintained. We study a neutral tracer in pressure-assisted electrokinetic and magnetohydrodynamic flow of a Casson fluid through a slit microchannel. The nonlinear stress and velocity equations determine the yielded layers, the unyielded core and the axial flow. Mei's multiple-scale homogenization of the advection-diffusion equation then separates transverse relaxation, mean drift and longitudinal spreading, yielding the Taylor-Aris auxiliary problem and effective diffusivity. An exact pressure-driven solution gives cubic decay of the mean velocity and eighth-power decay of the dispersion enhancement near flow arrest. Under fixed pressure and electrical forcing, increasing the yield parameter from $Y=0$ to $0.7$ moves the optimum Hartmann number from $Ha_p=0.696$ to $2.634$, while the corresponding normalized diffusivity decreases from $D_T^{\mathrm C}=1.454$ to $1.015$. At fixed mean throughput and $Ha_p=1$, the trend reverses: $D_T^{\mathrm C}$ increases from $1.000433$ to $1.002311$. The homogenized energy identity traces this difference to the velocity departure from the sectional mean, including that within the unyielded core. Analytical limiting solutions, direct concentration calculations, numerical convergence studies and a coupled Casson shear test support the reduced-flow predictions. An electrolyte-based dimensional assessment identifies the magnetic optima as theoretical forcing states for representative aqueous microchannels. These results are relevant to predicting longitudinal tracer spreading in microchannels carrying fluids with a yield stress, whether pressure or throughput is controlled.
Negative-Definite Plumbings and New Unknotting Numbers

We use Neumann's normal form to decide whether the double branched cover of a knot bounds a negative-definite plumbing tree in either orientation, starting from the recognised Seifert or graph-manifold structure of the cover. For many non-alternating knots with at most thirteen crossings whose unknotting numbers were unknown, this identifies the cases in which the Heegaard Floer homology of the cover can be computed from such a plumbing, and shows for most of the others that it cannot. We determine 112 new unknotting numbers. For 43 of them, the lower bound rests on Heegaard Floer homology computed from the plumbing; for the other 69, it comes from linking pairings and from a theorem of McCoy and Park on special alternating knots. Finally, we show that the knot 13n1587 is a further explicit counterexample to the Bernhard--Jablan conjecture, after 13n3370.
Categorical Torelli theorem for smooth Fano varieties

Let $X$ be a smooth Fano variety and $H$ an ample line bundle with $-K_X=rH$ and $r\le\dim X-2$. We prove that the appropriately defined Kuznetsov component of $X$ with respect to $H$, together with its rotation functor, determines $(X,H)$ when $H$ is very ample, and more generally when $H$ is globally generated and the image of the morphism defined by $|H|$ has a hypersurface as projective dual. As a consequence we prove Perry's conjecture, which predicts that a smooth Fano variety $X$ is determined up to isomorphism by the orthogonal complement $\mathcal{O}_X^{\perp}$ of its structure sheaf in $\mathrm{D}^b(X)$, for all smooth Fano varieties of dimension at least three with very ample anticanonical bundle, and more generally with globally generated anticanonical bundle whose image has a hypersurface as dual. We also prove it when a multiple $-qK_X$ is very ample and the corresponding embedding is cut out by equations of degree at most $(\mathrm{dim} X-1)/q$. The idea is to read off $X$ from its hyperplane sections. We show that the Kuznetsov component with its rotation functor contains the residual categories of all hyperplane sections of $X$, singular ones included. The sections whose categories are not smooth form the projective dual of $X$, and classical projective duality recovers $X$. When $H$ is not very ample, the nodes of a single tangent hyperplane section, defined over a function field and detected by its singularity category, recover $X$ as a finite cover of its image. Applications include Fano hypersurfaces, all prime Fano threefolds of index one and genus at least three, cyclic covers of quadrics, Fano complete intersections and Gushel--Mukai varieties.
Polynomial bounds for the stability of associated primes of monomial ideals

Let $I$ be a nonzero proper monomial ideal in ${\rm k}[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$, and let $d$ be the maximal degree of a minimal monomial generator. We prove that the index of stability of the associated primes of its ordinary powers satisfies \[ {\rm astab}(I)\le\frac{(4e)^{r-1}}4\,d^{r-1}\qquad(r\ge3), \] while ${\rm astab}(I)=1$ for $r=2$. If $I$ has $s\ge2$ minimal generators, we also obtain \[ {\rm astab}(I)\le\min\{r,s\}(s-1)d^{\min\{r-1,s-2\}}. \] The first estimate answers Hoa's question on polynomial bounds. The proofs reduce stabilization to integer optimization for a matrix whose last row records the power of the ideal. We bound the degrees of its circuits and Graver basis elements and prove proximity estimates for optimal solutions in fixed fibers. A Steinitz rearrangement and a lattice-point count in the difference body of a simplex give the generator-independent bound. The matrix estimates hold for arbitrary indexed integral configurations in a simplex and real linear objective functions. The stability bounds hold over an arbitrary field, without normality or equigeneration assumptions.
Efficient estimation of measures of functional dependence

Measures of functional dependence that characterize both independence and perfect dependence have attracted growing interest. Despite their appealing theoretical properties, existing rank- and graph-based estimators can suffer from substantial bias under general dependence, limiting their usefulness for statistical inference. Moreover, a systematic and practically accessible framework for mitigating such bias while achieving semiparametric efficiency remains largely unavailable. In this paper, we develop a general framework for efficient estimation of measures of functional dependence through sample-splitting and cross-fitting. Our approach enables systematic bias reduction and semiparametrically efficient inference, and thus offers a flexible and theoretically grounded alternative to existing rank- and graph-based methods.
Torsion Cycles in Projective Threefolds:From Serre's Construction to Artin-Mumford

The torsion subgroup of third integral cohomology is a birational invariant of smooth projective complex threefolds; its nonvanishing obstructs stable rationality. We recall a proof using Hironaka's elimination of indeterminacies and the integral blowup formula. The Godeaux--Serre construction and Poincaré duality imply that every finite abelian group is the third integral cohomology group of a smooth projective complex threefold. This classical realization also has a description through families of concurrent plane lines. Their incidence threefolds have smooth normalizations, obtained by an explicit blowup and described as projective-line bundles over smooth surfaces. The Lefschetz theorem determines the fundamental group of these surfaces, and the projective bundle formula computes the third cohomology. The resulting threefolds are birational to products of surfaces with the projective line, and their torsion three-cycles are represented by sphere bundles over loops. Examples and the comparison with the unirational Artin--Mumford threefold explain the role of the base surface and the distinction between smooth blowups and resolution of a singular space.
Maksym Chaudkhari; Kate Juschenko; Kyrylo Muliarchyk

We prove that Thompson's groups $F$, $T$ and $V$ are sofic. As a corollary, all of them are also hyperlinear and not permutation stable. The proof relies on an explicit construction of sofic approximations to $F$ and $V$. Moreover, the construction allows us to obtain effective quantitative bounds on the parameters of sofic approximations.
Symmetry algebra of a charged harmonic oscillator in the field of the Dirac magnetic monopole

A charged particle bound by an isotropic harmonic potential to a Dirac magnetic monopole, with the centrifugal term that makes the orbits close, has degeneracies beyond rotational invariance: for integer $q$, the product of the electric and magnetic charges, the levels are those of the oscillator with the states of angular momentum $l<|q|$ removed. The conserved rank-2 tensor $T$ built from the ladder operators that accounts for them was identified thirty-five years ago, but the algebra it generates with the angular momentum $\mathbf{J}$ was not obtained. We obtain its relations in covariant form and identify it. It is polynomial but not quadratic, and the shift $T'=T+2(H-1)J^{(2)}$ by the quadrupole of $\mathbf{J}$, and only this one, makes all commutators polynomials in $\mathbf{J}$. In each sector of fixed energy and $J_z$, $(\mathbf{J}^2,T'_{zz})$ generates a cubic algebra of Heun--Racah type whose parameters are symmetric, up to a scalar shift, in the magnetic charge and the magnetic quantum number. At $q=0$, $T$ is the algebraic Heun operator of the pair (Casimir of $\mathfrak{so}(3)$, quadrupole of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$): the symmetry algebra is the $\mathfrak{so}(3)$-covariant extension of a Heun--Racah algebra. We define it abstractly and classify its multiplicity-free finite-dimensional representations at the energies of the system: besides the levels, they include, for nonzero integer $q$, a second family carried by the states the monopole removes, the kernel of the Newman--Penrose operator. All relations are derived from the dynamical algebra of the ladder operators and hold for integer and half-integer charges alike.
A data-based conservative reduced collision model for the Boltzmann equation

The evaluation of the quadratic collision operator is one of the major computational bottlenecks in solving the Boltzmann equation owing to the high dimensionality and the nonlinear structure of the collision term. In this work, a conservative reduced collision (RC) model is developed within the discrete velocity framework. The bilinear collision operator is approximated through a kernel tensor preassembled with the problem-dependent reduced bases for the distribution function and the collision term. Consequently, online evaluation of the quadratic collision operator is reduced to tensor contractions. Exact discrete conservation of mass, momentum, and energy is enforced by constructing the collision basis in the orthogonal complement of the space spanned by the discrete collision invariants. Several numerical experiments validate the efficiency of this RC model.

We determine the $G$-birational rigidity of the $G$-Fano variety $\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1$ for all finite subgroups $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1)$.
Rapid Mixing for Sampling Colorings of Random Graphs up to Tree Uniqueness Threshold

We study the mixing time of the single-site Glauber dynamics for sampling proper \(q\)-colorings on sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs \(\mathcal{G}(n, d/n)\). We prove that, whenever \(q \ge (1 + o_d(1))d\), Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time with high probability over \(\mathcal{G}(n, d/n)\) for all sufficiently large integer \(n\). This improves the previous bound \(q = (α^* + o_d(1))d\) where \(α^* = 1.7632...\) is the unique solution of \(x = \exp(1/x)\) on \([1, \infty)\) by Efthymiou, Hayes, Štefankovič, and Vigoda (SODA, 2018) and asymptotically matches the uniqueness threshold on infinite regular trees. Our proof has three main ingredients. First we establish logarithmic bounds on the spectral and coupling independence constants of the Gibbs distribution by extending the tree analysis of Chen, Liu, Mani, and Moitra (J. ACM, 2026). Second, we extend the entropy-factorization framework for two-spin systems on random graphs, developed by Bezáková, Galanis, Goldberg, and Štefankovič (TALG, 2024), to proper colorings by introducing a buffer around high-degree vertices. Finally, we compare the resulting heat-bath block dynamics with the single-site Glauber dynamics.
Entropy Stable Element-Local Continuous-Discontinuous Residual Correction Summation-By-Parts Discretization
Zelalem Arega Worku; David C. Del Rey Fernandez

Residual correction provides an efficient alternative to two-point volume flux differencing for enforcing entropy stability in high-order discretizations of hyperbolic partial differential equations. We develop an element-local residual-correction summation-by-parts (SBP) method that combines continuous-SBP (C-SBP) and discontinuous-SBP (D-SBP) coupling on conforming meshes. The construction retains continuous assembly without simultaneous approximation terms (SATs) wherever suitable, restricts SATs to selected discontinuous facets, and permits the coupling to change in time as a foundation for adaptive discretizations. The scalar entropy defect and a graph-based distribution vector acting on conservative variables are computed entirely from element-local data, without neighboring states, auxiliary gradients, or correction SATs. The same correction applies to every facet partition, including the pure C-SBP and D-SBP limits. For fixed partitions, we establish conservation and entropy identities for each element residual, exact global conservation, entropy stability up to an explicit regularization defect, and design-order consistency. Changes in the partition are handled by a mass-weighted orthogonal projection that preserves conservative moments and convex admissible sets, does not increase entropy, and does not amplify error in the broken norm. Numerical experiments in one to three dimensions show that the hybrid method retains the smooth-solution accuracy of its D-SBP endpoint under repeated repartitioning. The nonlinear tests demonstrate robustness comparable to Hadamard-form two-point-flux discretizations, particularly when coupled with artificial dissipation.
On the maximally edge-connected square graphs with degree sequence conditions

Let $G=(V(G),E(G))$ be a finite connected simple graph. The edge-connectivity $λ(G)$ of $G$ is the minimum number of edges that must be removed to make $G$ disconnected. We call $G$ maximally edge-connected when $λ(G)=δ(G)$, where $δ(G)$ is the minimum degree of $G$. The square graph $G^2$ of $G$ is the graph with vertex set $V(G)$, where two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G^2$ precisely when their distance in $G$ is at most two. In this paper, first we prove that if $λ(G)\geq4$ and $λ(G^2)<δ(G^2)$, then $λ(G^2)>λ(G)^{3/2}-\frac54λ(G)$, which extends the result in \cite{ChenXu} from the edge-connectivity range $4\leqλ(G)\leq7$ to $λ(G)\geq4$. Then we show that $G^2$ is maximally edge-connected if one of the following conditions hold: (i) $δ(G)\geq\lfloor(n+2)/4\rfloor$, or $δ(G)\leq\lfloor(n+2)/4\rfloor-1$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{2k}d_{n+1-i}\geq k(n-4)-2δ(G)+3$, where $k$ is an integer satisfying $2\leq k\leqδ(G)+2$ and $d_1\geq d_2\geq\cdots\geq d_n$ are the degrees of $G$; (ii) $d_{n-δ(G)}+d_n\geq(3n-9)/4$.
Inequalities for Higher-Order Logarithmic Differences of Boros--Moll Coefficients
Cindy C. Y. Gu; Yafeng Liu; Matthew H. Y. Xie

Let $d_i(m)$ denote the coefficient of $x^i$ in the Boros--Moll polynomial $P_m(x)$. We prove that the sequence $\{d_{i-1}(m)d_{i+1}(m)/d_i(m)^2\}_{i=1}^{m-1}$ is strictly log-concave for every $m\ge4$, settling a conjecture of Chen and Gu. For every $m\ge 3$, we show that the consecutive ratios $d_i(m)/d_{i-1}(m)$ form a strictly log-convex sequence for $1\le i\le\lfloor m/2\rfloor+1$ and a strictly log-concave sequence for $\lfloor m/2\rfloor\le i\le m$, as conjectured by Zhao. For each fixed $i\ge 1$, we establish $(-1)^{r-1}Δ_m^r\log d_i(m)>0$ for $r\ge 2$ and $m\ge i$, where $Δ_m$ denotes the forward difference with respect to $m$. For $i=0$, we obtain the opposite inequalities. We thereby prove a conjecture of Jiang and Wang and two further conjectures of Zhao. For every integer $i\ge 0$, we prove strict infinite log-monotonicity of the sequence $\{d_i(m-1)d_i(m+1)/(\binom{m}{i+1}d_i(m)^2)\}_{m\ge i+1}$, strengthening another conjecture of Zhao. We further show that every positive real power of the binomially normalized ratio sequence is a Hausdorff moment sequence with a strictly totally positive Hankel matrix. We also obtain asymptotic formulas for forward differences of arbitrary fixed order, resolving a conjecture of Jiang and Wang. For integers $i\ge 1$, we prove that the sequence $\{2^n d_i(i)/d_i(i+n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ is an infinitely divisible Hausdorff moment sequence and that the Hankel matrix $[1/d_i(i+j+k)^τ]_{j,k\ge 0}$ is strictly totally positive for every $τ>0$. For the integral interpolation, we show that the Hausdorff moment property of the normalized reciprocals holds precisely when the positive real coefficient index is at least $1/4$.
The Corners of Ramanujan: Partial- and False-Theta Companions to Third-Order Mock Theta Functions
George E. Andrews; Mohamed El Bachraoui

Most of the traditional third-order mock theta functions occur naturally as specialized values of partition-rank generating functions. The same finite rank kernels also occur in the ordinary and odd unimodal-rank series studied previously in the literature. We organize a parallel collection of corner series by retaining these kernels and replacing their quadratic core weights by linear peak weights. Their root-of-unity specializations are governed by partial and false theta identities recorded in Ramanujan's Lost Notebook; in one exceptional case the corner companion is itself a mock theta function. The classical rank series and Ramanujan identities are used as inputs. Our new results include exact two- and three-color partition identities with sparse theta discrepancies and an oriented three-dimensional corner with a distinct tower. In both color cases, positive decompositions separate the colored companion into copies of the relevant odd-corner series and a corresponding decorated even-corner series. Thus both sparse discrepancies become signed differences between natural corner families. Burson's boxed modular involution provides a common rank-refined model for the two corrections, whose surviving fixed points produce the exceptional quadratic sequences. For the side rank of the three-dimensional corners we obtain an exact formula at $z=-1$, a strict parity bias, quartic and cubic root-of-unity rank-difference identities, and exact equidistribution modulo $3$ on the progression $6n+5$. The cubic identity also gives exact congruence formulas on the progressions $6n+2$ and $6n+3$. We further classify the associated binary triangular support modulo every integer and derive general congruence families.
Oriented Zoll families of minimal hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and $\mathbb{HP}^n$

Let $M$ be either $\mathbb{CP}^n$ or $\mathbb{HP}^n$. We prove that the family $\overline{\mathcal{F}}=\{Σ_σ\}_{σ\in M}$ of minimal geodesic spheres in $M$ characterizes the Fubini-Study metric $\overline{g}$, that is, $\overline{g}$ is the only metric that makes these real hypersurfaces minimal. This result is related to the recent theory of Zoll families of minimal hypersurfaces $(M,g,\mathcal{F}=\{Σ_σ\})\in\mathcal{Z}$. It is conjectured that the only Zoll metric in $\mathbb{CP}^n$ is $\overline{g}$. We present evidence that suggests a similar rigidity of $(\mathbb{CP}^n,\overline{g},\overline{\mathcal{F}})$ in this context of minimal hypersurfaces. Namely, we show that a direct adaptation of Guillemin's Theorem for conformal deformations of Zoll metrics in $\mathbb{S}^2$ is not possible for $(\mathbb{CP}^n,\overline{g},\overline{\mathcal{F}})$, when $p=2n-1$ is a prime number.
Generalized quaternion groups of order $4p$ are $4$-BCI-groups

For a finite group $G$ and a subset $S\subseteq G$, the bi-Cayley graph $\operatorname{BCay}(G,S)$ has vertex set $G\times\{0,1\}$ and edges $\{(x,0),(sx,1)\}$ for $x\in G$ and $s\in S$. The group $G$ is called an $m$-BCI-group if, for all subsets $S,T\subseteq G$ with $|S|\leq m$, the isomorphism $\operatorname{BCay}(G,S)\cong\operatorname{BCay}(G,T)$ implies that $T=gS^α$ for some $g\in G$ and $α\in\operatorname{Aut} G$. We prove that, for every prime $p$, the generalized quaternion group $Q_{4p}$ is a $4$-BCI-group. For $p\geq5$, the proof uses regular coverings and voltage assignments: we pass to quotient graphs modulo the Sylow $p$-subgroup and lift isomorphisms between them.
A dual variational principle for the Moser-Trudinger inequality: existence, uniqueness and stability of extremals

For $p>1$, with $p'=p/(p-1)$, we prove the sharp dual inequality $$ \int_0^1-\log\left(1-\frac{\left|\int_0^xf(y) dy\right|^{p'}}{x}\right) dx\leq\mathsf{K}_p, \qquad \|f\|_{L^p(0,1)}\leq1, $$ where $\mathsf{K}_p$ is the logarithm of the optimal value in Moser's one-dimensional formulation of the Moser-Trudinger inequality. The dual functional follows from the Gibbs variational principle, monotone transport and the Legendre transform. Its supremum is attained, giving a dual proof of the existence theorems of Carleson-Chang (1986) and Hudson-Leckband (2002); the classical concentration threshold is realized by equality cases in Hoelder's inequality. For $p=2$ we prove, with rigorous computer-assisted estimates, that the nonnegative dual maximizer is unique and nondegenerate. Hence the extremal of the Moser-Trudinger inequality on a disk $D$ is unique up to sign, confirming conjectures of Adimurthi-Karthik-Giacomoni (2016) and of Chen-Lu-Xue-Zhu (2026). The positive extremal $u_*$ is nondegenerate, and, writing $\mathcal{M}_D(u)=|D|^{-1}\int_De^{4πu^2} dx$, we obtain $$ \mathcal{M}_D(u_*)-\mathcal{M}_D(u) \geq c \min_{\pm}\|\nabla(u\mp u_*)\|_{L^2(D)}^2 $$ for all $u\in H_0^1(D)$ with $\|\nabla u\|_{L^2(D)}\leq1$. Here $c>0$, and the exponent two is optimal, giving a quantitative stability theorem of Bianchi-Egnell type.

We extend the tangency construction of López de Medrano, Verjovsky and Meersseman from diagonal abelian actions to non-abelian Samelson groups. For these groups the tangency locus is a moment-map zero set: the commutator term in the leafwise Hessian vanishes there, and under an admissibility hypothesis, Kempf--Ness convexity gives a global transversal whose projectivization is a compact complex manifold. The construction includes compact rotation groups and groups with non-closed central rotations. In the latter setting we construct explicit families of complex dimension $2m-3$, $m\geq5$, which are $4$-connected and admit no symplectic form. Their meromorphic function fields are rational of transcendence degree $m-2$, although every holomorphic map to a projective space is constant. We compute their connected automorphism groups and show that they admit no maximal torus action. They are Hopf-surface bundles over compact complex quotients of stable Grassmannian loci; these bases give related examples already in complex dimension five. The families demonstrate that the non-abelian tangency construction reaches beyond compact complex manifolds with maximal torus actions.
The inviscid limit of 2D Navier-Stokes near a self-similar vortex collapse

We study the inviscid limit of the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations with initial vorticity given by three point vortices whose inviscid trajectories collapse self-similarly at $t=1$. For every fixed $0<γ<1$, we prove that the solution is approximated by a superposition of Lamb--Oseen vortices centered at the point-vortex positions, with an $L^1$ error of order $O(ν^{1-γ})$, uniformly for $0<t\le T_ν=1-ν^γ$. We use coordinates adapted to the self-similar collapse and study a long-time inviscid limit problem on the interval $0<s\leγ\log(1/ν)$, with a time-dependent rescaled diffusion coefficient $η(s)$ that tends to zero as $s\to\infty$.
Mixed Tate Chabauty--Kim beyond the polylog quotient
David Corwin; Ishai Dan-Cohen; Martin Lüdtke

We develop an algorithmic approach to mixed Tate Chabauty--Kim theory for the full unipotent fundamental group of $\mathbb{P}^1 \smallsetminus \{0,1,\infty\}$, beyond the polylogarithmic quotient used in previous work. The key step is computing the cocycle evaluation map in the presence of a nontrivial motivic Galois action, using relations among motivic multiple zeta values. This yields explicit Kim functions involving multiple polylogarithms, as well as an algorithm for solving the $S$-unit equation whose halting is implied by certain natural conjectures.
Bulk universality of scaling limits for the almost Hermitian Coulomb gas

Inspired by the recent approach to edge universality of Cronvall and Wennman, we prove several local universality results for scaling limits in the bulk in the almost Hermitian regime, as well as associated results relating to reproducing kernel spaces of the Fock type.
Isotropy of symplectic involutions and motivic equivalence for groups of type $\sf{C}$
Demba Barry; Charles De Clercq; Anne Quéguiner-Mathieu

We extend to arbitrary characteristic a theorem due to Karpenko and Tignol on the isotropy of symplectic involutions after generic index reduction; as a consequence, we also prove the existence of critical varieties for semi-simple algebraic groups of type $\sf C$ over arbitrary base fields. The latter result relies on a characteristic-free argument, which involves the computation of the mod $2$ Tate trace of the variety of isotropic ideals of reduced dimension $2$ for a symplectic involution.
Improved algorithms for computing the matrix logarithm based on the double-exponential formula

Tatsuoka et al. proposed an efficient algorithm for computing the matrix logarithm using the double-exponential (DE) formula. Its discretization error decreases exponentially as the number of quadrature nodes grows, and its nested grids allow previously computed values to be reused when the mesh is refined. They also reported that their approach is more robust than Gauss--Legendre quadrature for ill-conditioned matrices. We propose two algorithms based on the DE formula. The first adaptively refines the mesh while reusing previously computed values and requires no matrix norm computations. The second uses a rigorous error bound to select the number of quadrature nodes a priori. Numerical experiments show that both methods attain lower errors than Tatsuoka et al.'s method at comparable elapsed times over the tested ranges.
Studying proof data with proof theory: the case of AI-generated mathematics

I present a method for analyzing large collections of formally verified mathematical proofs (e.g. OpenAI's) grounded in some historical and philosophical musings on mathematics in the age of AI. Many of the quantities involved, such as the size of a proof term or the number of redundant steps, are already computed by work on improving automated provers, where they serve as targets. My aim is to turn them into measurements of proofs themselves: compared against a reference library and against each proof's own cut-free form, checked against theorems they must obey, and controlled for how the proofs were compiled. With these instruments, I measure how (much) machine-generated mathematics diverges from human mathematics, and find that AI-written formal proofs realize far less of the logical compression available to them than human mathematicians do (31% against 73% in mathlib, and 55% against 86% on proofs that call no automation). These figures are broadly in line with reports from those who build provers and proof-improvement tools that AI-written proofs are often longer than they need to be.
A coupling normal form for reversible center-center Hamiltonians with application to the restricted three-body problem

Near a reversible center-center equilibrium, the Birkhoff normal form does not describe the families bifurcating from the continued tori, which resonant normal forms capture through a reduced system.With a reflection symmetry, we develop a coupling normal form in which the bifurcating families also appear as tori of action normal forms. Along a selected coupling direction, the first harmonic in the angle difference is absorbed into an action-dependent counterterm. We prove that the coupled recursion determines unique counterterm coefficients, a formal action normal form, and an exact counterterm factorization. The factorization gives a recovery constraint, whose trivial factor corresponds to the Birkhoff normal form. At every finite order, a symmetric pair of bifurcating branches leaves the trivial branch at a critical curve, carrying approximately invariant tori and circles with residual estimates. In the spatial circular restricted three-body problem, these give approximate halo orbits and quasi-halo tori.
Entropy hypocoercivity and query complexity for the bouncy particle sampler

We study convergence in relative entropy of the bouncy particle sampler with Gaussian velocity refreshment, for a target $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb R^d$ with $U$ $m$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth, and condition number $κ=L/m$. For initial laws with bounded density relative to equilibrium, we show that the relative entropy decays exponentially up to an arbitrary additive error $δ$, with a rate that depends only logarithmically on the density bound and on $δ$. From a Gaussian cold start and with a suitably chosen refreshment rate, the relative entropy falls below $δ$ after time $\widetilde O(\sqrt{d/m})$. Combined with exact simulation by windowed thinning, this gives an expected gradient-query complexity of $\widetilde O(d\sqrtκ)$, improving the $\widetilde O(d^2\sqrtκ)$ bound based on $L^2$ hypocoercivity.
Large deviations for the largest eigenvalue of a polynomial in Gaussian matrices
Alice Guionnet; Jonathan Husson; Jana Reker
In this article, we prove that the spectrum, the norm, and the largest eigenvalue of a self-adjoint polynomial $P$ in $k$ independent matrices from the GOE satisfy a large deviation principle.
Giuseppe Cannizzaro; Harry Giles; Fabio Toninelli

We construct an infinite-dimensional diffusion on the space of interlaced particle configurations on Z x R, a process we call the dynamical bead model. The process (self-)interacts through instantaneous reflection and preserves the bead measures of [C. Boutillier, Ann. Probab., 2009]. Through the height function correspondence, our process is equivalent to a reversible interface in (2+1) dimensions. We provide compelling evidence that at large space-time scales the interface exhibits diffusive behaviour, as we compute exactly its diffusivity matrix and show it is non-degenerate and independent of time.
A noncommutative weak $L_1$-estimate for rough singular integrals
Guixiang Hong; Liang Wang; Xumin Wang; Bang Xu

In this paper, we establish a noncommutative version of Andreas Seeger's weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for singular integral operators with kernels satisfying angular $L\log L$ integrability and an averaged radial Dini condition. The strategy for obtaining the sharp integrability condition involves not only some new estimates of the off-diagonal good and bad functions in Parcet's noncommutative Calderón-Zygmund decomposition but also certain essential modifications of Seeger's kernel decomposition and estimates.
The Calderón Problem for Quasilinear Currents

We study the Calderón problem for smooth quasilinear current laws on a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq3$. Under the stated structural assumptions and analyticity conditions, the interior current law is determined by local Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps, up to a partial-boundary-fixing diffeomorphism and a Hall-effect-type invisible current. The two obstructions come from the linearized inverse problem, which is solved by combining boundary determination for magnetic Schrödinger operators with analytic continuation in solution coordinates. Higher-order linearization and a boundary argument involving products of three solution gradients then determine the remaining Taylor coefficients.
Can Quantum Entanglement Increase the Capacity of a Classical Relay Channel?

We show positive and negative results on classical relay channels with entanglement assistance, revealing a sharp contrast between strictly causal and causal relay encoding. First, we consider van der Meulen's setting of a unit-delay relay, with strictly causal encoding. We show that the standard cutset upper bound continues to hold with entanglement assistance, and deduce that entanglement does not increase the capacity for several classes of relay channels. Second, we consider a zero-delay relay, where the encoding is causal. We present an example in which entanglement enables rates that exceed the cutset upper bound by at least 12.5%. Namely, entanglement shared between the source and relay significantly increases the capacity of a classical zero-delay relay channel.

We provide a complete classification of the rational $2$-adic Tate modules $V_2(E)$ of elliptic curves $E/\mathbb{Q}_2$ with potentially good reduction. The classification is given in terms of the filtered $(φ,\mathrm{Gal})$-modules associated to $V_2(E)$ via Fontaine's functor $D_{pcris}^{*}$.
A gentle introduction to approximating high-dimensional integrals with lattice rules and a maybe-not-so-gentle introduction to the relevant function spaces for QMC integration

These lecture notes give both a practical and theoretical introduction to high-dimensional integration with lattice rules. We introduce lattice points and rules in combination with accompanying Julia code. Next we introduce the typical function spaces used in the literature. We compare classical Sobolev spaces with Sobolev spaces of dominating mixed smoothness. We derive lower bounds and show that the curse of dimensionality is unavoidable for these unweighted function spaces. Next we switch to weighted periodic spaces and derive a constructive upper bound using the component-by-component construction for the generating vector of a lattice rule. We pick periodic spaces because they are a perfect match with lattice rules. The upper bound shows that under suitable conditions on the weights we obtain dimension-independent worst-case error bounds. We then use embedding constants to transfer these bounds to some common norms for these periodic spaces.
Observability of wave equations with time- and space-dependent potentials: a counterexample under GCC and a positive criterion on the disk
Zhonghua Liao; Qi Lü; Xu Zhang

We show that the geometric control condition (GCC) for the free wave equation does not guarantee internal observability in the presence of a smooth time-dependent potential. On a bounded connected domain with analytic boundary, we construct a nonempty open observation set such that the pair satisfies GCC and the free Dirichlet wave is observable, and a smooth $2π$-periodic potential for which there exists a nonzero smooth Dirichlet wave that vanishes on the observed cylinder for all time. The wave is the unique mild solution in the space $X_Ω=L^2(Ω)\times H^{-1}(Ω)$ on every finite interval, so no finite observation horizon yields an observability inequality for this fixed potential. The construction starts from a real-valued local counterexample to unique continuation across a noncharacteristic hyperplane; this local statement is of independent interest, since earlier constructions for the wave operator use complex-valued waves and potentials. The global counterexample is obtained by joining flat oscillatory solutions along the edges of a polygonal observation set, repairing their sum at the vertices without changing its zero set, and then using a spatial transition to a common time-independent pair near the boundary. For comparison, on the unit disk we show that an observation region containing a central disk and a neighborhood of an embedded cross-cut yields observability for every weak wave at sufficiently large observation time, with constants uniform over bounded measurable potentials; the proof uses a cut, logarithmic polar coordinates, and a Carleman weight whose favorable flux is confined to the observed artificial boundary.

The Bellaterra automaton gives three involutions of every set of binary words of a fixed length. We identify their Schreier graph at level $n$ with a cubic arithmetic graph over $\Q(\sqrt{17})$, and prove that every nonconstant adjacency eigenvalue satisfies the Ramanujan bound. In particular, this proves Malyshev-Pak's Conjecture that the Bellaterra graphs form a family of two-sided expanders.
Critical limits of generating functions for face-constrained labelled planar maps

We study connected planar maps with a fixed number of numbered faces, whose vertices carry integer labels such that the minimum label along the boundary of each face is one. Each face has its own positive weight, and an edge shared by two faces receives the geometric mean of their weights. For any fixed number $k\ge3$ of faces, we prove that the suitably rescaled generating function converges locally uniformly as the face weights approach the critical value $1/12$, possibly at different positive rates. The limit is a finite, continuous sum of integrals over cubic schemes. Each scheme edge carries a Green kernel for a singular differential operator on the positive half-line, and each face contributes one insertion of the derivative of the tree scaling profile. The main difficulty is obtaining uniform estimates for small vertex labels, where the minimum-label constraints of different faces can interact. A positive corner-marking expansion reduces this problem to establishing uniform bounds on the contributions of marked configurations, both for small and large vertex labels. These estimates prove integrability of the surviving diagrams and show that coincident marks and noncubic schemes contribute only lower-order terms.
Projective Decomposition and Intersection Cohomology of Rigid Spaces

We prove a rigid analytic analogue of the Beilinson--Bernstein--Deligne decomposition theorem for projective morphisms over $p$-adic fields, with $\mathbf{Q}_\ell$-coefficients for every prime $\ell$, including $\ell=p$. As an application, we show that the $p$-adic intersection cohomology of every proper rigid analytic space is de Rham. We also establish an independent criterion for de Rham intersection cohomology with local coefficients in terms of the dimension of the boundary, yielding further results for curves, surfaces, and finite covers. For finite coefficients of characteristic different from $p$, we obtain isotropic analytic upper bounds for singular support and prove that singular support is analytic and Lagrangian for complexes supported in dimension at most one.
Irreducibility of the Cuboid Polynomial $Q_{p,q}(t)$ via the Rank-One Chabauty-Coleman Method

Let $Q_{p,q}(t)\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be Sharipov's even monic degree-$10$ second cuboid polynomial, with coprime positive integers $p\ne q$. We prove that $Q_{p,q}(t)$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$, and hence over $\mathbb{Z}$. More generally, the normalized associated quintic $P_s(x)$ and its composition $P_s(t^2)$ are irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ for every $s\in\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{0,\pm1\}$. The proof reduces linear and quadratic factors to rational points and horizontal conjugate pairs on one fixed genus-$2$ curve. A certified rank upper bound for its Jacobian, together with an exact divisor calculation, gives a rank-one annihilating differential at the prime $3$. For the quadratic-factor case, the symmetric coordinates of a horizontal pair lie on an explicit double cover of an elliptic quartic. All rational affine points on this model are $3$-adically integral and reduce to six smooth residue classes. The pulled-back differential is a unit in each class, proving that six displayed points form the complete list. Their coordinates exclude every admissible parameter. A negative real root of the irreducible quintic then supplies the additional degree argument required for irreducibility of the degree-$10$ polynomial. The rank computation and all exact arithmetic certificates are specified explicitly for reproduction.
Local rigidity of conformally Euclidean metrics for the anisotropic Helmholtz equation at fixed energy

We prove local rigidity of smooth conformally Euclidean metrics $g_0$ on smooth compact domains $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge3$, for the anisotropic Helmholtz equation $(-Δ_g -k^2)u =0$ at a fixed energy $k^2>0$ which is not a Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-Δ_{g_0}$ in $M$. Any smooth metric sufficiently close to $g_0$ in $H^s(M)$, with integer $s>n/2+1$, and having the same Dirichlet-to-Neumann map, is its pullback by a smooth diffeomorphism fixing the boundary pointwise. The proof uses a Helmholtz embedding to fix the gauge and a compactness argument together with a characterization of the kernel of the linearization.
Sharp concentration levels and extremal functions for a planar Choquard-type Trudinger--Moser inequality

Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth bounded domain and let $0<α<2$. We study the exponential Choquard functional \[ \mathcal{F}_β(u)=\int_Ω\int_Ω \frac{e^{βu^2(x)}e^{βu^2(y)}}{|x-y|^α}d xd y \] on the unit Dirichlet ball of $H_0^1(Ω)$. We establish the sharp boundedness threshold $β_*=(4-α)π$ and prove attainment of the critical supremum. More precisely, we determine the exact concentration level at every point of $\overlineΩ$ in terms of the regular part of the Dirichlet Green function. The concentration upper bound follows from the classical planar Trudinger--Moser concentration formula and the sharp Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality, after separating the background contribution. A test function obtained by matching a logarithmic profile to the Green function attains this bound asymptotically. Its exact Dirichlet normalization produces a strictly positive lower-order correction, which rules out concentration of maximizing sequences. We also prove the Euler--Lagrange equation, positivity, and regularity of extremals.
Derived equivalence classification of twisted and generalized multifold extensions of affine type

Let $B$ be a piecewise hereditary algebra of affine type over an algebraically closed field. In this paper we give a derived and stable equivalence classification of twisted multifold extensions of $B$. The types $\widetilde D$ and $\widetilde E$ are already covered by the classification for tree type. We therefore consider the remaining types $\widetilde{A}_{p,q}$. We show that the $n$th power of the Nakayama functor on the full subcategory of a transjective component determines the twist, including its action on morphisms, up to conjugacy in the derived Picard group of a hereditary algebra. Together with the hereditary derived type and the folding number, this gives a complete invariant for derived equivalence, and also for stable triangle equivalence. We then compute these conjugacy classes in the unbalanced, balanced, bypass, and Kronecker cases, keeping the finite rotation data. Finally, by the normalization theorem of Asashiba--Kimura--Nakashima--Yoshiwaki, we obtain the same classification for generalized multifold extensions with nonzero integer jump.
Model Theory and Algorithms for One-Relator Groups

We study the elementary theories and algorithmic properties of one-relator groups. We give a first-order sentence characterizing Baumslag-Solitar-freeness in this class. For fixed $|m|>1$, we regularly interpret $\BS(1,m)$ as a definable subgroup in every one-relator group containing it. We uniformly, regularly and injectively interpret integer arithmetic in countable groups of cohomological dimension at most two. We obtain one uniform interpretation for all one-relator groups containing a non-unimodular Baumslag--Solitar subgroup. Every fixed finitely presented group is regularly interpretable in these groups, and their elementary theories are undecidable. We also describe the GBS overgroups of a non-unimodular Baumslag--Solitar subgroup. For the unimodular groups we construct finite-index direct products of free groups and $\Z$, and reduce the elementary theory of $\BS(k,k)$ to that of a free group with a named periodic automorphism. Using the recent Open AI result that BS-free one-relator groups are hyperbolic we obtain a terminating algorithm recognizing this class and obtain consequences. From the virtual compact specialness result of another Open AI paper, we obtain an effective construction of virtual free-by-cyclic presentations for hyperbolic one-relator groups, the free kernel may have infinite rank. For classes of torsion-free one-relator groups in which CSA implies toral relative hyperbolicity, we give a uniform algorithm deciding CSA and, in the affirmative case, the existence of a subgroup isomorphic to $\Z^2$.
Variance Reduction Note 2: The Convergence of SPIDER

The stochastic path-integrated differential estimator (SPIDER) tracks a gradient by accumulating small, shared-sample gradient differences and periodically refreshing the estimate. This second expository note on recursive variance reduction explains SPIDER-SFO and gives a self-contained proof of its expected first-order stationarity guarantee. The argument combines an epochwise mean-square error bound with descent under a clipped, normalized update. It yields $O(ε^{-3})$ stochastic gradient evaluations in the online setting and $O(n+\sqrt n\,ε^{-2})$ component gradient evaluations for a finite sum, with the remaining problem parameters fixed. All refresh costs are included. The presentation is pedagogical and makes no claim of a new algorithm or convergence rate.
Discrete geometry and de-Rham cohomology of graphs

We develop a theory of discrete spaces which are built by gluing coordinate patches together into an atlas, much as a manifold is built from charts. Graphs are the main examples, and an atlas on a graph gives it a geometric structure analogous to that of a manifold. This structure leads to a cohomology theory, which we show to be a discrete analogue of de Rham cohomology. We define a "discrete coordinatized space" as a cubical set equipped with the Alexandrov topology, on which differential forms become sheaves. When the atlas is regular, the de Rham cohomology agrees with the sheaf cohomology of the constant sheaf, just as in the smooth case. We compute it for several examples, including a torus graph and a graph resembling a sphere, and recover the cohomology of the corresponding surfaces.
Pseudoconvex Exhaustions of Hartogs Domains Associated with $L^2$-Optimal Pairs

By constructing a smooth pseudoconvex exhaustion of the associated Hartogs domain, we give a new proof of the Deng-Ning-Wang's characterization of plurisubharmonic functions without the smoothness assumption.
A Common neighborhood signed graph of a signed graph

Let G be a simple connected graph with the vertex set V (G) and the edge set E(G) such that |V (G)| = n and |E(G)| = q. The common neighborhood graph con(G) of G has the same set of vertices as that of G and uv is an edge in con(G) if u and v have at least one common neighbor in G. By a signed graph S, we mean a graph G whose edges has been assigned sign plus or minus. In this paper, the concept of common neighborhood graph has been initiated in the realm of signed graphs, that is, we define a common neighborhood signed graph of a signed graph.
A discrete-continuous-time stochastic framework for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder-related symptom modeling and pharmacological intervention via methylphenidate

This paper presents an original mathematical and computational framework for modeling the efficacy of methylphenidate as an optimal control policy acting on the nonlinear dynamics of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. Neural processes in ADHD are conceptualized as stochastic processes with trajectories that inherently converge towards stable, yet dysfunctional patterns associated with clinical symptoms. The pharmacological intervention is mathematically formalized as an external control signal that reassesses the system's drift and redirects these trajectories towards neurotypical regimes. To bridge these theoretical stochastic models with empirical clinical data, latent representations are inferred using a novel deterministic hybrid deep learning architecture, combining a one-dimensional convolutional neural network and a Vision Transformer, trained on preprocessed functional magnetic resonance imaging data.
De Finetti Structures in Networks of Quantum Systems

Consider $N$ identical quantum systems at the vertices of a graph, interacting via pairwise edge couplings. We designate $K$ vertices as a system of interest $\mathrm S$ and the remaining $N-K$ as a reservoir $\mathrm R$. Under generic connectivity assumptions between $\mathrm S$ and $\mathrm R$, we show that for $N\to\infty$, the reduced state of $\mathrm S$ converges to a convex combination of symmetric product states of $K$ single-vertex density matrices -- called a de Finetti representation. Unlike in standard derivations for symmetric (exchangeable) systems, we establish de Finetti representations for quantum networks, which are inherently non-exchangeable. We construct the representations explicitly and quantify the convergence rate. We show that Erdős--Rényi random graphs exhibit the de Finetti structure: as the reservoir grows, the reduced state of any fixed finite subgraph converges almost surely to an explicit deterministic product state. As applications, we establish a general area law for the entanglement entropy of $\mathrm S$, analyze mean-field and fluctuation scalings of the $\mathrm S$-$\mathrm R$ interaction, and illustrate our results on qubit networks. We also derive quantitative convergence estimates for information-theoretic quantities, including von Neumann entropy, mutual information, and entanglement within $\mathrm S$ and between $\mathrm S$ and $\mathrm R$.
New Bernstein functions and subordination representations for time-nonlocal evolution equations

This paper establishes subordination representations from multi-term time-fractional differential equations to single-term ones, a direction complementary to the previously known subordination from single-term to multi-term equations; combining the two complementary directions also yields subordination representations between two multi-term equations. The crucial step is to prove that certain implicitly defined functions are Bernstein functions. We show that the quotient $\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_jλ^{α_j}\big)/\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_jα_jλ^{α_j}\big)$ is a Stieltjes function whenever $0\leqα_1-α_m\leq 1$, and consequently that the inverse function of $λ=\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_jφ^{α_j}\big)^{1/β}$ is a Bernstein function for every $0<β\leqα_m$. As applications, we obtain subordination representations with a clear probabilistic meaning: from multi-term to single-term time-fractional diffusion-wave equations, between abstract nonlocal-in-time equations with kernels of type $(\mathcal{PC})$ (including equations of tempered stable type), and between nonlocal-in-time telegraph equations. A necessary and sufficient condition for $[(λ+b)^β-b^β]^γ$ to be a Bernstein function also yields a negative result: in general, no such subordination exists from an $α$-stable type dynamics to a tempered $β$-stable one when $α<1$.
Li Gao; Marius Junge; Zhendong Xu; Hao Zhang

We derive $L_p$-Poincaré inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups on finite von Neumann algebras, from a spectral gap (PI) or from a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality (MLSI). For $p\ge2$, the corresponding coefficients have optimal order $O(p)$ and $O(\sqrt p)$, respectively. Both estimates follow from Beckner inequalities by integration along semigroups. We also establish a non-tracial extension to quantum Markov semigroups satisfying GNS detailed balance. As a direct byproduct, we apply $L_p$-Poincaré inequalities to Schatten-valued functions on graphs in order to obtain the Schatten distortion of expanders.
Maximal $L^p$-$L^q$ regularity of finite element methods for stochastic parabolic equations in polygonal domains
Genming Bai; Jianbo Cui; Buyang Li

We prove that a spatial semidiscrete finite element method preserves the stochastic maximal regularity of the heat equation on bounded convex polygonal and polyhedral domains in dimensions two and three. A main difficulty is to establish suitable Green-function estimates for stochastic convolutions, whose paths generally lack classical time derivatives. Besides, the failure of the Burkholder-Davis-Gundy (BDG) inequality at the endpoint $p=\infty$ creates additional difficulties. Our approach leverages a hidden symmetry structure of the discrete Green's function, which enables the use of a key integration-by-parts type formula. Then the discrete stochastic maximal $L^p$-$L^p$ regularity with $p\in [2,\infty)$ is obtained from the discrete local energy estimates and interpolation inequalities.
